# BUG_LOG — журнал обнаруженных багов

**Назначение:** живой реестр багов, обнаруженных в процессе работы над проектом
(в проде, в dev-окружении, на ревью, в чатах с агентами). Каждая запись — это
готовый input для будущей fix-сессии: симптомы, проверенная гипотеза причины,
предлагаемое решение, известный workaround.

**Workflow:**

1. При обнаружении бага — добавить запись в § «Active bugs», статус `open`.
2. При начале fix-сессии — статус `in-progress`, сослаться на стартовый промпт
   (`docs/notes/START_PROMPT_SPRINT_*.md`) или PR.
3. После merge'а fix'а — статус `resolved`, перенести запись в § «Resolved
   bugs» с указанием commit'а / PR'а.
4. Если баг переоткрыт — вернуть в `Active`, добавить новую дату и контекст.

**Поля записи (обязательные):**

- `ID` — `BUG-NNN`, монотонно растёт.
- `Severity` — `Critical | High | Medium | Low`.
- `Status` — `open | in-progress | resolved | wontfix`.
- `Component` — какая подсистема (`mcp_server`, `bot`, `pipeline`, `api`, ...).
- `Discovered` — ISO-дата + кто/как обнаружил.
- `Symptoms` — что именно наблюдается у пользователя / в логах.
- `Root cause` — проверенная (не предполагаемая) причина с ссылками на код.
- `Why CI didn't catch` — где blind-spot в тестах (важно для fix-плана).
- `Proposed fix` — минимальный фикс + hardening, разделённые.
- `Workaround` — что делать прямо сейчас, пока баг не закрыт.
- `Artifacts` — токены, UUID, конфиги, логи, ссылки на чаты-репорты.
- `Linked` — ID связанных багов / TD / DI / PR.

**Severity definitions:**

- **Critical** — блокирует core-функционал в проде (auth, ingestion, RAG) или
  представляет security-issue. Чинится первым приоритетом.
- **High** — ломает важный feature, есть workaround, не утечка данных.
- **Medium** — ухудшает UX или затрудняет работу, но не блокирует.
- **Low** — косметика, edge case, низкочастотный сценарий.

### BUG-091 (Low/Medium — ops/perimeter, ✅ resolved 2026-08-11) — the live MCP vhost never got `proxy_buffering off`, so nginx buffered the Streamable-HTTP/SSE response contrary to the invariant and to the deploy recipe both documents state

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Low/Medium** — a latent degradation, not an outage. MCP has served traffic for four months in this state and plain request/response tool calls are unaffected in outcome: nginx flushes what it buffered when the upstream finishes, so the answer arrives, just not incrementally. What it does cost is the *streaming* property MCP Streamable HTTP is named for — SSE events sit in `proxy_buffers` (default 8×4k) until a buffer fills or the response ends, so notifications arrive in bursts. Bounded below Medium-High because nothing is lost and no data leaks; lifted above Low because two product documents state the requirement and the live perimeter silently does not meet it, which is the same false-assurance shape as BUG-089. |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (2026-08-11) — remedy **(a)** chosen and applied by the owner the same day: `proxy_buffering off;` added to the `location /` block of `/etc/nginx/sites-available/tgp-mcp` (line 13), `nginx -t` clean, `systemctl reload nginx` at `17:18:54 CEST` exited `0` (reload, not restart — no container touched, so BUG-078/BUG-090 do not apply); pre-edit backup kept as `tgp-mcp.bak.2026-08-11`. **Verified live post-fix:** full probe run 15:19 UTC — **16/16 checks pass**, including «буферизация ответа выключена»; MCP still answers (`https://mcp.tgp.efimov.mobi/mcp` → 401 auth-gate, API `/health` → 200). Rationale for (a) over amending the invariant, recorded at decision time: streaming is the defining property of MCP Streamable HTTP; buffering buys nothing on a loopback upstream with a single operator; and the vhost author demonstrably hand-copied three of the recipe's four streaming directives — option (b) would have promoted that omission to a specification. **The probe is now in cron** (`50 4 * * *`, after the 03:50 backup-watchdog; crontab backed up to `~/crontab.bak.2026-08-11` first), verified under `env -i` cron environment (16/16), alarms to `~/backup-alert.log` which remains `0` bytes. Was `open` (filed 2026-08-11, same day). |
| **Component** | The perimeter, not the application: `/etc/nginx/sites-available/tgp-mcp` on the reference host (outside this repository by [ADR-0021](../adr/0021-backup-and-recovery-requirements.md) § 5). Specification side: [`SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md`](../SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md) § Reverse proxy invariant 3; recipe side: [`PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md`](../../PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md) § Option B. |
| **Discovered** | 2026-08-11, by the first live run of [`ops/verify-perimeter-invariants.sh`](../../ops/verify-perimeter-invariants.sh) — the probe written to replace "review the perimeter before applying" with continuous verification (technical-debt-roadmap § 7). Found on the run that was expected to be silent, which is the outcome the probe exists to produce. Not reported by a user: this class has no symptom an operator would notice, only latency that looks like the model thinking. |
| **Symptoms** | None visible. `https://mcp.tgp.efimov.mobi/mcp` answers, tools execute, the 24h watches have been clean. The divergence is only observable by reading the config: the MCP `location /` block carries `proxy_http_version 1.1`, `Upgrade`/`Connection` pass-through and `proxy_read_timeout 300s`, but **no `proxy_buffering off;`**, so nginx's default `proxy_buffering on` is in effect. |
| **Root cause** | The vhost was hand-written on the host on 2026-04-02 (mtime `2026-04-02 20:29`, identical for all three `tgp-*` files — one sitting), and it picked up three of the four streaming directives from the recipe but not the fourth. Nothing checked it afterwards, because the perimeter config lives outside the repository and no test or CI job could see it. The recipe in `PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md` § Option B does contain `proxy_buffering off;`, so this is drift from a written procedure, not a gap in it. Note the application does not compensate: `X-Accel-Buffering` appears nowhere in the codebase (verified by grep — the only hit in the repository is the recipe itself), so there is no per-response header telling nginx to stop buffering. |
| **Why nothing caught it** | Precisely the gap this probe was built to close, and worth stating plainly because it is the general lesson rather than a detail of this bug: the invariants were written down in `SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md` as prose, and prose does not fail. Between 2026-04-02 and 2026-08-11 the config was read by a human at least twice (BUG-090 closure, the backup-script work) without the missing line being noticed — reading a config for one purpose does not verify it against a specification. The weekly `ops/backup-nginx-config.sh` would have reported a *change*, but the file has not changed since before that script existed, so a defect present at birth is invisible to a diff-against-last-week detector by construction. |
| **Two ways to close (owner decision, neither taken here)** | **(a) Fix the perimeter.** Add `proxy_buffering off;` to the `location /` block of `tgp-mcp`, `nginx -t`, `systemctl reload nginx`. Reload, not restart; no container is touched, so neither BUG-078 nor BUG-090 applies. Rollback is removing the line and reloading again. Then the probe goes green and the recipe, the invariant and reality agree. **(b) Amend the invariant.** If buffering is judged acceptable for this workload, `SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md` invariant 3 and the `PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md` recipe both drop the requirement, and the probe check goes with them. What must **not** happen is the third option — softening the probe while leaving both documents asserting the requirement, which is the BUG-089 anti-pattern of a test faithful to the code instead of the requirement. |
| **Adjacent observation, deliberately NOT made a probe check** | The same block sets `proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"` unconditionally, while the recipe uses `Connection ""`. Hardcoding `upgrade` sends `Connection: upgrade` upstream even on turns where the client requested no upgrade (`$http_upgrade` empty), which is what the conventional `map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade` idiom exists to avoid. It is left out of the probe on purpose: invariant 3 requires `Upgrade`/`Connection` **pass-through**, which this satisfies, and encoding a stricter rule in the checker than the specification states would make the checker the source of truth — the inversion this whole exercise is meant to prevent. If the map form is wanted, the invariant changes first and the check follows. |
| **Relation to BUG-008** | Untested hypothesis, recorded so it is not lost rather than claimed. BUG-008 (MCP remote endpoint hang, `open`, root cause unknown; § Active bugs below) was last characterised as most likely a client/transport stall, with transport hypothesis H3 tracked separately and unresolved. A proxy that buffers a streamed response is a transport-layer actor on that exact path. This is **not** evidence: the hang was a single flaky occurrence in 2026-04, the server-side handler was proven fast, and buffering delays delivery rather than withholding it for hours. Worth one line in the H3 notes, nothing more. |
| **Artifacts** | Live probe run 2026-08-11 16:38 UTC on the reference host: 16 checks, 15 pass, this one fail. Passing alongside it: all three upstreams on loopback (`127.0.0.1:8000` / `:8080` / `:3001`), each served by its own vhost, `/metrics` → `403` both statically and live, MCP `proxy_read_timeout 300s`, certificates valid 79 more days, host copy of `backup-nginx-config.sh` byte-identical to the repository one. The run wrote to a temp file, not to `~/backup-alert.log`, so the operator's alarm channel is still `0` bytes. |
| **Linked** | `technical-debt-roadmap.md` § 7 (perimeter outside the repo; the reformulation from review to verification that produced this probe); [ADR-0021](../adr/0021-backup-and-recovery-requirements.md) § 5; BUG-089 (same false-coverage class, and the source of the "fail in both directions" rule); BUG-090 (the work that first opened the perimeter question). |

### BUG-090 (Medium — ops/deploy) — a single-file bind mount pins the container to the OLD inode, so `git pull` + hot-reload silently deploys nothing for `alerts.yml` (and `docker compose up -d` does not fix it)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Medium** (ops/deploy correctness, no data loss). The failure mode is a **false green**: every step of the documented deploy reports success while the container keeps running the previous config. For an observability config that means alerts you believe you shipped simply do not exist. |
| **Status** | **`resolved`** (2026-08-06) — structurally fixed: the whole `docker/prometheus` **directory** is now bind-mounted, so a file replaced by `git pull` is visible in the container and `/-/reload` genuinely reloads it. Two earlier statuses in this same session were wrong and are left here on purpose: `resolved` (overstated — only the incident was closed), then `mitigated` (accurate at the time — procedure documented, trap intact). |
| **NOT a new discovery (important)** | This trap was **already documented** in [`PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md`](../../PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md) § deploy step 4b since **2026-06-18**, commit `529676d` «docs(deploy): force-recreate prometheus after alerts.yml change (stale inode)» — describing the stale inode and prescribing `--force-recreate`. I did not consult it, and the F5-C runbook plus PR [#370](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/370) asserted the **opposite** («BUG-078 does not apply here, hot-reload is enough»). So the real defect was never missing knowledge: it was **two deploy docs disagreeing**, with the feature-specific runbook — the one an operator actually follows for F5-C — contradicting the canonical one. Recording it as a fresh discovery would have been its own false green. |
| **Component** | `docker-compose.yml` Prometheus service — `./docker/prometheus/alerts.yml:/etc/prometheus/alerts.yml:ro` is a bind mount of a **single file**, not a directory. Same shape applies to `./docker/prometheus.yml`. |
| **Discovered** | 2026-08-06, deploying the F5-C T7 gate hygiene PR (#370) to prod. |
| **Symptoms** | After `git pull --ff-only` on prod (`HEAD=5ff7475`, host file containing the 3 new `resummarize_refusal_cooldown` references), `docker exec tg_parser_prometheus promtool check rules /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml` still reported **30 rules** — the pre-merge count — and `docker exec tg_parser_prometheus grep -c resummarize_refusal_cooldown /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml` returned **0** while the host file returned **3**. A hot-reload at that point would have been a no-op reported as success. |
| **Root cause (verified live)** | A Docker bind mount of a single file resolves to that file's **inode** at container-create time. Git does not edit files in place — `pull` / `checkout` write a temp file and `rename()` it over the target, producing a **new inode**. The container's mount still points at the now-unlinked old inode, so the process cannot see the new content by any means: not by re-reading, not by `/-/reload`. Directory bind mounts do not have this problem, which is why the same deploy shape works elsewhere in the project. |
| **Why the documented procedure did not catch it** | The runbook (and PR #370 as originally written) said: `git pull` → `promtool check rules /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml` → `/-/reload`, and explicitly argued BUG-078 does **not** apply here because rule files are bind-mounted rather than compose-interpolated. That reasoning is right about env interpolation and wrong about the outcome: **both** classes end with "the container keeps the old thing". Worse, the `promtool check` step ran **inside the container** on the mounted path, so it validated the STALE file and printed SUCCESS — the verification step itself was blind to the failure. |
| **Second trap** | `docker compose up -d prometheus` does **not** fix it either: compose compares the desired config hash, sees no change (the mount path is textually identical), and reports `Container tg_parser_prometheus Running` without re-creating. Verified live — the container file still showed `0` matches afterwards. |
| **Fix (verified live)** | `docker compose up -d --force-recreate prometheus`. After re-create: container file shows **3** matches, `promtool check rules /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml` reports **31 rules**, `StartedAt=2026-08-06T08:07:08Z`, and the recording rule / alert appear in `/api/v1/rules`. Prometheus TSDB lives in a named volume, so re-create preserves history. |
| **Non-vacuous verification rule (adopted)** | Never accept an in-container `promtool check` alone as proof of deploy — it happily validates a stale mount. Prove the **content** reached the container and that the numbers moved: `docker exec … grep -c <new-symbol> /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml` (host vs container), rule count before/after, and a pre/post pair on an affected query. Here: `ratio14d` **0.9887 → 0.8824** across the deploy. |
| **Structural fix (applied 2026-08-06)** | Bind-mount the **directory**, not the files — a new inode inside a mounted directory is visible immediately, which is exactly why the Grafana dashboards (`./docker/grafana/dashboards -> /var/lib/grafana/dashboards`) re-provisioned themselves on this same deploy with no intervention. Applied: `docker/prometheus.yml` moved to `docker/prometheus/prometheus.yml`, both files now served by one mount `./docker/prometheus:/etc/prometheus/conf:ro`, `--config.file=/etc/prometheus/conf/prometheus.yml`, `rule_files: /etc/prometheus/conf/alerts.yml`. **`rule_files` deliberately keeps an explicit filename rather than a `*.yml` glob** — the same directory holds `alerts_test.yml` (promtool unit tests), which is not a rule file and would fail to load. One prod re-create was needed to swap the mount itself; after that, config edits need only a reload. |
| **Residual — same class elsewhere (NOT fixed, audited 2026-08-06)** | An audit of every host bind mount in `docker-compose.yml` shows Prometheus was not the only single-file mount. Still file-mounted, therefore still inode-pinned: `./docker/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro` (**highest residual risk** — it is a config that changes via `git pull` exactly like `alerts.yml` did), `./docker/init-db.sh:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init-db.sh:ro` (low — runs only on first DB init), and `./.env:/app/.env:ro` on `tg_parser` / `mcp` / `tg_bot` (mixed — editing in place or `cp` over it keeps the inode and is visible, but any editor or tooling that writes-then-renames silently is not; this interacts with BUG-078, where the OS-env copy wins anyway). Directory-mounted and therefore immune: `./prompts`, both Grafana mounts, and now `./docker/prometheus`. Not bundled into this fix — Caddy and `.env` have different blast radii and rollbacks, and the `.env` case deserves to be reasoned about together with BUG-078 rather than patched blindly. |
| **Update 2026-08-07 — the `Caddyfile` residual is closed as NOT APPLICABLE, not as fixed** | The row above ranks `./docker/Caddyfile` as the **highest residual risk**. That ranking was made from the compose file without checking whether the service runs, and it is **wrong**: Caddy is not used on this host at all, so there was never a live trap to fix. Evidence (read-only, 2026-08-07): ports 80/443 are held by a **system nginx** (systemd unit, not Docker), `/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/` contains `tgp-api` / `tgp-mcp` / `tgp-grafana` — exactly the three sites `docker/Caddyfile` describes — serving a real Let's Encrypt certificate (issued 2026-08-01, valid to 2026-10-30, i.e. actively renewed); `https://tgp.efimov.mobi/health` → 200, `https://mcp.tgp.efimov.mobi/mcp` → 401, grafana → 302. There is **no caddy container even among stopped ones**, the caddy image is not pulled on the host, and the `tg_parser_caddy_data` volume is empty (8K, zero certificates) — Caddy has never served traffic here. Fixing the mount would have polished dead configuration. The planned slice is therefore **dropped, not deferred**. Remaining actionable residuals stay `./docker/init-db.sh` (low) and `./.env` ×3 (needs BUG-078 reasoning); the latter two keep the cost asymmetry noted below. |
| **Follow-up surfaced by that check** | Two divergences found while confirming the above, recorded so they are not lost. **(1) — CLOSED 2026-08-07** (see the row below). [`PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md`](../../PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md) § Reverse proxy documented `docker compose --profile production up -d` as the way to bring up the reverse proxy — on this host that command would **fail**, because Caddy wants `0.0.0.0:80/443` which system nginx already holds. Same defect class as BUG-090 itself: two sources of truth disagree and the operator follows the one that lies. (2) The nginx vhosts, TLS termination and access rules live **outside the repository** — not version-controlled, not reviewed, not backed up with the code; losing the host loses the proxy configuration. That is a materially larger gap than the inode trap this bug was about. Not acted on: needs an owner decision (document reality / vendor the nginx configs into the repo / drop the caddy service entirely). Checked and NOT a problem: nginx reproduces the Caddyfile's protection — `/metrics` on the public API domain returns 403. |
| **Update 2026-08-07 — divergence (1) closed** | Deploy docs now describe the deployed shape. The fix was **not** to write the live layout into another document: it turned out [`ROADMAP_V3_PRODUCTION_FIRST.md`](ROADMAP_V3_PRODUCTION_FIRST.md) § D5 had described this host's nginx layout accurately all along (3 vhosts, `/metrics` 403, Grafana on the published loopback port, certbot renewal), and [`PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md`](../../PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md) already pointed at [`SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md`](../SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md) "for a real Nginx layout" — the pointer just led to a generic diagram. Knowledge was never missing; the pointer had rotted. So: `SERVER_ARCHITECTURE.md` § Reverse proxy becomes the single source of truth and states **invariants plus read-live commands** rather than a config snapshot (a snapshot is what rots); ROADMAP_V3 § D5 is marked as a dated observation pointing there; `PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT.md` gains the mutual-exclusivity warning, loses the "recommended" label on the Caddy path (never executed anywhere — image not pulled, cert volume empty), and warns that the documented `--profile production up -d --build` also **rebuilds images and re-creates `tg_parser`/`mcp`/`grafana`**, not just Caddy. Two runbooks that asserted a `tg_parser_caddy` container exists were corrected — those mislead hardest, being followed under pressure. |
| **Cost asymmetry (why these were split)** | `init-db.sh` is not a free follow-on: Postgres is running, so changing its mount spec means the next `docker compose up -d` recreates the database container. Caddy had no such cost precisely because it does not exist. |
| **Relation to BUG-078** | Sibling, not duplicate. BUG-078 = OS-env baked by compose interpolation at container **create**, so `restart` is insufficient. BUG-090 = file **inode** bound at container create, so `git pull` + reload is insufficient and even `up -d` is insufficient. Shared lesson: on this deployment anything that "should be picked up automatically" needs a behavioural proof, not a structural argument. |
| **Verified in prod (2026-08-06)** | Deployed at `ba7d66d` with one `--force-recreate` (`StartedAt=2026-08-06T08:37:18Z`); mount is now `bind /home/user/TG_parser/docker/prometheus -> /etc/prometheus/conf`, `promtool check config` valid, `SUCCESS: 31 rules found`, all three scrape targets `up=1`, F5-C signals intact. **Direct proof the trap is closed** (not an argument — a measurement): replaced `alerts.yml` on the host by `rename()`, exactly what `git pull` does — inode went `396231 -> 656587` — and the container saw the new content **immediately without a re-create** (`grep -c BUG090-PROBE-MARKER` = 1), `/-/reload` succeeded on the new inode, and the same held for the restore. Probe file reverted; `git status` on prod clean. |
| **Artifacts** | Host `ls -i` = `396197`, host `grep -c` = 3, container `grep -c` = 0 (2026-08-06T08:06Z). `docker compose up -d prometheus` → `Container tg_parser_prometheus Running`, container `grep -c` still 0. `docker compose up -d --force-recreate prometheus` → `Recreated` / `Started`, container `grep -c` = 3, `SUCCESS: 31 rules found`. Post-deploy: gate alert gone from `ALERTS`, `ResummarizeRefusalCooldownPoisonPill` present as `pending`. |
| **Linked** | BUG-078 (re-create ≠ restart); BUG-088 / BUG-089 («merged ≠ deployed» precedent); PR [#370](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/370); runbook [`F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md) § T7. |

### BUG-089 (Medium — ops/observability) — HTTP metrics are double-namespaced (`tg_parser_http_http_*`), so the `HighHTTPErrorRate` alert can never fire and three dashboard panels are permanently empty; the intended latency buckets were silently dropped on top of that

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Medium** — no user-facing breakage and no data loss: the application serves traffic correctly and the series are collected, they simply carry names nobody queries. What lifts it above Low is that the damage is *false coverage assurance* on the HTTP surface — the one alert that watches 5xx rate cannot fire on a real incident, and the p50/p95/p99 latency panels an operator would open during that incident show «No data». Bounded below Severe because the API's own uptime is watched by `APIServiceDown` (a `up{job=...}` rule that does not depend on these names) and because RAG traffic in production goes through MCP/bot rather than HTTP, so the blind spot is on the least-used surface today. |
| **Status** | `resolved` (2026-08-04) — merged as `7e37907` ([PR #365](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/365)) and **verified live on prod**: image rebuilt 10:39 UTC, `tg_parser` container up 10:56 UTC, `/metrics` exposes single-prefixed `tg_parser_http_*` with **zero** `tg_parser_http_http` occurrences, the deliberate latency buckets `0.01 … 30.0, 60.0` are applied, `count(tg_parser_http_requests_total)` = 1 in Prometheus (the series exists where the alert reads it), and rule `HighHTTPErrorRate` is now `health=ok state=inactive` — it evaluated over an empty vector before and could never fire. Orphaned `tg_parser_http_http_*` series stop updating and age out by the 30d retention. Was `in-progress` (fix applied on branch `fix/bug089-http-metric-names`, 2026-08-04); prod was **not** fixed by the merge alone — this is application code, so it needed the image rebuild above, unlike the recent Prometheus/Grafana pin bumps. |
| **Component** | `api` / observability. One function: [`tg_parser/api/metrics.py::create_instrumentator`](../../tg_parser/api/metrics.py) (lines 651–718 post-fix). Consumers: [`docker/prometheus/alerts.yml`](../../docker/prometheus/alerts.yml) (rule `HighHTTPErrorRate`), [`docker/grafana/dashboards/system.json`](../../docker/grafana/dashboards/system.json) (3 panels), [`docker/grafana/provisioning/alerting/wave1_step4.yaml`](../../docker/grafana/provisioning/alerting/wave1_step4.yaml) (`tg_api_5xx_spike`, deleted 2026-06-15 — see BUG-038 § CORRECTION). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-08-04, comparing the metric names prod actually exposes on `/metrics` against the names the alert rules and dashboards query. Not reported by a user — this class of defect has no symptom other than silence. |
| **Symptoms** | Prod exposes `tg_parser_http_http_requests_total`, `tg_parser_http_http_request_size_bytes`, `tg_parser_http_http_response_size_bytes`, `tg_parser_http_http_request_duration_seconds`, `tg_parser_http_http_request_duration_highr_seconds` — a doubled `http_http` infix. Only `tg_parser_http_requests_inprogress` is correct, because its name is written by hand via `inprogress_name`. Consequence: `HighHTTPErrorRate` evaluates over an empty vector and can never fire; the `system.json` panels for request rate and for the p50/p95/p99 latency percentiles render nothing. Second, independent symptom: the HTTP latency histogram runs on the library default buckets `[0.1, 0.5, 1.0, +Inf]` — verified empirically at `/metrics` — not the ten buckets the code appears to configure. |
| **Root cause** | Two defects, one line apart. **(1) Double namespace.** `metrics.default(metric_namespace="tg_parser", metric_subsystem="http")` — but `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator` 8.0.0's base names ALREADY start with `http_` (`http_requests_total`, `http_request_duration_seconds`, …; see the `default()` docstring in the installed package). `prometheus_client` joins namespace + subsystem + name, so the subsystem inserts a second `http`. The hand-written `inprogress_name="tg_parser_http_requests_inprogress"` in the same constructor call is the tell: it is the only name in the block that did NOT go through the namespace/subsystem machinery, and it is the only one that came out right. **(2) Silently dropped duplicate registrations.** After `default()`, three more calls added `metrics.latency(...)` (with the intended ten buckets), `metrics.request_size(...)` and `metrics.response_size(...)`. `default()` has already registered those exact five series, so each re-registration raises `ValueError` inside the library's `_is_duplicated_time_series`, which catches it and returns `None`; `Instrumentator.add(None)` is a documented no-op. All three calls were therefore dead code that read as live configuration — which is why the bucket list sat in the file, looking applied, while the histogram ran on library defaults. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | Two distinct gaps. **(1) The one test that touched the name asserted the WRONG name as if it were right.** [`tests/test_metrics_instrumentation.py`](../../tests/test_metrics_instrumentation.py) built a local instrumentator with the same `metric_subsystem="http"` and asserted `"tg_parser_http_http_requests_total" in body`, with a comment explaining the doubled name as correct-by-construction («matches prod's create_instrumentator»). It was faithful to the code and blind to the requirement — it pinned the defect. **(2) Nothing compared the names the app EMITS against the names the alerts and dashboards QUERY.** The two sides live in different file types (Python vs YAML/JSON) and were never cross-checked by anything, in CI or by hand; `promtool` was not run in CI (see the 2026-08-04 Prometheus v3 CHANGELOG entry) and would not have caught this anyway, since a rule that queries a non-existent series is syntactically valid. **Update 2026-08-11: the promtool half of that sentence is no longer true** — CI now has a `Prometheus Rules (promtool)` job running `check rules`, `check config` and `test rules` on every PR (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). It still would not have caught BUG-089, exactly as the sentence says, because syntactic validity was never the gap; the cross-check test added by this entry remains the thing that catches it. Root-cause note on the dead `.add()` calls: no test asserted a bucket boundary, so a configuration that never took effect looked identical to one that did. |
| **Proposed fix (applied in this PR)** | **Minimal:** drop `metric_subsystem="http"` from `metrics.default(...)`; delete the three dead `.add()` calls; pass the buckets through `default()` as `latency_lowr_buckets`. Range extended to `(0.01 … 10.0, 30.0, 60.0)` rather than the original ten stopping at 10s — RAG endpoints inherit multi-second LLM latency (haiku avg 6.79 s, sonnet 8.72 s per [`S0_BASELINE_PROCESSING_METRICS_2026-07-07.md`](S0_BASELINE_PROCESSING_METRICS_2026-07-07.md) § Область 3), so a 10s ceiling would make `histogram_quantile(0.99)` return `+Inf`; `LLM_REQUEST_DURATION_SECONDS` already goes to 60. `latency_highr_buckets` left at the library default (it already reaches 60). **Hardening (the part that would have caught this):** a cross-check test that extracts every `tg_parser_http_*` name referenced by `alerts.yml` and `system.json` and asserts each is exposed by the instrumented app, plus a negative assertion that no `tg_parser_http_http` name exists and a positive assertion that the `le="0.01"` boundary is present. The cross-check fails in BOTH directions — an app-side rename or a consumer-side rename breaks it. One name is excluded with a comment: `tg_parser_http_requests_inprogress` is registered by the library's middleware without a `registry=` kwarg, so it always lands on the global default registry and cannot appear on a test-isolated `/metrics`; it is pinned separately against `create_instrumentator(registry=...).inprogress_name`. **The guard runs the PRODUCTION factory, and the first version of it did not — see § «Self-review: the first version of the guard was the same bug».** |
| **Self-review: the first version of the guard was the same bug** | The cross-check as first written built its own `Instrumentator` in the test file, hand-copied from `create_instrumentator` and kept in sync by a comment («Keep in sync with create_instrumentator»). Mutation testing before commit — reintroducing `metric_subsystem="http"` in `tg_parser/api/metrics.py` — left the suite **green**: the guard was asserting about a replica, so it could not have caught BUG-089 and would not catch its return. Structurally identical to the § «Why CI didn't catch» gap (1): a test faithful to a copy of the code rather than to the requirement. Fixed by giving `create_instrumentator` an optional `registry` parameter (prod path `registry=None` unchanged, singleton and all; an explicit registry bypasses the singleton and returns a fresh instrumentator) and building the test app from the real factory on an isolated `CollectorRegistry`, with the bucket tuple no longer duplicated in the test. Re-verified by three mutations, each now RED: `metric_subsystem="http"` back in the factory; `tg_parser_http_requests_total` renamed in `alerts.yml`; `latency_lowr_buckets` dropped. Note the app is built **once per module** — with the real factory, `should_instrument_requests_inprogress=True` means the library registers the inprogress gauge on the global registry, and a second build in the same session would raise on the duplicate. **A follow-up review the same day found two holes still left in the guard; both are now pinned.** (1) *The deliberate latency tail was unguarded.* Only the `le="0.01"` boundary was asserted, so deleting `30.0, 60.0` from `latency_lowr_buckets` left the suite green — and that tail is the owner decision that keeps `histogram_quantile(0.99)` off `+Inf` on RAG endpoints (see § «Proposed fix»). The tuple is now the module-level `HTTP_LATENCY_LOWR_BUCKETS` in `tg_parser/api/metrics.py`, consumed by the factory and imported by the test, which compares the FULL set of `le` values parsed out of the exposition body as **floats** (prometheus_client's `floatToGoString` formatting is not a contract worth pinning by string; the `+Inf` bucket is ignored). That equality alone is insufficient by construction — it reads both sides from the factory, so trimming the tuple moves expectation and reality together — so the ceiling is anchored *independently* against `LLM_REQUEST_DURATION_SECONDS`, the sibling histogram the 60 s was taken from, through a `_finite_bucket_bounds` helper that reads prometheus_client's private `_upper_bounds` and fails loudly if a future release moves it: `max(exposed) >= max(finite LLM bounds)`. No latency number is re-typed in the test. Deleting `30.0, 60.0` was GREEN before this change and is RED after it (`assert 10.0 >= 60.0`). (2) *The vacuity floor was per-suite, not per-file.* `assert len(checked) >= 2` is satisfied by `system.json` alone (it contributes 2 checked names, `alerts.yml` 1), so `alerts.yml` could be emptied — or the extraction regex could rot on YAML specifically — while the total stayed healthy. The floor is now **per file**: each consumer config must contribute at least one checked `tg_parser_http_*` name, and the failure message reports the per-file counts. Re-verified with a five-mutation matrix run in the worktree under a `cp`-backup + `trap restore EXIT` harness (never `git checkout --`, the worktree holds unrelated untracked work): tail deleted, `metric_subsystem="http"` restored, `latency_lowr_buckets` dropped, `tg_parser_http_requests_total` renamed in `alerts.yml`, every `tg_parser_http_*` stripped from `alerts.yml` — all five RED, suite GREEN again after restore. |
| **Workaround** | None needed pre-deploy, and none applied. Anyone who queried prod BEFORE the rebuilt image shipped had to use the doubled names (`tg_parser_http_http_*`); since it shipped (2026-08-04 10:56 UTC) the single names are the live ones. The consumer configs were already correct and were NOT touched by this fix. |
| **Artifacts** | Exposed-name list verified against a `TestClient` `/metrics` body on `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator==8.0.0` (`uv.lock`). Consumer references: `HighHTTPErrorRate` in `docker/prometheus/alerts.yml`; `tg_parser_http_requests_total` ×2, `tg_parser_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket` ×3, `tg_parser_http_requests_inprogress` ×1 in `docker/grafana/dashboards/system.json`. Historical records that deliberately KEEP the doubled name as observed fact (not corrected): [`WATCH_WINDOW_WAVE1_STEP4_VPS_2026-05-24.md`](WATCH_WINDOW_WAVE1_STEP4_VPS_2026-05-24.md), [`HANDOFF_NEW_CHAT_WATCH_WINDOW_WAVE1_STEP4_VPS_2026-05-24.md`](HANDOFF_NEW_CHAT_WATCH_WINDOW_WAVE1_STEP4_VPS_2026-05-24.md), [`REVIEW_2026-06-03_WAVE1_DONE.md`](REVIEW_2026-06-03_WAVE1_DONE.md), [`../runbooks/WAVE1_STEP4_VPS_POST_CLOSURE_CLEANUP.md`](../runbooks/WAVE1_STEP4_VPS_POST_CLOSURE_CLEANUP.md). |
| **Linked** | **BUG-038** — the same defect, misdiagnosed backwards on 2026-05-30 and closed 2026-06-03 by verifying that the rule text had changed rather than that the query returned data; a dated **CORRECTION 2026-08-04** paragraph is appended there and its `resolved` status deliberately stands (owner decision). **BUG-036** / **BUG-037** — the `DatasourceNoData` noise the mis-named rule generated, and the 2026-06-15 decommission (#149) that deleted the rule outright because it only ever emitted no-data. |

### BUG-088 (Medium — user-data hygiene / logging) — `fsm_confirm_unknown_token` writes the user's ENTIRE reply to the log at INFO (`normalized`), so on an armed ConfirmFlow turn any free text — including a pasted credential — lands in the log pipeline verbatim

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Medium**, reasoned rather than inherited from BUG-087 — and the honest range is Low/Medium, so the tie-break is recorded. **What argues DOWN.** No code path routes a secret here: `add_user_auth`'s `identifier` reaches BUG-087's two sites *structurally* (every successful call logs it), whereas it reaches `normalized` only if a human happens to type it. The obvious «confused re-paste» invitation is absent too — `add_user_auth`'s preview ([`_exec_add_user_auth`, `tools.py:3565–3583`](../../tg_parser/bot/tools.py)) names the credential type and the target user and never asks for the secret again, so nothing on screen prompts the user to send it. And the event is expected NOISE, not an anomaly (the runbook's own expectation column: «ожидаемый шум, не красный флаг»), so almost every record is a harmless «ладно» / «а что это значит». **What argues UP, and why it wins the tie-break.** (1) **The content is not shaped by the codebase at all.** A tool's arg set is a closed, enumerable vocabulary — that is exactly what makes BUG-087's deny-list possible. `normalized` is whatever a human typed, so there is no vocabulary to reason about and no upper bound on what a single record can contain. A redaction pass that fixes the three `args` sites and skips this one has fixed the predictable half of the exposure and left the unpredictable half. (2) **The branch's own gate selects FOR credential-shaped text.** A reply only reaches this log line after `_looks_like_new_intent` ([`handlers.py:533–549`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) has declined it, and that guard keys on a line-initial command verb or a question marker. An opaque `sk-…` / `mcp_…` paste has neither, so of all the free text a user could send on a confirm turn, secret-shaped strings are among the LEAST likely to be re-routed away and the MOST likely to land here. (3) **Wider population than BUG-087.** `add_user_auth` is admin-only, but ANY confirm-gated write tool arms ConfirmFlow — `add_channel`, `remove_channel`, `pause_channel`, `subscribe_*`, `unsubscribe_*`, `force_resummarize` — so every user of the bot can reach this branch, whereas BUG-087's credential vector needs an admin. (4) **The FSM deliberately stays armed**, so a user who is confused enough to paste the wrong thing once is invited to try again, and each attempt writes another full record. **Bound, stated as a property of the deployment rather than of the code** (the same honesty BUG-087's Severity row applies to itself): what actually keeps this below Severe is that the bot's logs are not currently shipped off-host, and that the one operator tool most likely to copy such a line out of the container is already field-whitelisted against it (see § «Operationally live» below). Neither is a property of `handlers.py`, and neither survives a decision to ship bot logs to an aggregator. Note explicitly what is NOT a mitigation: the record omits `tool`, so a leaked line carries no attached context — that is a diagnostic gap (see § Proposed fix), not a privacy control. |
| **Status** | `resolved` (2026-08-04) — merged as `245300e` ([PR #366](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/366); fix applied on branch `fix/bug088-unknown-token-log`, commit `11400ea`). See § **Fix applied** below for the shape, the key set and the test pins. **Prod is still leaking, and the merge did not change that: prod stays exposed until the bot container is re-created** on a rebuilt image — this is application code, not a compose tag, and `restart` keeps the old code (BUG-078), so until an operator re-creates `tg_parser_bot` the running container goes on writing the user's whole reply into `normalized`. That deploy is a separate owner decision and is NOT covered by this status. Filed 2026-07-31 as `open`. **NOT a #359 regression, and not touched by it — verified read-only, four independent ways.** (a) `git blame -L 1077,1092 tg_parser/bot/handlers.py` returns `66e8297` (2026-05-25) for **every** line of the block, comment and call alike. (b) `git log -S 'normalized=" ".join(text.split()).casefold()'` — repo-wide, not just this file — returns `66e8297` and nothing else. (c) `git log -G 'fsm_confirm_unknown_token' -- tg_parser/bot/handlers.py` returns TWO commits, `66e8297` and `48aeee7` (the #359 bot slice) — and the second is a **mention only**: its hunk adds the new `fsm_confirm_declined` block ([`handlers.py:1064–1073`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) whose comment names this event as the contrast case («the affirmative branch writes `fsm_confirm_execute` and the unknown one `fsm_confirm_unknown_token`»). Read the hunk before concluding anything from the `-G` hit — a grep-level match on an event name is not a change to the call that emits it. (d) `git log --follow --diff-filter=AR -- tg_parser/bot/handlers.py` returns only `22bea6d`, so no rename is hiding earlier history of the line. `66e8297` is two months before #359 / [PR #360](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/360) (`48aeee7` + `5752bdb`, merged `102bb4c`, 2026-07-31). |
| **Component** | `bot`, **one call site**. [`tg_parser/bot/handlers.py:1083–1087`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py) — `logger.info("fsm_confirm_unknown_token", chat_id=…, normalized=" ".join(text.split()).casefold())`, at the tail of `_handle_confirmation_response`. The kwarg set is exactly **two** fields, `chat_id` and `normalized`, and that is load-bearing in both directions: `normalized` is the record's ONLY diagnostic payload (so «just drop the field» empties the event), and there is no `tool` — unlike its three siblings `fsm_confirm_execute` / `fsm_confirm_declined` / `fsm_pagination_execute`, this record does not say which pending action the user failed to answer. `normalized` is the whole message: `str.split()` + `" ".join` collapses whitespace, `.casefold()` folds case, nothing is truncated and nothing is dropped. |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-31, adversarially re-reading BUG-087's «two sites» claim to see whether the entry's own framing («two exceptions to an otherwise-clean module») survived a full sweep of the bot's `logger.info` / `logger.warning` calls. It did not: this is the fourth full-VALUE site and the first one whose payload is raw user text rather than a tool's arguments. |
| **Root cause** | The line was born at INFO with the full value in it and has never been touched since. `66e8297` (2026-05-25, «fix(bot): require explicit affirmative confirmation before subscribe side-effects (BUG-031, BUG-032) (#111)») introduced the whole unknown-token branch as the BUG-032 closure: pre-fix the handler cleared the FSM and re-routed the reply through the LLM, producing the opaque «Я не совсем понимаю ваш ответ»; the fix keeps the FSM armed and answers with the accepted-token list, and logged the normalized reply so an operator could see WHY the classifier rejected it. The diagnostic intent is legitimate and is why this cannot be fixed by deletion (see § Proposed fix). The privacy dimension was simply never considered at the time — there is no comment about it at the call site, in contrast to the `arg_keys` sites two hundred lines above, which carry theirs in-line. **Methodology note for anyone re-deriving this, learned the expensive way on BUG-087 an hour earlier:** `git log -S` counts *occurrences* of a string, so it is blind to a commit that changes only a log LEVEL or moves a value between two calls — that is precisely how `b0dcef3`'s deliberate INFO→DEBUG demotion of `agent_tool_call`'s `args` was nearly missed. Both `-S` and `-G` were therefore run here, `-G` on the event name and on `normalized=` separately, and the `-G`-only hit was opened and read rather than counted. Conclusion after that check: **this field's level has never moved.** |
| **Why no security pass caught it — the precedent check, and the answer is more interesting than «nobody looked»** | Two F9 security passes exist and the field falls in the gap between them. **(1) `b0dcef3` (2026-04-10, «security: F9 Phase 1 — close critical and high vulnerabilities»)** is the pass that judged values-at-INFO to be a vulnerability and demoted `agent_tool_call`'s `args` to a separate `logger.debug` (BUG-087 § Root cause). It cannot have examined this field: `git show --stat b0dcef3` touches exactly one bot file, `tg_parser/bot/agent.py`, and the pass predates the birth of this line by six weeks. **(2) `757eba3` (2026-07-16, «feat(f9): Phase 2 prompt-injection defense») DID touch `handlers.py`** — and it is the finding. It added the input choke-point ([`handlers.py:754–760`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)): `sanitize_user_input(...)` followed by `logger.info("user_message", text_length=len(user_text))` — **length only, never the text**, on the bot's main free-text path. Its inline comment states the scope decision verbatim: «FSM confirm/clarify/pagination paths above are unchanged (**short tokens**)». So a security pass looked at this module, reasoned explicitly about the FSM confirm path, and excluded it on the stated assumption that it carries short tokens. The unknown-token branch is, by construction, the one branch of that path where the reply is **not** one of the short tokens — it is reached only when the whole normalized reply and its first token both fail both whitelists — and it logs that non-token in full. The assumption is falsified exactly where it matters. Note the ordering consequence too: the ConfirmFlow gate ([`handlers.py:698–700`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) returns **before** the sanitizer runs, so this text never passes through `sanitize_user_input` at all. Do not overstate that half — `MAX_USER_INPUT_LENGTH` is 4096 ([`input_sanitizer.py:27`](../../tg_parser/utils/input_sanitizer.py)), the same as Telegram's own per-message limit, so the cap would barely have bounded a single reply anyway. The point is the reasoning, not the number. **Contrast with BUG-087, and it is a clean inversion:** there, values at INFO were examined, judged a vulnerability, closed, and then consciously traded back for forensics — a decision the project can be held to. Here the field was never adjudicated at all; it was skipped by an assumption this very branch contradicts. |
| **When it fires — branch semantics, verified against the code** | A reply reaches line 1083 only after ALL of: the FSM is in `ConfirmFlow.awaiting_confirmation` (so a preview is live and a write is pending); the pending action has not expired (`_is_pending_expired` returns first, [`handlers.py:952–955`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)); `_looks_like_new_intent(text)` is False, i.e. no line-initial command verb and no question marker (otherwise the turn is re-routed at [`handlers.py:965–967`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py) and no record is written); and `classify_confirmation_token(text)` returns `"unknown"`, which requires that **neither** the whole normalized reply **nor** its first whitespace-token (minus trailing `,.;:!?`) is in `AFFIRMATIVE_TOKENS` or `NEGATIVE_TOKENS` ([`handlers.py:454–494`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)). Note the first-token rule: «да, вот мой ключ …» classifies as **affirmative** and goes to `fsm_confirm_execute` instead, so this site sees only replies whose opening word is not a confirmation word — which is the shape of a bare paste. The FSM is **deliberately left armed** afterwards (no `state.clear()`); the user gets the accepted-token list and the TTL, and can retry within the same flow. Retries re-enter the same branch and re-log. |
| **Blast radius** | Every free-text reply that misses both whitelists on an armed confirm turn, from every user of the bot, for the whole retention of the container log. Per record the content is unbounded up to Telegram's 4096-character message limit. The credential case is the one that motivates the entry, but it is not the only sensitive class a confused user can paste on a «Подтвердите [да/нет]» turn. Volume is expected to be non-trivial by design — the runbook classes this event as normal noise, so unlike BUG-087's two sites this one is not rare. |
| **Why this is its OWN number and not a widening of BUG-087 (owner decision, 2026-07-31)** | The file's convention is one CONCERN per entry, and the test the project has been applying is whether the FIX is indivisible. BUG-087's second site was folded IN because a redaction of `agent_tool_call` alone would leave the same credential landing via `fsm_confirm_execute` — one deny-list, two consumers, one change or it is not correct at all. This site is the mirror image: BUG-087's proposed mechanism is **a deny-list keyed on argument NAMES**, and it cannot reach here even in principle, because there is no argument name to deny — the offending value is free-form user text in a dedicated field, not a member of a key/value arg map. Same file, adjacent lines, overlapping motivation, **disjoint fix mechanism** ⇒ separate entry. The practical consequence is the one that matters for closure hygiene: BUG-087 can be fully fixed and correctly closed while this exposure is still live, which is exactly the state a single shared number would have made unrepresentable. BUG-087's `Component` and `Blast radius` rows therefore stay at **two** sites, and its audit row now points here. |
| **Precedent for the norm this violates** | «Log the shape, never the value» is written down in this codebase in four places, three of them verified in the working tree and one in git history. **(1)** `write_intent_set` ([`handlers.py:901–907`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) — `arg_keys=sorted(...)`, with the reason as a code comment: «Keys only — `add_user_auth` carries a raw credential in a VALUE». **(2)** `write_intent_router_resume` ([`handlers.py:2830–2836`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) — the same `arg_keys` kwarg, same shape. Both are pinned by `TestWriteIntentLogPrivacy` ([`tests/test_bot_write_intent_trigger_359.py:1072–1104`](../../tests/test_bot_write_intent_trigger_359.py)), whose docstring already states the rule this entry is about — «argument KEYS only … **and the user's message never reaches the log**» — and whose assertions include `assert secret not in blob` on a `json.dumps` of every captured record. The test enforces that over `write_intent_*` events only; `fsm_confirm_unknown_token` is outside its `_EVENTS` set. **(3)** `user_message` ([`handlers.py:760`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) logs `text_length=len(user_text)` — the bot's own main path already answers the exact question this entry raises, with a length. **(4)** The #359-deleted shadow layer stated the rule in full, in a comment removed by `48aeee7` from [`tg_parser/bot/agent.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/agent.py) (recoverable via `git show 48aeee7`): «Keys only — `add_user_auth` args carry a raw credential value. The same norm covers `user_message`: only the BOOLEAN verdict is logged, never the text (not even truncated) — **a user's message can quote a credential just as easily as an argument can.**» That sentence is this bug, written down by the project two weeks before this entry was filed, as the justification for a design that was applied one function away and not here. Its pin survives the deletion: `test_the_agent_logs_no_verdict_and_no_message_text` ([`tests/test_f5c_bot_force_resummarize.py:761–789`](../../tests/test_f5c_bot_force_resummarize.py)) still asserts `user_message not in blob`, again scoped to the agent, not to this handler. **(5)** A bounded-snippet precedent also exists, and it is the closest thing to a sanctioned exception: `_record_suspect` ([`input_sanitizer.py:63–72`](../../tg_parser/utils/input_sanitizer.py)) logs `snippet=(snippet or text)[:80]` plus `text_length` — but at **WARNING**, gated on an injection-pattern match, i.e. deliberately traded for a security signal, not a default. |
| **Operationally live right now — and one correction to the framing this entry was filed under** | **(1) The 24h #359 watch is running until 2026-08-01 18:18 UTC** ([`F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md) § «#359 / ADR-0020 — deterministic confirm trigger»; container `StartedAt 2026-07-31T18:18:43Z`), and its documented filter is `select(.event \| test("^write_intent_\|^fsm_confirm_"))` — which **captures these records whole**, `normalized` included, because the manual `jq` fallback prints the entire object. That is the live path by which a full record can end up pasted into a check-point note. The watch table's row for this event was given an explicit privacy caveat the same day («⚠️ это **ВЕСЬ** ответ пользователя целиком … **дословно в заметки / issue такие строки не тащить**»), which is the correct interim control: narrowing the filter instead would blind the watch it exists to run. **(2) `docker/watch_359.sh` — the framing this entry was commissioned under said the script «prints an error dump of raw log lines». That is not what the script does, and the correction is a mitigating fact worth recording rather than a nitpick.** Its error dump is field-whitelisted (`["logger","tool","chat_id","error_class","arg_keys","rendered_verbatim"]`); every other key is reported BY NAME ONLY as `[suppressed: …]`, so `normalized` would be named and not printed; the script says so on screen («REDACTED view … these logs can carry user text and secrets»); and if `jq` fails it prints nothing rather than falling back to raw lines. Its header comment cites BUG-087 and names **this very field** as one of the two reasons the whitelist exists. So the operator tooling built for this watch is already hardened against this record — the remaining operator-facing exposure is the runbook's manual `jq` command, which is unfiltered by design. Two secondary notes: the script's dump only ever sees an INFO record like this one if the user's own text happens to contain `error` / `warn` / `traceback` / `exception` / `critical`, since the dump is selected by a raw `grep -Ei` over log LINES; and none of this was reviewed further, as that script is owned elsewhere — the claims above are from a targeted read of its error-dump block only. |
| **Fix shape analysis — four candidates weighed when the entry was filed; (d)+(a) was recommended here and is what shipped on 2026-08-04. Row kept as written; § Fix applied below records what the code actually does** | **The tension to respect: the field is not gratuitous.** An operator needs to know WHY a token was rejected, and the answer is usually IN the text — an unlisted synonym («ладно», «окей», «yep»), punctuation the normalizer does not strip (only trailing `,.;:!?` on the first token is), a typo («дя»), a wrong keyboard layout, an emoji outside the set. Dropping the field would make the whitelist un-tunable from production evidence and would silently discard the one thing that closed BUG-032. Four candidate shapes, with what each costs. **(a) Shape summary — `length` + character-class facts** (`token_count`, `is_single_token`, script/`has_digits`/`has_punct` flags). Keeps: «one short Cyrillic word» ⇒ probably a synonym; «47 chars, mixed alnum, single token» ⇒ probably a paste, and that second verdict is itself the alert you would want. Costs: you can no longer learn WHICH synonym to add — the highest-value action the field currently supports. Precedent: `user_message`'s `text_length`. **(b) Truncation to a few characters.** Keeps: nearly all real synonym recovery, since every token in both whitelists is ≤ 14 characters, so a ~12–16 char prefix captures the realistic cases intact. Costs: a short secret (a 12-character password) is exposed in full, and a long API key leaks a correlatable, often provider-identifying prefix — this is a reduction in blast radius, not a redaction, and it should be described that way if chosen. Precedent: `_record_suspect`'s 80-char snippet, though that one is WARNING-gated on a match. **(c) Hash of the normalized text.** Keeps: repeat correlation — «the same unrecognised reply 40 times this week» is exactly the signal that says «add it to the whitelist», and it survives without any content. Costs: **an unsalted hash of a short, low-entropy human reply is not a privacy control** — a dictionary of candidate tokens reverses it trivially, and a 12-character password is well within brute-force range. Honest framing: a correlation key that happens to be opaque to a casual reader, not redaction. A keyed HMAC with a per-deployment secret fixes the reversal but also destroys cross-deployment comparability. **(d) Whitelist-shaped classification — the shadow layer's own answer, and the recommended default.** Emit a verdict from a CLOSED vocabulary computed against the whitelists rather than extracted from the text: `near_miss_affirmative` / `near_miss_negative` (edit distance ≤ 1, or equal after stripping non-alphanumerics — catches «дя», «да!», «"да"», Latin-`a`-in-Cyrillic-`да` homoglyphs), `single_token_unlisted`, `multi_token_free_text`, `non_text`. Keeps: the entire typo/near-miss class, which is the one an operator can act on immediately, at ZERO value exposure — the output vocabulary is fixed at compile time, so no user byte can ride out on it. Costs: an unlisted synonym that is not a near-miss («ладно») degrades to `single_token_unlisted`, telling you a synonym problem exists but not which word; recovering that would need one of (a)/(b)/(c) alongside. **Recommendation: (d) + (a) together** — a closed-vocabulary verdict plus length and token count — and add the missing `tool` field while the line is being touched, since the record currently cannot be correlated to the pending action it belongs to. **If the full text is judged indispensable**, the in-repo precedent for how to keep it is `b0dcef3`'s shape: split the line, structural fields at INFO and the raw value at `logger.debug` — but record that this precedent cuts both ways, since `8332aa3` reverted exactly that split for forensic reasons, and DEBUG in production would re-expose everything. **Test that would pin it**, in the spirit of `TestWriteIntentLogPrivacy` and belonging next to `TestUnknownConfirmationTokenException` in [`tests/test_bot_confirm_flow.py`](../../tests/test_bot_confirm_flow.py): drive `_handle_confirmation_response` with an armed `ConfirmFlow` and a secret-shaped reply, then assert three things, not one — that a `fsm_confirm_unknown_token` record still EXISTS (a privacy test that passes when the event is deleted is a trap), that the secret is absent from `json.dumps` of the captured records, and that the record's key set equals an expected literal set, so a future field addition has to be deliberate. Pair it with a positive diagnostic test — «дя» ⇒ `near_miss_affirmative` — so the fix is pinned on BOTH axes and cannot be satisfied by quietly emptying the event. |
| **Fix applied (2026-08-04)** | Shape **(d)+(a)**, in a new bot-local helper [`tg_parser/bot/confirm_unknown_log.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/confirm_unknown_log.py) (stdlib only; deliberately NOT folded into `log_redaction.py`, whose deny-list is keyed on argument NAMES and cannot reach free text). The INFO record is now exactly the eight keys of `UNKNOWN_CONFIRM_LOG_KEYS` — `chat_id`, `tool`, `verdict`, `length`, `token_count`, `is_single_token`, `has_digits`, `has_punct` — and `normalized` is gone from the call site. `verdict` is one of five compile-time strings (`UNKNOWN_CONFIRM_VERDICTS`): `non_text`, `near_miss_affirmative`, `near_miss_negative`, `single_token_unlisted`, `multi_token_free_text`. **What the shape buys back.** The BUG-032 question «why was the token rejected» still answers: «дя» → `near_miss_affirmative` (Levenshtein ≤ 1, single token only, or equality after stripping non-alnum, since the classifier strips only trailing `,.;:!?` from the first token); a long alnum single token with `has_digits` → `single_token_unlisted`, which is the paste shape and the alert an operator would actually want; emoji-only → `non_text`. What is NOT recoverable is WHICH synonym to whitelist — the accepted cost of (d)+(a), recorded in the row above. **Оговорка: любой одиночный алфавитно-цифровой символ (`x`, `5`) даёт `near_miss_affirmative`** — в whitelist есть односимвольные `y` / `n`, до которых расстояние 1 достигается тривиально. Смотреть `length` прежде, чем читать вердикт как опечатку. Это следствие LOCKED-правила «edit distance ≤ 1», не дефект: класс односимвольных ответов целиком читается как near-miss, поэтому «прямой кандидат на расширение whitelist» к нему не относится. Записано и в runbook-строке события. `tool` also closes the diagnostic gap noted in § Component: the record now says which pending action went unanswered. **Whitelists are read, never copied.** The helper resolves `AFFIRMATIVE_TOKENS` / `NEGATIVE_TOKENS` from `handlers` through a function-local import (a module-level one would be a cycle, since `handlers` imports the helper), so the near-miss verdict is always computed against the same frozensets `classify_confirmation_token` uses. A local copy would have passed its tests and silently drifted on the next whitelist entry. **Handler behaviour is untouched:** user-facing text bit-for-bit identical, FSM still armed, no branch re-ordered — the diff at the site is the `logger.info` kwargs and a comment. Pins in [`tests/test_bot_confirm_unknown_log_088.py`](../../tests/test_bot_confirm_unknown_log_088.py): a handler-level privacy pin through the real `_handle_confirmation_response` (secret-shaped reply ⇒ event **exists**, literal key set, no `normalized` / `text` / `message`, secret absent from `json.dumps` of every captured record — compared **casefolded**, because the pre-fix site folded the reply and a plain substring check would have missed its own defect), a source tripwire on the defect expression and on a DEBUG re-dump (`b0dcef3` / `8332aa3`), the verdict table, and a near-miss pin that mutates every single-token alnum entry of the live whitelists by one edit (the non-alphanumeric entries `+` / `👍` / `-` / `👎` and the two-word negatives are skipped by construction — one edit of a bare `+` is not a single-token alnum reply, and doubling the first character of «не надо» leaves two tokens). Verified by mutation: with the pre-fix `logger.info` restored in a throwaway copy of the tree, seven of the twenty tests fail and the privacy pin prints the leaked record. |
| **Adjacent sites audited and deliberately EXCLUDED (recorded so their omission is not mistaken for an oversight)** | **(1)** `fsm_pagination_execute` ([`handlers.py:1430–1435`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) — full `args` at INFO, already audited and excluded under BUG-087 as read-only (pagination cursors and offsets, no confirm-gated write tool). Unchanged by this entry. **(2)** `tool_validation_error` and `tool_permission_denied` ([`tools.py:1387–1399`](../../tg_parser/bot/tools.py)) log `message=str(exc)`, and an exception message CAN echo the offending input value. Out of scope here on three counts: level **WARNING** not INFO, a different mechanism (an exception's own string, not a field the call site chose to pass), and a different fix. Flagged for the owner rather than folded in — **which validators actually echo a VALUE rather than a key name was not audited**, and `watch_359.sh`'s header already names `tool_validation_error` alongside this entry's field as a reason its dump is whitelisted, so someone has already noticed. **(3)** `UnknownConfirmationToken.__init__` ([`handlers.py:445–451`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) embeds `normalized_text!r` in its exception message. Not a log site today — the class is exported and unit-tested but **never raised in production code** (only [`tests/test_bot_confirm_flow.py`](../../tests/test_bot_confirm_flow.py) constructs it). Recorded because a future `raise` of it onto a logged path would silently re-create this exposure through a second door. |
| **Left open for the owner (deliberately not decided here)** | (1) **Which fix shape** — (d)+(a) is recommended above, not chosen. (2) **Whether this lands in the same PR as BUG-087.** Separate NUMBERS is settled; a shared privacy slice is still a reasonable delivery choice and this entry does not presume the PR boundary either way. (3) **Whether that slice also sweeps `fsm_pagination_execute`** — cheap consistency, zero known exposure. (4) **Whether to retro-scan the live container log** for `fsm_confirm_unknown_token` records with credential-shaped payloads before the watch window closes at 2026-08-01 18:18 UTC. That needs prod access this session did not have and must not be presumed done; note that `MemoryStorage`-era logs only reach back to the 18:18:43Z re-create anyway. (5) **Whether the runbook caveat is sufficient interim control** for the remaining window — assessed above as yes, since narrowing the watch filter would blind the watch, but it is the owner's call. **Decided 2026-08-04, when the fix was commissioned:** (1) shape → **(d)+(a)**, applied (§ Fix applied); (2) **own PR** — BUG-087 had already merged, so there was no shared slice left to join; (3) `fsm_pagination_execute` → **not swept**, it stays excluded on the reasoning in the row below; (5) runbook caveat → superseded, the table row now describes the new fields instead of warning about `normalized`. **(4) is the one that stayed open: the retro-scan was NOT done** — it needs prod access this session deliberately did not take, and it must not be read as closed by the code fix. The window it was scoped to has since passed (2026-08-01 18:18 UTC), so it is now an ops judgement call on whatever log stream still exists, not a pre-merge task. |
| **Linked** | **BUG-087** (the three `args`-at-INFO sites in the same module; its § «Precedent for the norm» row records this site's audit and now points here), **BUG-031** / **BUG-032** (the incidents `66e8297` closed — the branch and its diagnostic exist because of them, so any fix must keep the unknown-token cause diagnosable), **BUG-086** § «Architectural replacement» (the #359 adjudication whose deleted shadow layer wrote down the norm this violates), [issue #359](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/issues/359), [`F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md) § «#359 / ADR-0020» (the live watch filter that captures these records, and the privacy caveat on the table row). |
