### BUG-087 (Medium — credential hygiene / logging) — TWO bot log sites (`agent_tool_call` and `fsm_confirm_execute`) log every tool's `args` unredacted at INFO, so a raw `add_user_auth` credential is written to the log pipeline in plaintext on BOTH turns of the confirm protocol

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Medium** — credential hygiene, not correctness. Nothing breaks and nothing is mis-written; the exposure is that a secret the tool otherwise HASHES before storage is emitted verbatim to logs, i.e. to disk and to whatever ships them onward, with a retention nobody chose for it. Bounded by the fact that `add_user_auth` is admin-only and rare, and that the bot's logs are not currently shipped off-host — which is what keeps it below Severe rather than any property of the code. |
| **Status** | `resolved` (2026-08-02) — shared deny-list helper [`tg_parser/bot/log_redaction.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/log_redaction.py) (`redact_tool_args`) consumed by **both** INFO sites: `agent_tool_call` ([`agent.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/agent.py)) and `fsm_confirm_execute` ([`handlers.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)). `add_user_auth.identifier` redacted (prefix/length token; key retained); non-secret args unchanged for BUG-002/004 forensics. Privacy pins + declaration tripwire in [`tests/test_bot_log_redaction_087.py`](../../tests/test_bot_log_redaction_087.py). Does **not** touch BUG-088 (`normalized`), FSM-in-memory credential storage, or `fsm_pagination_execute`. |
| **Component** | `bot`, **two independent call sites** (both must be fixed — see § «Second call site» below). **(1)** [`tg_parser/bot/agent.py:424–429`](../../tg_parser/bot/agent.py) — `logger.info("agent_tool_call", tool=…, turn=…, args=tool_args)` inside `GeminiAgent.process_message`'s function-call loop; kwarg **`args`**, level **INFO**, full values. **(2)** [`tg_parser/bot/handlers.py:982–987`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py) — `logger.info("fsm_confirm_execute", tool=…, args=confirmed_args, chat_id=…)` in `_handle_confirmation_response`'s affirmative branch; kwarg **`args`** (line 985), level **INFO**, full values, and `confirmed_args = {**original_args, "confirm": True}` so it carries every original arg verbatim. |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-31, while adjudicating a Bugbot finding on [issue #359](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/issues/359) that claimed the new `pending_write_intent` snapshot introduced a credential exposure. That claim was **wrong** (the snapshot is in-process `MemoryStorage` for ≤ `PENDING_TTL_SECONDS`, and the normal confirm path already writes the same args to `pending_action`), but checking it surfaced this larger, older, and genuinely persistent one — which the review did not flag. |
| **Root cause** | **The two sites have DIFFERENT origins — corrected 2026-07-31 against `git log -S` / `git show`, read-only; the earlier «same commit» claim mis-dated site (1) by three weeks and hid a deliberate reversal.** Site **(1)** shipped with the bot itself: `git log -S 'args=tool_args' -- tg_parser/bot/agent.py` returns exactly one commit, `22bea6d` (2026-04-04, «feat: Phase 3 — Telegram bot with Gemini agent (V1.0)»), and `git show 22bea6d:tg_parser/bot/agent.py` already carries `logger.info("agent_tool_call", tool=tool_name, args=tool_args, turn=turn)` on line 118 — **three weeks BEFORE** the BUG-002 / BUG-004 incidents this row used to credit it to. It did not stay at INFO throughout, and the gap is the most interesting fact in this row: the security pass `b0dcef3` (2026-04-10, «security: F9 Phase 1 — close critical and high vulnerabilities») **deliberately demoted the args off INFO**, splitting the line into `logger.info("agent_tool_call", tool=…, turn=…)` + `logger.debug("agent_tool_call_args", …, args=tool_args, …)`, and `8332aa3` **re-promoted them** to INFO with the BUG-002/004 forensics comment written above them. So this project has ALREADY once judged tool `args` at INFO to be a vulnerability and closed it; the present exposure is a conscious reversal of that judgement in exchange for forensic value, which strengthens rather than weakens the case for a redaction pass (the forensic goal and the security goal were never reconciled, only traded back and forth). Note the corollary for anyone re-deriving this: `git log -S 'args=tool_args'` shows only `22bea6d` because both later commits kept the string's occurrence count at 1 — the LEVEL moved, the string did not, so `-S` alone cannot see `b0dcef3`; `-G 'agent_tool_call'` is what surfaces all three. Site **(2)** genuinely originates in `8332aa3` (`git log -S 'args=confirmed_args' -- tg_parser/bot/handlers.py` → that commit alone), since `fsm_confirm_execute` did not exist before the FSM landed. Both current INFO levels therefore date to `8332aa3` (2026-04-28, «fix(bug-002+004): bot FSM — deterministic confirm + stateful pagination (Session D)»), added as forensics for BUG-002 / BUG-004, where the whole point was seeing the exact args of a destructive call (`remove_channel args={'channel_id': …, 'confirm': true}`) — `agent_tool_call` for the call the LLM issued, `fsm_confirm_execute` for the call the FSM replayed with `confirm=True`. Both log `args` wholesale and there is no allow-list, deny-list or redaction anywhere on either path — the codebase's only two redaction helpers, `_redacted_key_prefix` ([`tg_parser/api/auth.py`](../../tg_parser/api/auth.py)) and `_mask_password` ([`tg_parser/storage/engine_factory.py`](../../tg_parser/storage/engine_factory.py)), are in the API and storage layers and are not reached from the bot. `add_user_auth`'s `identifier` is documented in its own declaration as «Raw credential value (hashed automatically for api_key/mcp_token)», so the hashing that protects it at REST is defeated in the log. |
| **Blast radius** | Any confirm-gated write tool whose args carry a secret. Today that is `add_user_auth.identifier` only; `register_user` / `update_user` / `remove_user_auth` carry identifiers but not secrets. Note the multiplier: the loop logs on EVERY turn, and the #359 double-confirm path re-issues the tool, so one credential can appear several times per conversation. **And the exposure survives fixing the agent loop alone** — the second site writes it again on the confirm turn, from a different module, on a path the agent loop is not on at all. |
| **Second call site — `fsm_confirm_execute` (found 2026-07-31, after this entry was filed; the reason the entry was widened rather than closed)** | [`handlers.py:982–987`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py) logs `args=confirmed_args` — **full values, INFO** — in the affirmative branch of `_handle_confirmation_response`. `add_user_auth` IS confirm-gated ([`tools.py:149`](../../tg_parser/bot/tools.py), inside `_WRITE_TOOLS_REQUIRING_CONFIRM` declared at `tools.py:110`), so an auth-mapping write always reaches this branch: the raw `identifier` is written to the container log a **second** time, on the CONFIRM turn, **independently** of the `agent_tool_call` write on the initial preview turn. `confirmed_args` is `{**original_args, "confirm": True}`, so nothing is filtered on the way in. **Why this had to be recorded rather than left implicit:** BUG-087 as originally filed named ONE site. A fix that redacts `agent_tool_call` alone would leave the credential still landing on disk via the confirm turn, pass its own tests, and let the bug be closed while the exposure it describes is still live — the confirm turn is the one turn that is GUARANTEED to happen for every successful `add_user_auth`, whereas the preview turn's arg set is whatever the LLM chose. Any fix must be verified against BOTH events in the log. |
| **Fix applied (2026-08-02)** | Shared deny-list helper [`tg_parser/bot/log_redaction.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/log_redaction.py) (`redact_tool_args`) consumed by **both** INFO sites — `agent_tool_call` and `fsm_confirm_execute` — so the two cannot drift apart. `add_user_auth.identifier` replaced by a `_redacted_key_prefix`-style prefix/length token (key retained); non-secret args unchanged (deny-list, not allow-list) so BUG-002/004 forensics stay. Declaration-scanning tripwire + privacy pins on **both** events in [`tests/test_bot_log_redaction_087.py`](../../tests/test_bot_log_redaction_087.py). See **Status** row for scope boundaries (BUG-088 / FSM storage / pagination excluded). |
| **Precedent for the norm — the deliberate contrast that makes these two sites a NORM VIOLATION, not an oversight** | «Keys only, never values» is an established, deliberately-implemented project norm, and the two sites in this entry are the places that break it. **(1)** `write_intent_set` ([`handlers.py:901–907`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) passes **`arg_keys=sorted(...)`** — keys only, never values — with the reason written into the code at the call site as a comment: «Keys only — `add_user_auth` carries a raw credential in a VALUE». Pinned by `TestWriteIntentLogPrivacy`, and observed holding on live prod traffic (`arg_keys=["topic_id"]`, see BUG-086 § «Production e2e verification of the replacement»). **(2)** Its sibling `write_intent_router_resume` ([`handlers.py:2830–2836`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) uses the same **`arg_keys`** kwarg. **(3)** `add_user_auth`'s own preview payload ([`_exec_add_user_auth`, `tools.py:3561–3583`](../../tg_parser/bot/tools.py)) deliberately NAMES the credential type and target user while never echoing the raw secret — with the intent stated in a comment («The preview NAMES the credential type + target user but NEVER echoes the raw secret»). **(4)** The deleted #359 shadow layer logged a boolean verdict rather than the user's message text, explicitly because «a user message can quote a credential just as easily». So the codebase knows the rule, states it in-line, and tests it — `agent_tool_call` (`args`) and `fsm_confirm_execute` (`args`) are the only two places in the bot that pass a TOOL'S full arg VALUES on a path that can carry a credential, i.e. exactly where the norm says KEYS. The contrast is what settles the severity question: this is not an unexamined default, it is two sites left behind a norm the rest of the module already follows. **Third `args`-with-values site, checked and deliberately EXCLUDED from this bug's scope:** `fsm_pagination_execute` ([`handlers.py:1430–1435`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) also logs `args=page_args` in full at INFO, but its `page_args` come from the read-only pagination surface (`list_*` / `search` cursors + offsets), so no confirm-gated write tool and no secret-bearing arg can reach it. Recorded here so a future reader does not mistake its omission for an oversight — and so that if the fix lands as a shared redaction helper, extending it to this site is a cheap consistency win rather than a newly-discovered exposure. **FOURTH full-VALUE site, of a DIFFERENT shape — it logs the USER'S TEXT rather than a tool's args, and it is FILED SEPARATELY as **BUG-088** (§ BUG-088 above; owner decision 2026-07-31; the audit below is kept here as the trail that found it).** The `Component` / `Blast radius` rows of THIS entry therefore stay at two sites: widening them would commit the indivisible-fix argument to a site the proposed deny-list cannot reach, which is precisely the reason the split was made rather than a widening — this entry's mechanism is a deny-list keyed on argument NAMES, and there is no argument name to deny in a free-text field. This is the mirror image of the § «Record-keeping decision» row below: the second site was folded IN because its fix is indivisible from site (1)'s, and this fourth site is kept OUT because its fix is disjoint from both. `fsm_confirm_unknown_token` ([`handlers.py:1083–1087`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py)) logs `normalized=" ".join(text.split()).casefold()` — the user's **entire** reply, verbatim modulo whitespace and case, at **INFO**, on a turn where a ConfirmFlow is **armed**. Pre-existing and NOT a #359 regression: `git log -S 'normalized=" ".join(text.split()).casefold()'` and `git blame -L 1083,1087` both give `66e8297` (2026-05-25, «fix(bot): require explicit affirmative confirmation before subscribe side-effects (BUG-031, BUG-032)»), two months before #359. **This is in tension with the severity argument above and the tension must be stated, not glossed.** That argument leans on the norm quoted from the deleted shadow layer — «the user's message text is never logged, not even truncated … a user message can quote a credential just as easily» — to show that the two `args` sites break a rule the module otherwise keeps. This site shows the rule is kept **less** universally than that framing implies: the shadow layer honoured it, but the unknown-token branch has been writing whole user replies to INFO since May. It does not change the two `args` sites' severity (a tool's `args` carry `add_user_auth.identifier` **structurally** on an admin-only path, whereas a credential lands in `normalized` only if a user happens to type one at a ConfirmFlow prompt — lower likelihood, unbounded content), and it does not change the «keys only, never values» norm being real and deliberately implemented where it is implemented. What it changes is the claim's SCOPE: the correct statement is «the bot has four INFO sites that emit full values, three of them tool args and one of them raw user text», not «two exceptions to an otherwise-clean module». Any redaction pass must therefore decide about `normalized` too — truncate it, hash it, or replace it with a classification verdict (the shadow layer's own answer: log the verdict, never the text) — and the deny-list helper proposed above does not reach it, since there is no arg name to deny; that decision now lives in **BUG-088** § «Proposed fix», which weighs those four shapes against the diagnostic they would destroy. Operator-facing consequence recorded in [`../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md) § «#359 / ADR-0020 …»: the `^fsm_confirm_` watch filter captures these records, so the runbook now carries an explicit «do not paste verbatim» caveat on the field. |
| **Record-keeping decision (2026-07-31) — the second site EXTENDS BUG-087 rather than getting its own number** | The file's convention is one CONCERN per entry, and this is the same concern — a bot log site passing tool `args` with full VALUES at INFO, exposing `add_user_auth.identifier` — at a second location, with the same root cause, the same severity bound, and a fix that must be applied as one change to be correct at all. The «same origin commit (`8332aa3`)» support this row used to claim is **narrowed** (2026-07-31, per the Root cause row): `8332aa3` is where BOTH sites reached their current INFO level, so «same origin» holds of the EXPOSURE — but site (1)'s log line is three weeks older (`22bea6d`) and passed through a deliberate demotion in between, so it does not hold of the code. The decision stands on its four remaining supports either way. A sibling BUG number would split a single indivisible fix across two entries and invite exactly the half-fix this row exists to prevent (redact one site, close its number, leave the other open under a different one). The entry's **Component** and **Blast radius** rows were widened instead; no new number was allocated. Precedent in this file for widening an entry with a later-found instance of the same defect rather than re-filing: BUG-086's four «precision pass» rows, each a newly-found instance of one detector defect, all kept under BUG-086. |
| **Linked** | **BUG-002** / **BUG-004** (the incidents both log lines were added for — any fix must keep them forensically useful), **BUG-086** § «Architectural replacement» (the adjudication that surfaced this), [issue #359](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/issues/359). |

### BUG-086 (Severe — bot correctness) — the new `force_resummarize` `dry_run` flag re-opened the BUG-046 dead-end: a mutation request answered with the terminal dry-run report + an LLM-authored «Подтвердите … [да/нет]», so «да» hit «Я не совсем понимаю ваш ответ»

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Severe** — bot correctness. The primary UX of a just-shipped admin write-tool was unreachable conversationally: a re-summarize could not be triggered from Telegram at all (the confirmation the bot itself asked for had no effect). No data loss, no token burn — the failure is a dead-end, not a wrong write. Same class as BUG-046 / BUG-045 / BUG-039 («да» dead-ends on the opaque fallback). |
| **Status** | `resolved` (2026-07-26) — **fixed & deployed to prod**. [PR #358](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/358) (commits `11c71c7` + `8a7cf79`) merged as `9aadf5e`; prod `b6c21ef → 9aadf5e`, `tg_parser:latest` rebuilt, `tg_parser_bot` re-created (BUG-078: re-create, NOT `restart`) and `healthy`. In-container smoke PASS — 35 tools, `bot.yaml` `1.9.3`, and the detector verified against live code (prod ask → `True`; the report paraphrase and the `next_step` echo → `False`); 0 error/traceback in the first 25 min. Deploy record: [`F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md). ✅ **Owner e2e smoke in `@Tgingest_bot` PASS 2026-07-26 07:50–07:56 UTC** — the original failing scenario now behaves correctly end-to-end, verified against prod logs (row «Production e2e verification» below). Shadow-mode `read_only_intent` watch: first window closed with a **structurally empty** sample — see the same row. |
| **Component** | `bot`. [`tg_parser/bot/tools.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/tools.py) (`force_resummarize` declaration + `_exec_force_resummarize` branch A), [`tg_parser/bot/agent.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/agent.py) (`GeminiAgent.process_message` preview-hint capture), [`prompts/bot.yaml`](../../prompts/bot.yaml) (write-ops instruction, v1.9.2 → v1.9.3). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-25 — **manual prod smoke** by the owner immediately after the F5-C bot `force_resummarize` slice was deployed (commit `88d4c94`, [PR #357](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/357), merged as `b6c21ef`). |
| **Symptoms (prod transcript, admin user)** | «покажи, что будет, если пере-суммаризировать тему topic:tg:Docma_ru:post:252» → correct dry-run report. Then «пере-суммаризируй тему topic:tg:Docma_ru:post:252» (a REAL mutation request) → the bot repeated the **same dry-run report** and appended its own «Подтвердите, пожалуйста, пере-суммаризацию темы "Сервис DocMa …" [да/нет]». The follow-up «да» → «Я не совсем понимаю ваш ответ. Пожалуйста, уточните, что вы имели в виду.» Nothing was ever re-summarized. |
| **Root cause (verified — prod logs + code-traced)** | Two coupled defects. **(1) Wrong call shape.** Prod `agent_tool_call` lines show the mutation turn (`request_id=28b0d1c9`, 2026-07-25T16:30:59Z) called `force_resummarize` with `args={"dry_run": true, "topic_id": "topic:tg:Docma_ru:post:252"}` — `dry_run=true`, **no `confirm` at all** — identical to the preceding read-only turn (`68c99d49`, 16:30:17Z). Routing is `mode="AUTO"` at temp 0.2 and the shipped declaration advertised «Set dry_run=true **first** for a no-op report», which reads as a step *towards* a run, so the LLM used the report shape for both intents. **(2) The framework could not arm ConfirmFlow.** `_exec_force_resummarize` branch A returns the dry-run report WITHOUT `preview: True`, and `agent.py` sets `preview_pending` **only** on `result.get("preview") is True` — the sole ConfirmFlow arming path (`handlers.py:761` → `ConfirmFlow.awaiting_confirmation`). Prod logs confirm the absence: that turn has **no `fsm_confirm_armed` line**. So the LLM hand-authored the confirmation sentence, the user's «да» arrived with `current_state is None`, fell through to a stateless LLM turn, and produced the opaque fallback — bit-for-bit the BUG-046 mechanism. The `dry_run` parameter created a **second, preview-LESS shape inside a confirm-gated write tool**, which is precisely the structural hole BUG-046 closed. **(3) Latent third defect found while fixing:** `dry_run` was evaluated BEFORE `confirm`, so `dry_run=true, confirm=true` silently returned a report — a *confirmed* write becoming a no-op. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | `tests/test_f5c_bot_force_resummarize.py` (shipped with the slice) tested each branch in ISOLATION at the executor level — dry-run fields, preview fields, confirm outcome — and never asserted the **cross-branch FSM contract**: that the dry-run payload does not arm ConfirmFlow, and that a mutation *conversation* reaches an armed ConfirmFlow. No test drove `GeminiAgent.process_message` with the two-call shape at all, and the BUG-046 regression file (`test_bot_unsubscribe_confirm_gate_g1.py`) is unsubscribe-specific — nothing generalised «a write tool that returns no preview + an LLM-authored confirm = dead-end» into a reusable guard. Prompt-level rules were the only defense against the wrong arg choice, and `mode="AUTO"` temp-0.2 routing makes those probabilistic (the BUG-047 lesson, re-learned). |
| **Fix** | Three layers, deliberately ordered weakest → strongest. **(a) Prompt hardening** ([`prompts/bot.yaml`](../../prompts/bot.yaml) v1.9.2 → **v1.9.3**, all three version sites): a HARD RULE in § «Confirmation semantics» separating the two call shapes — `dry_run=true` ONLY on an explicit «что будет / покажи без запуска / dry-run» ask (terminal, read-only, arms nothing); a REAL re-summarize request MUST use `confirm=false` and OMIT `dry_run`; never author your own «Подтвердите … [да/нет]» (the framework owns confirmation); never pass `confirm=true` (BUG-009). The declaration's own `description` / `dry_run` description were rewritten too — the shipped «Set dry_run=true **first**» wording was actively misleading. **(b) Executor guard** (`_exec_force_resummarize`): `dry_run` + `confirm` together is now rejected with `error_class="InvalidArguments"` BEFORE either branch (kills the silent-no-op), and the dry-run payload carries machine-readable `terminal: True` / `mutation_requires_confirm_preview_turn: True` / `next_step` so its terminality is stated rather than inferred. **(c) Structural guard — the load-bearing one** ([`tg_parser/bot/agent.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/agent.py) `_recover_llm_authored_confirm`): the agent loop now records confirm-gated write calls that produced NO preview (`unpreviewed_write_calls`); if the turn ends with text that matches the narrow `_LLM_AUTHORED_CONFIRM_PATTERN` («Подтвердите …», «[да/нет]», «confirm», «[yes/no]») while nothing armed, the framework **deterministically re-issues the same tool in its preview shape** — `confirm` dropped (BUG-009: only the FSM sets it) and every `_PREVIEW_SUPPRESSING_ARGS` flag (`dry_run`) stripped — and arms ConfirmFlow from the resulting `{"preview": True, …}`, rendering the tool's own Russian preview verbatim. Same deterministic re-run pattern as `handlers._arm_delete_preview` / the clarify re-run paths. Fires ONLY on that exact state (write call + no preview + confirm-ask text), so read turns and correct preview turns are untouched; when no preview is obtainable it gives up and preserves the LLM text (no invented FSM state). **BUG-009 semantics unchanged.** **(c′) Detector precision — a high-severity defect INSIDE layer (c), caught by Bugbot review before commit.** The first cut of `_LLM_AUTHORED_CONFIRM_PATTERN` accepted a bare `\bconfirm\b`, and layer (b)'s own `next_step` hint tells the LLM to «call again with **confirm=false** … do NOT ask the user to **confirm** this report» — the one string the LLM is most likely to paraphrase. Echoing it made a LEGITIMATE read-only dry-run turn match, so the recovery replaced the requested report with a mutation preview and armed ConfirmFlow; a stray «да» would then have burned LLM tokens on a re-summarize the user never asked for — precisely the failure mode layer (c) was designed to avoid (and the reason `dry_run` was deliberately NOT given `preview: True`). Fixed by keying the detector on the STRUCTURE of an ask (`подтвердите` / `подтверждаете` / `[да/нет]` / `[yes/no]` / `please confirm` / `confirm?` / `do you confirm`) instead of the mere word; scrubbing argument literals (`confirm=…`, `dry_run=…`) via `_ARG_LITERAL_PATTERN` before matching (plumbing quoted at the user is never an ask); rewording `next_step` to avoid the bare verb (defense in depth); and funnelling the decision through the single production helper `_looks_like_llm_authored_confirm` so tests cannot re-implement the scrub and mask a regression. **Second precision pass** (same review loop): `подтвержда[еюя]\w*` also matched the FIRST-PERSON «Подтверждаю, что это только отчёт» and the gerund «Подтверждая …» — declarative relay text, so only the second-person interrogative forms (`подтверждаете` / `подтверждаешь`) are kept; and an explicit «no confirmation pending» disclaimer (`_CONFIRMATION_DISCLAIMED_PATTERN`) now **vetoes** the whole detector, which keeps «[да/нет]» — the prod signature and the single strongest ask marker — usable instead of having to weaken it. The governing asymmetry, recorded so future passes do not re-widen it: a missed ask costs the user one rephrase, a false positive silently replaces a requested read-only report with a mutation preview and lets a stray «да» spend LLM tokens ⇒ **precision is preferred over recall**. |
| **Layer (d) — read-only-intent classification, SHADOW MODE (log-only, deliberate)** | The natural next precision layer is to VETO the recovery when the USER's own message asked for a read-only report («что будет, если …», «только покажи», «без запуска», «dry-run», «what would happen», «preview only»). It is **built but not wired to behaviour**: `_READ_ONLY_REQUEST_PATTERN` + `_MUTATION_IMPERATIVE_PATTERN` → `_looks_like_read_only_request` ([`agent.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/agent.py)) feed a single boolean field `read_only_intent=` on the guard's existing `llm_authored_confirm_detected` / `llm_authored_confirm_recovered` records and **nothing else** — control flow is bit-for-bit what it was without them. Rationale: the FP class this would veto has so far been observed only in REVIEW, never in prod, so a keyword list written today is tuned against imagined phrasings; shadow mode turns that guess into a measurement. **Evidence that justifies flipping it to enforcing:** any `llm_authored_confirm_recovered` record with `read_only_intent=True` — the guard armed a mutation preview for a user who asked for a report. Flipping is monotone-safe: a veto can only SUPPRESS an arming, never create one, so a phrasing the classifier misses behaves exactly as today. **Only ANCHORED multi-word phrases** — a bare «покажи» is forbidden because «пере-суммаризируй тему X и покажи, что получилось» is a MUTATION request, and an enforcing version keyed on the bare verb would re-open this very dead-end; an explicit mutation imperative (`пере-суммаризиру(й\|йте)`, morphologically distinguished from the infinitive `-ть` of the legitimate «…если пере-суммаризировать X») vetoes the read-only verdict for the same reason. **PRIVACY:** the boolean ONLY — the user's message text is never logged, not even truncated (same norm as the argument-KEYS-only logging next to it: `add_user_auth` args carry a raw credential, and a user message can quote one just as easily). Watch field documented in [`../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md) § «BUG-086 — bot confirm-recovery guard» (replaced by § «#359 / ADR-0020 — deterministic confirm trigger», which records why this field is gone rather than documenting it). |
| **Fourth precision pass — the FOURTH detector false-positive vector, FIXED (2026-07-25, own red→green slice)** | `подтвердит[еь]` conflated the second-person imperative «подтвердите» with the **INFINITIVE** «подтвердить» — the same morphology conflation the second precision pass removed from `подтвержда…`, one alternative over. A legitimate read-only turn whose text paraphrases the payload's own `next_step` («Это только отчёт. Чтобы **подтвердить** реальный запуск, попросите меня ещё раз») was read as a self-authored ask ⇒ report replaced by a mutation preview, ConfirmFlow armed. The disclaimer veto does not save it: `next_step`'s «no confirmation is pending» clause is exactly the part a Russian paraphrase drops. Found while building layer (d) and deliberately left open there (narrowing the alternative CHANGES CONTROL FLOW, which the shadow-mode slice forbids by construction). **Fix:** the alternative is now `подтвердите\b\|подтверди\b\|подтвердить[^?.!\n]{0,40}\?` — the imperative forms are an ask by grammatical FORM (the informal `подтверди` is added deliberately: no FP risk, closes a small recall gap), while the infinitive counts ONLY when it heads an interrogative clause («Подтвердить пере-суммаризацию?»), the `[^?.!\n]` class stopping the match at a sentence boundary so a declarative infinitive followed by an unrelated question does not match. Verified through the COMPOSED production helper (scrub + veto + pattern), not the alternative in isolation: **7** `next_step`-paraphrase report texts flip `True`→`False`, **6** ask texts (3 imperative, 3 interrogative-infinitive) stay/become `True`, and `_PROD_SELF_AUTHORED_CONFIRM` is still detected. **Running lesson, now the dominant one:** three of this detector's four FP vectors were MORPHOLOGICAL (person — «подтверждаю»; finiteness — the gerund «подтверждая»; mood/finiteness — the infinitive «подтвердить»), only the first was lexical (bare `confirm`). A Russian verb alternative in a text detector must therefore be enumerated by FORM, and every `\w*` / `[..]` tail audited for which mood, person or finiteness it silently admits. |
| **Fifth precision pass — clause boundaries; the LAST regex pass on this detector (2026-07-25, own red→green slice)** | The fourth pass let the infinitive count only when it heads an INTERROGATIVE clause, but its window `[^?.!\n]{0,40}` stops at a SENTENCE boundary only — **not at a clause boundary** — so a declarative infinitive followed by a short unrelated question was still stitched into one interrogative clause: «Нужно подтвердить запуск — показать ещё раз?» and its `,` / `:` / `;` variants all matched, re-opening the same FP the fourth pass closed. **Fix:** the window now also ends at a clause separator, but only where the separator ACTS as one. A plain exclusion class (`[^?.!\n,;:—–-]`) was **rejected** — it kills two of the six pinned asks, the intra-word hyphen of «Подтвердить пере-суммаризацию?» and the colons of «Подтвердить запуск для темы topic:tg:c1:post:1?». The tempered form `подтвердить(?:(?![?.!\n])(?![,;:]\s)(?!\s[-–—])(?![-–—]\s).){0,40}\?` counts `,;:` only before whitespace and a dash only when spaced, covering all three dashes Russian text uses (`-`, `–`, `—`). **Accepted FALSE NEGATIVE — recorded, not hidden:** excluding the clause comma also drops the genuine «Подтвердить, пожалуйста, запуск?». Under the governing asymmetry that trade is correct (a missed ask = one rephrase; the alternative = an unrequested mutation preview a stray «да» pays LLM tokens for) and it is the owner's decision, so it is pinned by a dedicated test whose NAME and docstring state it is deliberate — a future reader must not "fix" it and silently re-open the FP. Verified through the COMPOSED production helper: the six new texts → `False`; the fourth pass's **7** report paraphrases still `False` and **6** asks still `True`; `_PROD_SELF_AUTHORED_CONFIRM` still detected. Mutation-verified: reverting the window to `[^?.!\n]{0,40}` fails **exactly** the two new tests (`4050 passed` otherwise unchanged). **Last regex pass by owner decision** — see the deferred-follow-up row below. |
| **Production e2e verification — the original failing scenario, re-run in prod (2026-07-26, owner manual smoke in `@Tgingest_bot`) — PASS** | The exact BUG-086 trace plus a negative control, all five steps green; timings from `docker logs tg_parser_bot` (log timestamps are authoritative, ~12 s later than the client-side ones). **(1) Dry-run stays terminal.** «покажи, что будет, если пере-суммаризировать тему `topic:tg:Docma_ru:post:252`» → `07:50:55.232` `agent_tool_call force_resummarize args={"dry_run": true, "topic_id": "topic:tg:Docma_ru:post:252"}` → report «текущая версия 8, новых элементов 0, элементов в бандле 197. LLM не вызывался, версия не записывалась.», **no `fsm_confirm_armed`**, no self-authored confirmation. **(2) The mutation request now uses the RIGHT call shape.** «пере-суммаризируй тему `topic:tg:Docma_ru:post:252`» → `07:51:32.847` `agent_tool_call force_resummarize args={"topic_id": "topic:tg:Docma_ru:post:252", "confirm": false}` → `07:51:33.732` **`fsm_confirm_armed`**, and the user saw the framework's own preview («…вызов LLM (расход токенов), будет записана новая версия сводки. Подтвердите [да/нет].»). **(3) «да» commits.** `07:51:44.179` `fsm_confirm_execute args={…, "confirm": true}` → `resummarize.yaml` loaded → Anthropic `claude-sonnet-4-6` 4778 in / 571 out at `07:51:57.411` → `topic_embedding_complete Docma_ru` at `07:51:59.277`; turn 15158 ms; bot replied «✅ force_resummarize: `topic:tg:Docma_ru:post:252` — ok.». **(4) Version advanced 8 → 9** — `get_topic_versions` at `07:52:40` → 9 versions, last summarized `2026-07-26 07:51:57Z`. **(5) Negative control clean.** `07:56:09.887` `force_resummarize {"topic_id": "topic:tg:mediamedics:post:2954", "confirm": false}` → `07:56:10.718` `fsm_confirm_armed` (preview: version 9, 3 new items) → «нет» → «❌ Отменено.», turn `e161cc42` completed in **46 ms** with no LLM call and no `fsm_confirm_execute`; `get_topic_versions` at `07:56:40` → still **9** versions, `last_summarized_at` still `2026-07-21T09:37:18Z`, bit-for-bit the pre-test baseline. No stuck FSM state. **0 errors / warnings / tracebacks** in 07:40–08:05 UTC across `tg_parser_bot`, `tg_parser`, `tg_parser_mcp`. **🔑 The structural guard (c) never fired.** Zero `llm_authored_confirm_detected` / `_recovered` / `_recovery_failed` records over the whole container lifetime (`StartedAt 2026-07-26T07:04:53Z`). Layer **(a) — prompt hardening — produced the correct `confirm=false` call on its own**; layer (c) remains untested-in-prod belt-and-braces (CI-covered, incl. the tool-agnostic case). Deploy record with the full log excerpt: [`F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md) § Deploy record — BUG-086. |
| **Shadow-mode observability GAP found by that verification (2026-07-26) — layer (d) cannot measure its own false-positive rate** | The e2e run produced exactly the two turns layer (d)'s classifier was written for — a genuine read-only ask («покажи, что будет, если пере-суммаризировать …») and a genuine mutation imperative («пере-суммаризируй …») — and **logged a verdict for neither**: `read_only_intent` does not appear in the logs at all. Cause is structural, not sampling: `read_only_intent = _looks_like_read_only_request(user_message)` is computed **inside** `_recover_llm_authored_confirm`, i.e. **after** the `_looks_like_llm_authored_confirm` gate, so the boolean is only ever emitted on turns where the guard ALREADY fired. On the happy path — the correct `confirm=false` → real preview flow, which after layer (a) is the overwhelming majority of traffic — the classifier is silent **by construction**. ⇒ the watch window measures the classifier's behaviour only on the population where it is least needed, and its false-positive rate on quiet turns is **unmeasurable no matter how long the window runs**. The «check the denominator first» caveat already recorded in the runbook turns out to be a ceiling, not a warm-up. **Proposed fix (routed to [issue #359](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/issues/359), not applied here):** compute the verdict **before** the detector gate and log it on every turn that made a confirm-gated write call, whether or not the guard fired — still the BOOLEAN only, so the privacy norm (never log the user's message text) is unchanged. Without that, «flip layer (d) to enforcing?» can never be decided on production evidence. |
| **Follow-up (deferred, owner decision 2026-07-25) — ✅ CLOSED 2026-07-31 by the «Architectural replacement» row below (#359 / ADR-0020 landed; the detector and both remaining FP vectors are gone, not narrowed).** The two REMAINING false-positive vectors get an ARCHITECTURAL replacement, not a sixth regex pass. Tracked as [issue #359](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/issues/359) (filed 2026-07-26). Plan: [`START_PROMPT_SESSION_BOT_AFFIRMATIVE_CONFIRM_TRIGGER_2026-07-31.md`](START_PROMPT_SESSION_BOT_AFFIRMATIVE_CONFIRM_TRIGGER_2026-07-31.md). The «keep or drop `dry_run` in the bot declaration» question it carried is **CLOSED (owner, 2026-07-31): `dry_run` STAYS** — dropping it would not remove the need for the recovery mechanism (a preview-less turn stays reachable via the BUG-009 rejection path) and would empty `_PREVIEW_SUPPRESSING_ARGS`, making a live class-wide tripwire vacuous.** | **Why stop tightening.** Six FP vectors across four review rounds, three of the four fixed ones morphological — the approach itself is the defect: predicting an ASK from the LLM's open-ended prose. The two that remain are structurally unreachable by regex. **(a) Word order.** `_CONFIRMATION_DISCLAIMED_PATTERN` is order-sensitive while Russian word order is free: «подтверждение не требуется» is vetoed, but «Ничего подтверждать не нужно …», «Подтверждать этот отчёт не требуется …» and «Подтверждения от вас не требуется …» are not, and each gap restores a FP on the `[да/нет]` marker. That matters because the veto is precisely what makes it safe to KEEP that marker — the strongest and the only prod-observed one. **(b) Third-party text.** The detector reads the turn's FINAL TEXT, which can contain text relayed by tools: a quoted Telegram post or topic title containing «Подтвердите … [да/нет]» is detected, so a turn that both makes a preview-less confirm-gated write call AND quotes knowledge-base content can arm a preview off text **nobody authored as an ask**. **Replacement design.** Stop predicting from prose; react to the USER's deterministic reply. Persist a small snapshot when a turn calls a confirm-gated write tool that produced no preview; on the NEXT message, if it classifies as an affirmative token, re-issue that tool in its preview shape and arm `ConfirmFlow` then. The trigger becomes a CLOSED vocabulary of ~a dozen tokens this codebase already classifies reliably (`classify_confirmation_token` / `AFFIRMATIVE_TOKENS`, [`tg_parser/bot/handlers.py`](../../tg_parser/bot/handlers.py), hardened since **BUG-032**) instead of unbounded prose — which removes the morphology class entirely and closes the third-party-text channel with it. **Direct precedent for the shape:** `_handle_delete_intent_router` / `_handle_subscribe_intent_router` already persist an intent snapshot and deterministically resume it on the following message (**BUG-048 Part A** for `delete_intent`, **BUG-050** for `subscribe_intent` — corrected 2026-07-31 against the code; the earlier «BUG-047 / BUG-031» attribution here and in #359 was WRONG and would send an implementer to the wrong precedent: BUG-047 is the delete **pre-router**, which resolves the target inside the SAME turn and therefore has no persisted snapshot at all, and BUG-031 is the subscribe two-phase gate). **Cost:** in the degraded path (LLM chose the wrong call shape) the user confirms TWICE — «да» surfaces the real preview, a second «да» commits; the happy path (`confirm=false`) keeps a single confirmation. Same double-confirm shape the BUG-047 `delete_suggest` clarify already ships. **Expected benefit:** `_LLM_AUTHORED_CONFIRM_PATTERN`, `_CONFIRMATION_DISCLAIMED_PATTERN`, `_ARG_LITERAL_PATTERN` and all four precision passes can likely be deleted outright. **Data source for prioritising it:** the shadow-mode `read_only_intent` field added in layer (d) — a watch window with zero `llm_authored_confirm_detected` records says the whole detector never fired in prod, which is itself the argument for replacing it rather than growing it (watch procedure in [`../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/F5C_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md) § «BUG-086 — bot confirm-recovery guard», replaced by § «#359 / ADR-0020 — deterministic confirm trigger»). **First window says exactly that (2026-07-26):** across the whole container lifetime the detector fired **zero** times — the owner's e2e mutation turn was routed correctly by prompt layer (a) alone, so all five precision passes guard a path production has not yet taken. That LOWERS the urgency of a sixth regex pass and RAISES the case for the architectural replacement, since a deterministic affirmative-token trigger would not need the detector at all. Two things #359 should absorb from that window: the **observability gap** in the row above (the shadow verdict is emitted only when the guard fires, so its FP rate is unmeasurable) and, secondarily, that the cancel path (`❌ Отменено.`) emits no structured event of its own — a rejected confirm is visible only as a bare short `request_completed`, which makes «did the user decline or did the flow break?» unanswerable from logs. |

| **Architectural replacement (2026-07-31) — #359 / ADR-0020 landed: the prose detector is GONE, the trigger is now the user's own affirmative token** | Layers (c) and (d) are deleted outright — `_recover_llm_authored_confirm`, `_looks_like_llm_authored_confirm`, `_looks_like_read_only_request`, the five regexes (`_LLM_AUTHORED_CONFIRM_PATTERN`, `_CONFIRMATION_DISCLAIMED_PATTERN`, `_ARG_LITERAL_PATTERN`, `_READ_ONLY_REQUEST_PATTERN`, `_MUTATION_IMPERATIVE_PATTERN`) and the whole shadow layer with its three `llm_authored_confirm_*` events and the `read_only_intent` verdict. **Nothing reads the turn's prose any more**, so the entire morphological FP class (person, finiteness, mood, clause boundaries) and both structurally-unreachable vectors (free word order in the veto, a `[да/нет]` quoted from the knowledge base) cease to exist rather than being approximated by a sixth pass. Replacement: a preview-less confirm-gated write call leaves a **snapshot** (`AgentResult.write_intent_pending` → `pending_write_intent`, args sanitized at creation — `confirm` + `_PREVIEW_SUPPRESSING_ARGS` stripped, so the mutating shape cannot be reconstructed from FSM storage), and the trigger becomes the user's NEXT message classified against a **closed** vocabulary. Only a **bare** token fires it (the whole normalized form, trailing `,.;:!?` stripped — «да.» is the same bare answer as «да» and no whitelisted token contains punctuation) — a deliberate divergence from `_handle_confirmation_response`, which also accepts the first token of a compound: on a ConfirmFlow turn the framework itself printed «Подтвердите [да/нет]», here the previous turn may have been an HONEST report, so «да, покажи темы канала X» must NOT show a mutation preview and silently drop the request. Adjacency is **structural**, not a list of clear-sites: the snapshot is popped at the very top of `handle_text` and carried as a local, so it cannot survive a message down any path (state gates, the three pre-routers, the agent) and a «да» can never resume a write call from two turns ago. `write_intent_router_resume` **never** mutates — it obtains the real preview and arms ConfirmFlow, so the mutation still needs the user's second «да» (BUG-009 / BUG-046 gate bit-for-bit; the re-issue carries no `confirm`). Authorization is re-checked on the resume turn by the executor itself (the snapshot carries no identity and no role), and `current_user is None` is load-bearing rather than defensive — the executors fall back to `user = current_user or await get_default_admin()`. Observability: `write_intent_set` / `write_intent_router_resume` / `write_intent_router_failed` / `write_intent_router_execute_failed` / `write_intent_declined` / `write_intent_dropped` (`reason` = `fsm_armed` / `unrelated` / `ttl`), plus `fsm_confirm_declined`, which closes the separate #359 § 3 gap where the negative branch of `_handle_confirmation_response` logged **nothing** and «the user cancelled» was indistinguishable from «the flow broke». TTL = `PENDING_TTL_SECONDS` (5 min, the confirmation window — not the 15-min intent window) via the fail-**safe** `_is_stale`, deliberately not `_is_pending_expired`, which treats a missing / unparseable `created_at` as «not expired» and would fail **open** on a path that arms a mutation preview. `prompts/bot.yaml` 1.9.3 → **1.9.4** (the hard rule now tells the model the framework reacts to the user's bare «да» directly). **Mutation-verified: all 12 rows of the plan's §3.9 table killed tests**, plus **five** rows added across three review rounds (harness: `scripts/mutation_verify_359.py`, blast radius = the 42 test modules importing the bot adapter). Each review-added pin closed a real defect in this slice. **(1)** The pop sat BELOW `handle_text`'s blank-text guard, so a whitespace-only message (which `F.text` admits and which returns before any router) let the snapshot outlive it. **(2)** The resume armed `ConfirmFlow` without `_clear_subscribe_intent`, unlike the agent-preview arm site it mirrors — reachable because one turn can set both detectors and the confirm-execute path deliberately RESTORES `subscribe_intent` for any non-subscribe tool, so a stale intent outlived the whole double-confirm and would misroute a later bare channel name. **(3)** The same resume omitted `_last_subscription_from_preview` (BUG-047 B-2); the two arm sites are now equivalent across all five of their actions. **(4)** A punctuated bare token («да.», «нет!») failed the whole-form match and was dropped as `unrelated`, dead-ending the user on the very turn the mechanism rescues, while the ConfirmFlow classifier accepted the same reply — trailing `,.;:!?` is now stripped, which cannot admit a compound because what makes one dangerous is the content AFTER the separator. **(5)** The `MAX_AGENT_TURNS` exhaustion exit dropped the snapshot (see the row above). Of two further review findings one was rejected and one fixed. **Rejected:** the snapshot storing a raw `add_user_auth` credential in FSM is a property of the confirm protocol itself (the normal preview turn writes the same args to `pending_action`, in the same in-process `MemoryStorage`, for the same 5 min), not a regression — the review's premise that the old recovery path never held secrets is wrong, since it re-issued that same call from `unpreviewed_write_calls`. Investigating it did surface a real and much larger pre-existing exposure, filed as **BUG-087**: `agent_tool_call` logs every tool's `args` unredacted at INFO, so the raw credential reaches the log pipeline on every `add_user_auth` — disk, not RAM. **Fixed (round-3 review):** the `MAX_AGENT_TURNS` exhaustion exit propagated `preview_pending` but not `write_intent_pending`. Parity with the old guard (which likewise only ran in the text-only branch) made it a non-regression, but not correct: running out of turns leaves the user with «переформулируйте» after a preview-less write call — the same dead-end this mechanism exists to close — and the two returns of the same function disagreed. Both now go through one helper, `_write_intent_or_none`, so they cannot drift apart again; pinned by `test_turn_limit_exhaustion_still_hands_over_the_snapshot` and mutation-verified. Three rows kill more than the row's own prose claimed, each legitimately: «set-site as an independent `if`» also kills BUG-050's `test_subscribe_create_with_preview_does_not_set_intent` (the chain structure is pinned from both sides); «stop stripping `dry_run`» kills 22, because the whole `TestFinalTextNeverArmsConfirmFlow` corpus asserts the snapshot's exact shape; «bring the detector back ALONGSIDE the router» kills 5, which is the point — it is the pin against a phased rollout where **two** mechanisms could arm the same preview. |

| **Production e2e verification of the replacement (2026-07-31, owner manual smoke in `@Tgingest_bot`, log window 19:28:13 → 19:35:43 UTC) — 3 of 4 scenarios PASS; the compound-affirmative invariant was NOT exercised, so this is NOT a complete e2e — ✅ both gaps closed by the second run, row below** | Timings from `docker logs --timestamps tg_parser_bot` and they are the authoritative ones — the owner's Telegram client renders UTC+3 (22:28–22:35 local). **(1) The degraded double-confirm path — the main scenario — PASS, and the only mutation of the whole run.** The mutation request went out in the dry-run shape: `19:28:13` `user_message` → `19:28:14.731` `agent_tool_call force_resummarize` → `19:28:15.902` `write_intent_set arg_keys=["topic_id"]`; the reply was the report «текущая версия 3, новых элементов 0, элементов в бандле 9» with **no** confirmation ask and **no** `fsm_confirm_armed`. A second «да» → `19:30:39.297` `fsm_confirm_execute` → «✅ force_resummarize: `topic:tg:mediamedics:post:1239` — ok.», `last_summarized_at` landing at `19:30:50.453171+00`, i.e. ~11 s of real LLM work. **This is bit-for-bit the trace that used to dead-end on «Я не совсем понимаю ваш ответ»** (the BUG-086 / BUG-046 class). **(2) Punctuated bare token + the new cancel event — PASS.** `19:31:52` / `19:31:53.361` / `19:31:54.621` reproduce the same degraded entry on `topic:tg:AgeManagment:post:977` (report «версия 3, новых 0, бандл 14») → `write_intent_set`; the reply «**да.**», with a full stop, gave `19:32:11.578` `write_intent_router_resume` + `fsm_confirm_armed` — review-added pin **(4)** of the «Architectural replacement» row validated **on live prod code**, since before it a punctuated token was dropped as `unrelated` and fell through to the agent. «нет» on the preview → `19:32:31.421` **`fsm_confirm_declined`** + «❌ Отменено.» with no `fsm_confirm_execute`; that event is NEW in this slice — before #359 the cancel branch logged nothing at all and «the user declined» was indistinguishable from «the flow broke». **(3) Compound «да, …» — INCONCLUSIVE, recorded as NOT exercised.** The compound was sent at `19:32:57`, but by then **no snapshot was pending** — it had been popped at `19:32:11` by the resume and the ConfirmFlow was declined at `19:32:31` — so no `write_intent_dropped` fired and the message was simply served as an ordinary read (`19:32:58.812` `agent_tool_call list_topics`). ### BUG-085 (Critical — ingestion outage / observability) — F9 Phase-3 `TELEGRAM_SESSION_KEY` dropped from the `tg_parser` compose `environment:` allow-list → `SessionCryptoError` on every incremental tick → ~18h SILENT ingestion outage (scheduler tick stayed `status="success"`)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Critical** — full ingestion outage in prod for ~18h (**2026-07-16T19:52Z → 2026-07-17T13:41Z**). Every incremental tick failed ALL 13 sources (`succeeded=0, failed=13`) but the job returned normally, so nothing was ingested for the window AND no alert could fire (the tick stayed `status="success"`). Core-функционал prod-ingestion заблокирован — Critical по §Severity. Same OS-env-priority class as BUG-078. Fix `1fbc9b5` deployed & verified. |
| **Status** | `resolved` (2026-07-17) — **fixed, deployed & verified in prod**. Commit [`1fbc9b5`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/1fbc9b5) («fix(compose): pass TELEGRAM_SESSION_KEY into tg_parser scheduler») mirrored the key into the `tg_parser` env allow-list; prod force-recreated 2026-07-17T12:39:08Z (prod HEAD now `1fbc9b5`). **PREVENTION IMPLEMENTED** (2026-07-19): tech-debt B shipped in [`ca80dba`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/ca80dba) / [PR #331](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/331) — B1 metric + `IncrementalIngestionAllSourcesFailing` alert, B2 `SCHEDULER_CRITICAL_ENV` compose-parity guard (+ `SCHEDULER_DEFAULT_INTERVAL` mirrored). START_PROMPT: [`START_PROMPT_TECHDEBT_B_INGESTION_OBSERVABILITY_2026-07-19.md`](START_PROMPT_TECHDEBT_B_INGESTION_OBSERVABILITY_2026-07-19.md). **PREVENTION DEPLOYED & SMOKE-VERIFIED on prod (2026-07-19)** — `tg_parser` + `prometheus` force-recreated at prod HEAD [`4b499e4`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/4b499e4) (PR [#332](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/332)); B1 metric `tg_parser_incremental_pipeline_sources_total{outcome}` emitting live samples (succeeded/failed/degraded), alert `IncrementalIngestionAllSourcesFailing` loaded & inactive (health=ok). Nothing left pending. |
| **Component** | `ops` / `ingestion` / observability. Compose allow-list [`docker-compose.yml`](../../docker-compose.yml) `tg_parser` `environment:` block (`:48-132`; fixed key on `:116-122`); `unseal_session_for_use` ([`tg_parser/ingestion/telegram/session_crypto.py`](../../tg_parser/ingestion/telegram/session_crypto.py) `:81-102`, raises `SessionCryptoError` fail-closed when key empty + sealed `.enc` present); the connect-time unseal call ([`tg_parser/ingestion/telegram/telethon_client.py`](../../tg_parser/ingestion/telegram/telethon_client.py) `:211-214`); the scheduler ([`tg_parser/services/scheduler_service.py`](../../tg_parser/services/scheduler_service.py) `run_incremental_for_all_sources` + `incremental_pipeline_task` `:1417-1433`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-17 — during the Phase-1 watch recovery investigation (`docker inspect StartedAt` + log grep on prod); documented in [`PHASE1_WATCH_BASELINE_2026-07-15.md`](PHASE1_WATCH_BASELINE_2026-07-15.md) **Gap #6** (t2 re-snapshot section). |
| **Symptoms** | Every incremental tick logged `Incremental pipeline completed: succeeded=0, failed=13, degraded=0` (`scheduler_service.py:940-948`) and finished WITHOUT raising; each source failed with `SessionCryptoError` (encrypted `.session.enc` present but `TELEGRAM_SESSION_KEY` unset → fail-closed). No new data ingested for ~18h. The only exposed scheduler signal, `tg_parser_scheduler_tasks_total{status="success",task_name="incremental_pipeline"}`, kept incrementing `success` throughout — a green monitor over a dead pipeline. |
| **Root cause (verified, not hypothesis)** | F9 Phase-3 added Telethon session-at-rest encryption reading `TELEGRAM_SESSION_KEY` (Fernet). The key was added to prod `.env`, but the `tg_parser` service in `docker-compose.yml` enumerates env vars with an EXPLICIT allow-list (unlike `mcp`/`tg_bot`, which use `env_file: .env`), and `TELEGRAM_SESSION_KEY` was never mirrored into it. The scheduler singleton reads OS env at startup (pydantic-settings prioritises OS env over the bind-mounted `/app/.env` — the documented BUG-078 gotcha), so the worker saw `telegram_session_key=None`; on connect, `unseal_session_for_use` found the sealed `.enc` with no key and raised `SessionCryptoError` (`session_crypto.py:95-102`). Confirmed via `git show 1fbc9b5` (7 insertions, the key + BUG-078 comment) and the compose block. |
| **Why CI didn't catch (detection gap)** | Two blind spots. **(1) No observability:** `incremental_pipeline_task` deliberately does NOT call `record_scheduler_task` (comment `scheduler_service.py:1422-1423`), and the `BackgroundScheduler.add_task` wrapper marks `status="success"` whenever the job returns without raising; `run_incremental_for_all_sources` catches per-source errors and returns the aggregate dict normally — so an all-sources-failing tick is indistinguishable from a healthy one at the metric level. Per-source outcomes (`succeeded/failed/degraded`) live ONLY in the completion log line, not in any metric ⇒ no alert could fire. **(2) No env-parity guard:** no test asserts that scheduler-critical settings are mirrored into the `tg_parser` compose allow-list, so a key silently dropping out is invisible to CI. |
| **Fix** | Commit [`1fbc9b5`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/1fbc9b5): added `- TELEGRAM_SESSION_KEY=${TELEGRAM_SESSION_KEY:-}` (plus a BUG-078-gotcha comment) to the `tg_parser` `environment:` block (`docker-compose.yml:116-122`), mirroring it alongside the other scheduler-critical vars. Deployed to prod (force-recreate; StartedAt `2026-07-17T12:39:08Z`). |
| **Verified in prod (recovery)** | First healthy tick ≈`2026-07-17T13:41Z` after the restart. Post-fix soak (per `PHASE1_WATCH_BASELINE_2026-07-15.md` t2 re-snapshot, merged as [`1a2a9aa`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/1a2a9aa)): **0 `SessionCryptoError` over 72h**; incremental ticks back to `succeeded=6` (0 outage-ticks `succeeded=0`); `tg_channel_processed_coverage_ratio` restored / ≥ baseline for all **13** channels. **Gap #6** (the outage window / missing-key recovery) closed. |
| **Prevention / follow-up** | ✅ **Built** (2026-07-19) — [`ca80dba`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/ca80dba) / [PR #331](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/331); START_PROMPT [`START_PROMPT_TECHDEBT_B_INGESTION_OBSERVABILITY_2026-07-19.md`](START_PROMPT_TECHDEBT_B_INGESTION_OBSERVABILITY_2026-07-19.md). **B1** — Counter `tg_parser_incremental_pipeline_sources_total{outcome}` (`outcome ∈ {succeeded,failed,degraded,lock_contended,skipped}`; `failed` = HARD only = `sources_failed - sources_degraded`) emitted at the completion-log site + critical alert `IncrementalIngestionAllSourcesFailing` (`increase(failed[2h])>0 AND (increase(succeeded[2h]) or vector(0))==0`, `for:30m`; degraded excluded). **B2** — parameterized `SCHEDULER_CRITICAL_ENV` guard in [`tests/test_compose_env_propagation.py`](../../tests/test_compose_env_propagation.py) + `SCHEDULER_DEFAULT_INTERVAL=${SCHEDULER_DEFAULT_INTERVAL:-3600}` mirrored into the `tg_parser` compose allow-list (protects the alert's `[2h]` window math). ✅ **Deployed & smoke-verified on prod (2026-07-19)** — `tg_parser` + `prometheus` force-recreated at prod HEAD [`4b499e4`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/4b499e4); B1 metric now emits live `succeeded/failed/degraded` samples and the `IncrementalIngestionAllSourcesFailing` alert is loaded & inactive (health=ok). Nothing remaining. |

### BUG-083 (Low/Medium — F5-C re-summarize observability + waste) — Anthropic hard content-safety `stop_reason='refusal'` on a legitimate medical topic turns it into a poison-pill: re-summarize is refused every tick, burning one Sonnet call and pinning `tg_resummarize_total{outcome="llm_error"}`

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Low/Medium** (observability + minor spend). No data loss, self-noisy: one deterministic refusal on a single topic wastes ~1 `claude-sonnet-4-6` call per tick (~24/day) and pins the `ResummarizeLLMErrorRate` tripwire at a false-positive «outage». The valid prior summary (`summary_version=2`) is preserved. |
| **Status** | `resolved` (2026-07-10) — **fixed, deployed & verified in prod**. Commit `07355ab` (`fix(f5c): quarantine content-safety refusals in resummarize`) pushed to `main` and deployed to prod (HEAD `07355ab`, containers recreated 2026-07-10T08:18Z). bugbot + security-review clean. Refusal outcome + poison-pill cooldown + config-gated fallback (default off). Discovered during the S1–S3 post-deploy investigation. See «Verified in prod» row. |
| **Component** | `services/resummarization_service.py` (F5-C `resummarize_topic`), model `claude-sonnet-4-6` (`resummarize` stage). Manifesting topic `topic:tg:labdiagnostica_logical:comment:8992` («Диагностика аллергии на ботулотоксин»). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-09 — **live read-only probe** on prod (reconstructed the exact resummarize prompt and called Anthropic directly across input variants). |
| **Symptoms** | `tg_resummarize_total{outcome="llm_error",trigger="age",channel_id="labdiagnostica_logical"}` grows ~1 per tick (`increase[1h]≈1 … [24h]≈23`); `ok/age`≈0–1. Every tick logs `f5c_resummarize source=labdiagnostica_logical candidates=1 resummarized=0 skipped=1 tokens=0` followed by `f5c_resummarize_empty_llm_response` — **24** occurrences 2026-07-08T19:21Z→2026-07-09T18:20Z, **all the same topic**. |
| **Root cause (verified, not hypothesis)** | The live probe returned `stop_reason='refusal'`, `out_tok=1`, empty text for **every** input variant — `full` (summary+text), `summary`-only, AND `refs`-only (no comment text at all), deterministically (`temperature=0`, two identical runs). Anthropic's safety classifier hard-refuses on the topic terminology (title/scope/summary contain «ботулотоксин / токсин / лидокаин»), returning HTTP 200 with empty `content[]`. The code classified that empty body generically as `llm_error` and, since the refusal never commits a new summary, the **age-trigger re-selects the same topic every tick** → infinite retry. |
| **Not an S1 regression** | `refs`-only (the pre-S1 prompt shape, no document text) **also refuses** → the S1/F-02 document-text injection is NOT the trigger. Consistent with the S0 baseline already showing `llm_error/age=11` on this channel BEFORE the block. The content is entirely benign medical lab-diagnostics; this is a **model-side false-positive refusal**, not bad data. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | Refusal is live-model behaviour; unit tests mock the LLM. The empty-content branch existed (`test_empty_anthropic_content_returns_llm_error_without_raise`) but folded refusal into generic `llm_error` — there was no `stop_reason='refusal'` discrimination and no re-selection/backoff assertion. |
| **Proposed fix (prepared this session)** | (1) Detect `resp.stop_reason == 'refusal'` → distinct outcomes `refusal` / `refusal_cooldown` (NOT `llm_error`), so the LLM-health tripwire is not skewed. (2) **Poison-pill guard**: on refusal persist an escalating cooldown (`resummarize_refusal_until/count`) into `topic_cards.metadata_json` via new metadata-only `TopicCardRepo.set_resummarize_backoff` (**no migration**); skip the topic before the LLM call while in cooldown. (3) **Config-gated fallback** `resummarize_refusal_fallback_stage` (default `""`=off): retry once on a different-provider stage's model; a usable reply commits a normal `ok` and clears the markers. New settings `resummarize_refusal_backoff_s` (86400), `_backoff_max_s` (2592000), `_fallback_stage`. **System prompt deliberately NOT touched** (per owner: the project may later serve non-medical domains, so hard-coding domain-specific framing would be wrong). Tests: `tests/test_f5c_resummarization_service.py::TestRefusalPoisonPillGuard`. |
| **Workaround** | Operationally none — self-heals as noise. Before deploy, read `labdiagnostica_logical` resummarize `llm_error/age` as this refusal, not an LLM outage. |
| **Artifacts** | Probe (2026-07-09, temp=0): `[full] stop='refusal' out_tok=1 EMPTY=True`, `[summary] stop='refusal' EMPTY=True`, `[refs] stop='refusal' EMPTY=True`. Topic card: title «Диагностика аллергии на ботулотоксин», `summary_version=2`, `last_summarized_at=2026-06-20`. 24× `f5c_resummarize_empty_llm_response` all `topic:tg:labdiagnostica_logical:comment:8992`. |
| **Verified in prod (2026-07-10)** | Post-deploy watch (metrics reset at container recreate 08:18Z; counters below are since-restart). **First tick touching the poison-pill topic (09:20:37Z):** `tg_resummarize_total{channel_id="labdiagnostica_logical",outcome="refusal",trigger="age"}=1` (NOT `llm_error`), log `f5c_resummarize_refusal refusal_count=1 cooldown_until=2026-07-11T09:20:37Z` — 24h quarantine set. **Subsequent age-ticks:** `outcome="refusal_cooldown"` climbs (1→2→…→**6** by 15:42Z) i.e. the topic is skipped **before** the LLM call = **0 extra Sonnet calls**. Over ~7h: **exactly 1 refused call + 6 zero-cost skips**, and `outcome="llm_error"` for this channel **never appeared** (was ~1/tick ⇒ ~7 avoided). **No regression:** healthy channels resummarize `outcome="ok"` (`BiocodebySechenov`, `profendocrinologist`, `mediamedics`). `ResummarizeLLMErrorRate` no longer skewed by this topic. |
| **Update 2026-08-05 — minimal fallback experiment (C)** | One-shot CLI (no prod `.env` write, no re-create): cleared cooldown markers on `comment:8992`, then `docker exec -e RESUMMARIZE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK_STAGE=rag -e RAG_LLM_PROVIDER=openai -e RAG_LLM_MODEL=gpt-4.1 … topic resummarize`. **Result: cured.** Log `f5c_resummarize_fallback_ok stage=rag provider=openai model=gpt-4.1`; CLI `status: ok` `new_version: 3`; `metadata.resummarize_llm=openai/gpt-4.1`; refusal markers cleared; `last_summarized_at=2026-08-05T21:46:19Z`, `new_items_since_last_summary=0`. Prior summary preserved as `topic_card_versions` v2. Status stays `resolved` (original quarantine fix did not regress). Permanent scheduler fallback (D-4) **rejected** by owner — it would require a second chat-LLM vendor account, against the single-operator/self-host model; the knob stays an opt-in default-off option. **T7-gate hygiene (A) done in the same session:** `refusal_cooldown` excluded from both sides of `tg:resummarize_age_trigger:ratio14d`, the permanently-firing gate alert removed, and a compensating poison-pill signal added (`tg:resummarize_refusal_cooldown:count24h` + `ResummarizeRefusalCooldownPoisonPill`, info, >=12/24h per channel) so a future quarantined topic still reaches an operator on its own. Session note: [`SESSION_F5C_MINIMAL_FALLBACK_2026-08-05.md`](SESSION_F5C_MINIMAL_FALLBACK_2026-08-05.md). |
| **Linked** | **Corrects BUG-082** (the `labdiagnostica llm_error/age` attributed there to DB-pool is, in the post-pool-fix window, this refusal — see BUG-082 update 2026-07-09). BUG-081 (S1/F-02 resummarize text); S0 baseline (`S0_BASELINE_PROCESSING_METRICS_2026-07-07.md` — pre-deploy `llm_error/age=11`). Note: unrelated per-tick `failed=7/degraded=7` persists = structural BUG-082 (concurrency-budget + DB-error outcome classification), not this fix. |

### BUG-082 (Medium — reliability/observability) — DB connection-pool exhaustion (`QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached`) cascades a whole scheduler tick into `degraded` under per-source concurrency

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Medium** (reliability + observability). Transient, self-healing (idempotent retry next tick), **no data loss** (coverage actually rose post-deploy). But a single starvation spike fails multiple sources' stages in one tick and the resummarize path mislabels the DB error as `outcome="llm_error"`, so it corrupts health signals. Not on fire; a pool-sizing / concurrency-budget structural fix. |
| **Status** | **`resolved`** (2026-07-10) — branch `fix/bug082-db-pool-concurrency`. Fixes #1+#2+#3 from proposed fix; #4 (embeddings `429`) → **BUG-084** (separate item). Prod `.env` `DB_POOL_SIZE=10` override becomes redundant after merge (matches repo default). |
| **Component** | SQLAlchemy async DB connection pool. Effective prod config `DB_POOL_SIZE=5` + `DB_MAX_OVERFLOW=10` (= 15 max; from `.env`, not the compose `:-10` default). Simultaneous consumers observed starving it in one tick: `services/advisory_lock.py` (`channel_advisory_lock` → separate `engine.connect()`), `services/processing_service.py` (`run_processing`), `services/topicization_service.py` (`get_by_source_ref` in `_run_incremental_topicization_locked`), `services/background_scheduler.py` (topic auto-embedding), `services/resummarization_service.py` (`list_resummarize_candidates`), `processing/pipeline.py` (`failure_cooldown_load`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-08 — post-deploy metric watch of the S1–S3 remediation block (originally surfaced as `tg_resummarize_total{outcome="llm_error",trigger="age"}=7` on `labdiagnostica_logical`; log inspection showed the real error is DB pool, not LLM). |
| **Symptoms** | A single tick (`2026-07-07T23:16:40–41Z`) emitted **10** `sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00` events fanned across subsystems: `kdl_ru` processing failed at `channel_advisory_lock` (`engine.connect()`), `Lab4health` incremental topicization failed at `get_by_source_ref`, `AgeManagment` `bug077_resume_checkpoint_read_error`, topic auto-embedding failed, `failure_cooldown_load_failed`; affected sources logged `outcome=degraded`. The resummarize age-path counted its pool failures as `outcome="llm_error"` (metric mislabel). Same window also had **independent** OpenAI `429 Too Many Requests` on `/v1/embeddings` (a separate embedding rate-limit issue, NOT pool-related). |
| **Root cause (hypothesis)** | Peak per-tick concurrency transiently demands **> 15** pooled connections: processing runs at `concurrency=5` while, in the same tick, per-source topicization / auto-embedding / resummarize-candidate / advisory-lock paths each check out their own connection (advisory lock uses a **separate** `engine.connect()`). With `pool_size=5 + max_overflow=10` and a 30 s checkout timeout, a burst starves the pool and every late checkout raises `TimeoutError`. Fundamentally an under-sized pool relative to the concurrent per-source workload, not a logic bug. |
| **Pre-existing vs S1–S3 block** | **Assessed pre-existing**, not introduced by the block: (1) the S0 baseline (`S0_BASELINE_PROCESSING_METRICS_2026-07-07.md`, snapped BEFORE deploy) already recorded `tg_resummarize_total llm_error/age=11` on the **same** channel/trigger; (2) `DB_POOL_SIZE`/`DB_MAX_OVERFLOW` are unchanged by the block; (3) the block **net-reduces** DB query volume (S2 refs-only loads O(N²)→O(N); S3 batched `find_by_*`/`get_by_source_refs`; S1 one LLM client per tick). No mechanism was identified by which the block raises the peak *concurrent connection* count. **Caveat:** pre-deploy container logs rotated on recreate, so a block contribution cannot be excluded from post-deploy logs alone — this is a hypothesis backed by the S0 counter, not a proof. |
| **Impact** | Transient: affected sources retry next tick (pipeline is idempotent), and post-deploy coverage **improved** across all channels (no lost work). Two observability defects: (a) DB pool errors on the resummarize path are miscounted as `llm_error` (skews the F5-C LLM-health tripwire); (b) a pool spike shows as multiple unrelated `degraded` sources, obscuring the shared root cause. |
| **Proposed fix (not applied — future session)** | (1) Raise the pool budget for the prod workload — e.g. `DB_POOL_SIZE` 5→10 (+ revisit `DB_MAX_OVERFLOW`) in `.env`; cheap, no code/schema change, immediately relieves starvation. (2) Audit per-source parallelism vs pool size (cap concurrent per-source connection consumers, or give the advisory-lock path a tiny dedicated engine so lock acquisition can't be starved by the data pool). (3) Classify DB/pool `TimeoutError` on the resummarize path as its own outcome (e.g. `db_error`) instead of `llm_error` so the metric reflects reality. (4) Separately track the OpenAI embeddings `429` (embedding rate-limit backoff) — distinct from this pool issue. |
| **Workaround** | None required operationally — ticks self-heal. For calmer signals before the fix, treat `labdiagnostica_logical` resummarize `llm_error/age` and one-off `degraded` bursts as pool contention, cross-check against `QueuePool limit` log lines rather than assuming an LLM/billing fault. |
| **Artifacts** | Traceback tail: `sqlalchemy/pool/impl.py:167 … raise exc.TimeoutError → QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00`. Log events: `Incremental topicization failed for Lab4health`, `Source kdl_ru failed: Pipeline failed at processing stage`, `failure_cooldown_load_failed`, all `2026-07-07T23:16:40–41Z`. Post-deploy resummarize metric: `llm_error/age=7` (labdiagnostica), `ok/age=1` (Lab4health). |
| **Linked** | S0 baseline (`S0_BASELINE_PROCESSING_METRICS_2026-07-07.md` §2 обл.5 — pre-deploy `llm_error/age=11`); S1 (F-02, resummarize path); deploy runbook [`../runbooks/S1_S3_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/S1_S3_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md) § Tripwires T2/T4; `services/advisory_lock.py`. Separate co-occurring issue: OpenAI embeddings `429` (embedding backoff — own future item). |
| **Update 2026-07-09 — root-cause correction (see BUG-083)** | The `labdiagnostica_logical` `tg_resummarize_total{outcome="llm_error",trigger="age"}` counter originally cited here as evidence of DB-pool mislabelling is, in the post-deploy window, **NOT** a DB `TimeoutError` — a live probe proved it is an Anthropic hard `stop_reason='refusal'` on a benign medical topic (**BUG-083**). After the pool mitigation (`DB_POOL_SIZE 5→10`, applied 2026-07-08) `QueuePool limit` = **0 over 24h** while resummarize `llm_error/age` kept climbing ~1/tick — confirming the two are independent. The genuine DB-pool mislabel (proposed fix #3: classify DB `TimeoutError` as its own outcome, not `llm_error`) **still stands** for the actual starvation case, but this channel's steady counter is refusal, tracked in BUG-083. Pool-sizing mitigation holding; remaining BUG-082 work = structural concurrency-budget + DB-error outcome classification. |
| **Fix applied (2026-07-10, `fix/bug082-db-pool-concurrency`)** | **#1 durable pool:** repo default `db_pool_size` 5→10 (`.env.example` aligned; compose already `:-10`). **max_connections headroom:** 3 data pools × (10+10) + 1 lock pool × (6+4) = **70** vs compose `max_connections=200` → **130 spare**. **#2 structural:** dedicated `advisory_lock_engine` (`db_advisory_lock_pool_size=6`, `max_overflow=4`; sized for `scheduler_max_concurrent_sources × scheduler_max_instances + headroom`); `channel_pipeline_lock` + `channel_incremental_topicization_lock` checkout from lock pool, not processing data pool. **#3 observability:** resummarize path classifies `sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError` / `OperationalError` / `InterfaceError` as distinct `outcome="db_error"` (breakdown + Prometheus, single record via `_ResummarizeDbErrorRecorded` guard); `llm_error`/`refusal*`/`AnthropicBillingError` unchanged. **#4 deferred:** OpenAI embeddings `429` → BUG-084. |

### BUG-084 (Low/Medium — embedding rate-limit) — OpenAI `/v1/embeddings` `429 Too Many Requests` co-occurring with pool starvation (independent issue)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Low/Medium** (cost/reliability). Distinct from BUG-082 pool exhaustion — observed in the same tick window (`2026-07-07T23:16:40–41Z`) but root cause is embedding API rate-limit, not DB pool. |
| **Status** | **`resolved`** (2026-07-15) — deployed to prod at main HEAD `186b60e`; OpenAI embedding quota restored + post-deploy validation green (see Update 2026-07-15). Was `in-review` (2026-07-13) — code fix implemented + ЗК passed, committed to branch `fix/bug084-embedding-429-backoff` and PR opened against `main`. Was `open` (2026-07-10) — filed as out-of-scope for BUG-082 session. **Follow-up (was deferred — now ✅ resolved 2026-07-16 via PR [#318](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/318), merge `9ca0cc7`; see Update 2026-07-16):** MCP `search_knowledge_base` now surfaces `degraded` via an additive `SearchResults{result, degraded}` envelope. |
| **Component** | Topic auto-embedding path / OpenAI embeddings client (`services/background_scheduler.py`, embedding client). |
| **Symptoms** | HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` on `/v1/embeddings` during high-concurrency ticks; topic auto-embedding stage fails independently of `QueuePool` errors. |
| **Proposed fix (future session)** | Separate backoff/retry tracking for embedding rate-limits; optional dedicated rate-limiter or concurrency cap on embedding calls; distinct metric/log classification so embedding `429` is not conflated with DB pool or LLM processing errors. **Revised per 2026-07-12 diagnostic (see Update row):** retry logic MUST classify by `error.code` — back off only on transient `rate_limit_exceeded` (+5xx/overload), raise a distinct terminal exception immediately on `insufficient_quota` (no retry); RAG semantic→keyword fallback promoted to CORE; metric `outcome` split into `rate_limited` vs `quota_exhausted`. Full plan: [`START_PROMPT_BUG084_EMBEDDING_429_BACKOFF_2026-07-12.md`](START_PROMPT_BUG084_EMBEDDING_429_BACKOFF_2026-07-12.md). |
| **Linked** | BUG-082 (co-occurring in same tick, explicitly split); deploy runbook [`../runbooks/S1_S3_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md`](../runbooks/S1_S3_DEPLOY_AND_WATCH.md); S7/O-9b per-loop embedding client [`START_PROMPT_S7_TAIL_DISPOSITIONS_2026-07-12.md`](START_PROMPT_S7_TAIL_DISPOSITIONS_2026-07-12.md); FUTURE «Configurable Embedding Provider» ([`FUTURE_FEATURES.md`](FUTURE_FEATURES.md)); fix plan [`START_PROMPT_BUG084_EMBEDDING_429_BACKOFF_2026-07-12.md`](START_PROMPT_BUG084_EMBEDDING_429_BACKOFF_2026-07-12.md). |
