| **Update 2026-07-13 — tracked follow-up (deferred, Bugbot): MCP `search_knowledge_base` cannot expose `degraded`** — ✅ **RESOLVED 2026-07-16 (PR [#318](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/318), merge commit [`9ca0cc7`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/9ca0cc7); see Update 2026-07-16 below)** | Known limitation flagged by Bugbot on branch `fix/bug084-embedding-429-backoff`. The MCP tool `search_knowledge_base` (`tg_parser/mcp_server.py` `async def search_knowledge_base` ~L1131, return type `list[SearchResultItem]` ~L1138, body ~L1177–1189) returns a **bare `list[SearchResultItem]` with no query-level envelope**, so the `degraded` flag that `retrieval_service.search()` already computes (`SearchResults.degraded`) is **silently dropped** on this path (the `search(...)` call ~L1170 doesn't even read it). **Impact:** an MCP search client requesting `mode=semantic`/`hybrid` can silently get **keyword-only rankings on embedding failure with no degraded signal**. The functional **keyword-fallback mitigation is already in place** (only the *indicator* is missing, not the functionality). **Parity:** HTTP `/search`, HTTP `/ask`, and MCP `ask_question` **already expose `degraded`** (additive field) — the gap is confined to this one bare-list tool. **Proposed fix (BREAKING):** wrap the list in an envelope object carrying query-level `degraded` (e.g. `{results, degraded, query, total}`), which changes the tool's return shape and requires client + test migration — its **own API-design decision**, so **intentionally NOT done in this PR (user decision)**; documentation/tracking only. Full entry (deferred API-design): [`FUTURE_FEATURES.md`](FUTURE_FEATURES.md) «Configurable Embedding Provider» → follow-up «MCP `search_knowledge_base` не отдаёт `degraded`». |
| **Update 2026-07-12 — root-cause diagnostic** | Live prod probe confirmed the embeddings `429` is **terminal `insufficient_quota`**, NOT a transient rate-limit. **Evidence:** HTTP `429` with `error.type=insufficient_quota` / `error.code=insufficient_quota` (message "You exceeded your current quota…"), `x-request-id=req_7b8dc2fc9ac046159e1157fe4b6cd0dd`, and **NO** `x-ratelimit-*` / `retry-after` headers; the state persisted continuously ~2h (14:25–16:59 UTC) across all polls. **Live impact:** after the S7 deploy (O-9b) both the background topic/incremental embedding stage **and** the live semantic/hybrid RAG query path hard-fail on this `429` (`OpenAIEmbeddingClient.embed()` `embedding_service.py:56–65` has no retry/classification — `raise_for_status()` surfaces it raw). **Verdict:** retries are **futile** for `insufficient_quota` — this is a billing/quota state, not throttling; retrying only burns latency/attempts. **Split remediation:** (operator) billing/tier action — add credits / payment method / raise usage tier at `platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing` + `/settings/organization/limits` (code cannot restore embeddings without this); (code) retry-classify by `error.code` (retry transient `rate_limit_exceeded` + 5xx/overload only; terminal `insufficient_quota` → distinct exception, no retry) + semantic→keyword RAG fallback (CORE — only mitigation that keeps RAG usable during terminal quota) + distinct metric `tg_embedding_requests_total{outcome, stage}` with `outcome ∈ {ok, rate_limited, quota_exhausted, error}`. **OpenAI docs (2026):** `429` has two classes — transient `rate_limit_exceeded` (RPM/TPM/RPD; retry w/ backoff, honor `Retry-After`/`x-ratelimit-reset-*`) vs terminal `insufficient_quota` (exhausted credits/usage-cap; retry won't help); `Retry-After` is not guaranteed on every `429`; provider overload is `503`, not `429`. Status remains **`open`** — fix plan persisted in [`START_PROMPT_BUG084_EMBEDDING_429_BACKOFF_2026-07-12.md`](START_PROMPT_BUG084_EMBEDDING_429_BACKOFF_2026-07-12.md). |
| **Update 2026-07-16 — resolved (follow-up): MCP `search_knowledge_base` now exposes `degraded`** | The deferred Bugbot follow-up (see Update 2026-07-13) is **closed** via PR [#318](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/318) (`feat/mcp-search-degraded-envelope`, merge commit [`9ca0cc7`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/9ca0cc7); CI green — Test 3.12, Lint Documentation, Alembic guardrails/smoke, Docker Build, Dependency Lock Guard all pass). **Delivered design (NOT the originally-feared BREAKING return-shape migration):** an **additive envelope** `SearchResults { result: list[SearchResultItem], degraded: bool }` in [`tg_parser/mcp_server.py`](../../tg_parser/mcp_server.py) — `search_knowledge_base` now returns `SearchResults` instead of a bare list. **Key insight:** FastMCP already auto-wrapped a bare `list` into structured output `{"result": [...]}` (`_create_wrapped_model`), so the explicit model **preserves that exact `result` array key** and merely ADDS a sibling `degraded` (default `False`). Structured-output consumers are therefore **backward-compatible / additive**; only the unstructured `content` shape changed (model JSON dump vs array), acceptable for an MCP tool. This brings `search_knowledge_base` to **parity with HTTP `SearchResponse.degraded` and MCP `ask_question`'s `AnswerResultItem.degraded`**, so no versioned-tool / dual-return transitional period was needed. Tracking entry updated in [`FUTURE_FEATURES.md`](FUTURE_FEATURES.md) «Configurable Embedding Provider» → follow-up «MCP `search_knowledge_base` не отдаёт `degraded`» (marked ✅ DONE). |

### BUG-081 (Critical — F5-C re-summarize) — Re-summarize LLM never receives document text → summaries cannot be enriched (tokens burned each tick)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Critical** — the single Critical of the 2026-07-07 processing-algorithms code review ([`CODE_REVIEW_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_FABLE5_2026-07-07.md`](CODE_REVIEW_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_FABLE5_2026-07-07.md) — finding **F-02** §4 / A12, optimization **O-1** §5). Core F5-C (evolving topic summaries) feature is effectively a no-op that still spends tokens. |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** — remediation session **S1** merged (PR [#299](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/299) `fix/S1-resummarize-text`, fix commit [`415476d`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/415476d) «fix(resummarize): send document text to LLM (F-02) + one client per tick (O-9a)»; on `main`). Fix implemented + RED→GREEN tested (default + PR-standard `TEST_POSTGRES=1`). Start prompt: [`START_PROMPT_S1_RESUMMARIZE_TEXT_2026-07-07.md`](START_PROMPT_S1_RESUMMARIZE_TEXT_2026-07-07.md). |
| **Component** | `resummarization` / `llm` — `tg_parser/services/resummarization_service.py` (`resummarize_topic` `items_payload`), `prompts/resummarize.yaml`, `tg_parser/services/db_context.py` (`resummarization_repos`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-07 — Fable-5 code review of processing algorithms (F-02, Critical). |
| **Symptoms** | Re-summarize LLM prompt carried only `source_ref` / `role` / `score` / `justification` for each bundle item — never the document `summary` or `text_clean`. The prompt instructs "DO NOT invent claims not supported by the items" while providing no claims, so the model either rephrases the stale summary (wasted call) or hallucinates from keyword-ish justification strings. Up to ~10 calls × 4096 max_tokens per channel-tick, ≈1388 prompt-tokens/call at baseline (S0). |
| **Root cause** | `items_payload` (built in `resummarize_topic`) omitted document content; the batch loader `ProcessedDocumentRepo.get_by_source_refs` (which already selects `text_clean` + `summary`) was never called, and the repo was not wired into the service. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | The existing F5-C service tests seeded only cards + bundles (no `processed_documents` rows) and asserted on outcome status / version bookkeeping, never on the material composition of the user-prompt. No test asserted that a document fact reaches the LLM. |
| **Proposed fix (S1 — implemented)** | **O-1 (F-02):** batch-fetch window docs via the existing `get_by_source_refs([it.source_ref …])` (single query, not N+1); add each doc's `summary` + a `text_clean` snippet truncated to `RESUMMARIZE_ITEM_TEXT_MAX_CHARS` (500) per item (missing doc row → empty content, no crash); wire `SAProcessedDocumentRepo` through `resummarization_repos()` + `ResummarizationService.__init__` (all 6 tuple-unpack sites updated); correct `prompts/resummarize.yaml` header + system prompt to describe the new items composition and bump `metadata.version` 1.0.0→1.1.0. **Hardening — O-9a (part of F-11):** hoisted `resolve_llm_config` + `create_llm_client` out of `resummarize_topic` into `run_for_channel` — one LLM client per tick, created only after the candidate check and closed once in a `try/finally`; standalone `resummarize_topic` (MCP `force_resummarize`, CLI) keeps an in-place client via an optional `llm=(client, provider, model)` param. |
| **Workaround** | None — feature silently under-delivers; no operator action recovers it pre-fix. |
| **Artifacts** | RED test `tests/test_f5c_resummarization_service.py::TestItemsPayloadCarriesDocumentContent::test_document_summary_and_text_reach_user_prompt` (failed pre-fix: document text absent from prompt; green post-fix). Baseline ≈1388 prompt-tokens/call — S0 §2 обл.5; expected post-fix ≈+1.5–3.5K/call, well within the 50K/tick cap. |
| **Linked** | F-02 (Critical) / O-1 / F-11 O-9a — [`CODE_REVIEW_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_FABLE5_2026-07-07.md`](CODE_REVIEW_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_FABLE5_2026-07-07.md); remediation plan [`PLAN_REMEDIATION_SESSIONS_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_2026-07-07.md`](PLAN_REMEDIATION_SESSIONS_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_2026-07-07.md) §1 «S1». O-9b (retrieval client) is deferred to S7 — out of scope here. |

### Remediation series (code-review processing algorithms 2026-07-07) — S3 pre-LLM dedup + batched checks (F-01 / F-09)

Findings from [`CODE_REVIEW_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_FABLE5_2026-07-07.md`](CODE_REVIEW_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_FABLE5_2026-07-07.md), remediation session **S3** (main processing token-leak: exact reposts were paid for in full before being discarded post-LLM). Plan: [`PLAN_REMEDIATION_SESSIONS_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_2026-07-07.md`](PLAN_REMEDIATION_SESSIONS_PROCESSING_ALGORITHMS_2026-07-07.md) §1 «S3»; start prompt [`START_PROMPT_S3_PRE_LLM_DEDUP_2026-07-07.md`](START_PROMPT_S3_PRE_LLM_DEDUP_2026-07-07.md). Branch `fix/S3-pre-llm-dedup`. **No migrations, no `docs/contracts/**` changes** (WORKFLOW §7).

| Finding | Severity | Status | Fix (O-code) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-01** — exact dedup ran only AFTER the paid LLM call (`content_hash` is computed over the post-LLM `text_clean`), so every exact repost/forward within a channel burned a full ~2–4K-token processing call before being discarded | **High** (cost) | `addressed` (S3, pending merge) | **O-2** — `pipeline.py`: pre-LLM dedup by the RAW-text hash. `_process_single_message` now stashes `metadata['raw_content_hash']=compute_content_hash(message.text)` on every text doc; `process_message` (single) and `_process_batch_parallel` (Phase 1.5) check the raw hash BEFORE the LLM. On a hit the repost is materialised as a **new persisted mirror row** (own `source_ref`/`id`/`processed_at`; copied `text_clean`/`summary`/`topics`/`entities`/`language`/`content_hash`; provenance `metadata['dedup_of']`) — traceable, not a silent skip / `return existing` — and the LLM is not called. New `tg_dedup_pre_llm_hits_total` counter (distinct from the post-LLM `tg_dedup_duplicates_detected_total`). Post-LLM dedup kept (catches formatting variations). Honours `dedup_enabled` + `force`. |
| **F-09** — `_process_batch_parallel` Phase 1 called `processed_doc_repo.exists()` **per message** (up to ~300 round-trips/tick/channel) although the tick selection already applied `NOT EXISTS (processed_documents)`; `_filter_duplicates` called `find_by_content_hash` **per doc** (~N/chunk) | **Medium** (speed) | `addressed` (S3, pending merge) | **O-8** — `pipeline.py` + repo: Phase-1 `exists()` fan-out replaced by one batched `get_by_source_refs` (the `for msg` loop is kept — it still computes `cooldown_skipped_refs`; non-tick callers stay correct); `_filter_duplicates` now does one batched `find_by_content_hashes(channel_id, [hashes])` per chunk instead of N. Two new repo methods (`ports.py` + `SAProcessedDocumentRepo`): `find_by_content_hashes` (indexed `content_hash = ANY`) and `find_by_raw_content_hashes` (raw-hash lookup for O-2 cross-tick). |

**Design decision — cross-tick without a migration (start-prompt `<design_decision>`).** Implemented **both** offered paths: **path 2** (within-tick, on-the-fly, zero persistence — the default/SQLite-safe baseline) **and path 1** (cross-tick via the existing `metadata_json` TEXT column, `metadata_json::jsonb ->> 'raw_content_hash'`, PostgreSQL-specific). Path 1's lookup is an **unindexed per-channel scan** bounded by `processed_documents_channel_idx` on `channel_id` + a runtime `jsonb` cast; cost was judged acceptable (one batched query per tick/chunk, thousands of rows × cast ≈ sub-second, vs. saving a full LLM call) so no index/migration was added. **Escalation path 3 (indexed raw-hash column) was NOT taken** — if real-volume performance proves unacceptable it is a separate, agreed schema decision outside S3.

**Provenance decision.** The start-prompt corrected the plan's wording: the post-LLM branch does `return existing` and writes NO row, whereas S3's pre-LLM hit **creates a new mirror row** (so the repost is traceable and flows into `new_doc_refs`/topicization). `id = make_processed_document_id(source_ref)` (never copies the original `id` — would duplicate the PK). Pre-LLM hits are counted in `processed_count` (they produce a real row) but **excluded from `attempted_count`** (never sent to the LLM), so the scheduler's B1 degraded fail-ratio is unaffected; surfaced as `pre_llm_dedup_count` in process stats.

**Bugbot follow-up #3 (2026-07-07, medium, fixed pre-merge).** *«Invalid metadata_json aborts lookup»* — `find_by_raw_content_hashes` cast **every** non-null `metadata_json` in the channel scan to `jsonb` inside the `WHERE` clause (`metadata_json::jsonb ->> 'raw_content_hash'`). PostgreSQL evaluates that cast per row, so a single row with malformed JSON (empty string, truncated text, any non-JSON payload — e.g. a legacy/hand-edited row) would error the entire query, bubbling up through Phase 1.5 / single-message pre-LLM dedup and **failing the whole processing tick** for the channel whenever `dedup_enabled` is on — even though other paths read that row fine one-at-a-time via `stable_json_loads`. **Fix:** dropped the `jsonb` cast; the `WHERE` now uses a **total** `metadata_json LIKE ANY(:patterns)` prefilter (`patterns = ['%"raw_content_hash":"<hash>"%', …]`). This is safe because `metadata_json` is always written by `stable_json_dumps` (sort_keys + compact `separators=(",", ":")`) so the field serialises verbatim as `"raw_content_hash":"<hash>"`; hashes are SHA-256 hex (no `%`/`_` LIKE metachars) and the key literal rules out cross-key false positives. `LIKE` never errors on bad rows. The exact hash is re-verified in Python from each returned row's parsed metadata, so a LIKE over-match can't leak a wrong row. Regression test `test_find_by_raw_content_hashes_tolerates_malformed_metadata` (a sibling row with non-JSON `metadata_json` in the same channel scan → valid mirror still returned, no error).

**Bugbot follow-up #2 (2026-07-07, high, fixed pre-merge).** *«Within-tick repost stuck when leader filtered»* — a within-tick pre-LLM repost was mirrored ONLY from its leader's row in `persisted`. But the leader can be dropped later by post-LLM `_filter_duplicates` when its `content_hash` already exists on a **legacy DB row lacking `metadata['raw_content_hash']`** (so the cross-tick pre-LLM lookup misses it and the leader is sent to the LLM anyway). The repost was then counted as `_batch_pre_llm_deferred` **every tick, never persisted**, while the leader kept burning a full LLM call that was also discarded — a permanent stuck loop + recurring cost. **Fix:** `_filter_duplicates` now also returns `dropped_to_canonical` (dropped `source_ref` → the surviving in-batch/DB doc it collapsed into); `_persist_chunk` threads it up and `_process_batch_parallel` resolves each within-tick dup against `persisted_by_ref` **OR** `dropped_to_canonical`. The repost is mirrored against the canonical existing doc (carrying its own `raw_content_hash`), so the NEXT tick the leader itself resolves cross-tick (no more burn) — the loop self-heals in one tick. Only a leader that TRULY failed (no doc at all) still leaves its duplicate deferred. Regression test `test_within_tick_repost_mirrored_when_leader_dropped_post_llm` (legacy row without raw hash → leader dropped post-LLM, repost still mirrored with `dedup_of=<legacy>`, `_batch_pre_llm_deferred==0`, `llm.call_count==1`). Existing `_filter_duplicates` callers/tests updated for the new tuple return.

**Bugbot follow-up (2026-07-07, high, fixed pre-merge).** *«Pre-LLM dup inflates fail ratio»* — Phase 1.5 excludes within-tick exact reposts from `to_process` (never sent to the LLM), but if their **leader FAILS to persist** no mirror row is written and the repost falls through all buckets. `failed_count = total − processed − skipped` then miscounted each deferred repost as a failure while `attempted_count` (LLM-bound leaders only) excluded it, so the scheduler's B1 `fail_ratio = failed/attempted` could exceed 100 % and falsely mark a healthy repost-burst tick degraded. **Fix:** pipeline now surfaces `_batch_pre_llm_deferred = len(within_tick_dups) − mirrors_built`; `run_processing` folds it into `skipped_count` (both normal and `retry_failed` paths) and exposes `pre_llm_deferred_count` in stats — deferred reposts are retried next tick, never a failure. Regression test `test_within_tick_repost_deferred_when_leader_fails` (failing leader → `results==[]`, `_batch_pre_llm_deferred==1`, `_batch_pre_llm_dedup==0`, nothing persisted).

**Out of scope / deferred:** §6.4 (cheap model for short messages) remains a **separate later track**, gated on the new dedup metric. near-dup Phase 1 (ADR-0016) untouched; dedup stays **per-channel** (cross-channel not in F-01); `normalize_for_hash` used as-is; no Alembic revision, no `docs/contracts/**` change.

**Verification:** default suite (`pytest -q`) green incl. new `tests/test_s3_pre_llm_dedup.py` (within-tick, cross-tick via fake repo, raw-vs-clean layering, idempotency, `dedup_enabled=false`/`force`, O-8 batching spy, F-09 no-per-message-`exists()`); PR-standard (`TEST_POSTGRES=1`) green incl. the PG-specific `find_by_raw_content_hashes` JSON-cast SQL and the cross-tick end-to-end pipeline test (AC#1). ### BUG-081 (Low — test-only / stale fixture) — `test_batch_stats_degrades_to_zeros_on_aggregation_error` fails on clean `main` after the BUG-066 per-aggregate refactor (bare `AsyncMock` sibling repos leak un-awaited coroutines into the coverage arithmetic → `TypeError`)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|

Additive **coverage-aggregate** degrade-variant regression hardening added in PR [#317](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/pull/317) ([`a0f848d`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/a0f848d), test-only). Originally filed `open` (2026-07-07) during S2 (`fix/S2-perf-quickwins`) full-suite runs. |
| **Component** | `tests/test_mcp_management.py::TestGetAllChannelStats::test_batch_stats_degrades_to_zeros_on_aggregation_error` (`:645–679`); production code under test `tg_parser/services/channel_service.py` `get_all_channel_stats` (`:136–181`, BUG-066 per-aggregate `try/except`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-07 — S2 remediation session full-suite run (`3335 passed, 3 failed`; the other 2 were S2-owned scheduler-mock migrations, now fixed). This one is outside S2 scope (channel stats), so it was left and filed here. |
| **Symptoms** | `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'coroutine' and 'coroutine'` at `channel_service.py:168` (`covered / processed_count`). The captured log first shows the *expected* `RuntimeError: DB down` being caught + logged (`Channel raw-message count aggregation failed`), then the test blows up downstream. |
| **Root cause (verified — reproduced)** | The test's `error_ctx` stubs **only** `raw_repo.count_all_grouped_by_channel` to raise, and yields **bare `AsyncMock()`** for the sibling repos (`proc_repo`, `topic_card_repo`, `topic_link_repo`, …). It was written for the **pre-BUG-066** shape, where all four aggregates lived in ONE shared `try/except`, so the `raw` failure tripped the single `except` and every stat was zero-filled — the sibling mocks were never exercised. After BUG-066 split them into **per-aggregate** `try/except`, only `raw` degrades; `proc_repo.count_all_grouped_by_channel()` / `coverage_counts_by_channel()` now actually run. On a bare `AsyncMock`, `await proc_repo.count_all_grouped_by_channel()` returns a **child `AsyncMock`** (not a dict), and the subsequent `.get(cid, 0)` returns an **un-awaited coroutine**; the coverage arithmetic `covered / processed_count` then does `coroutine / coroutine` → `TypeError`. Repro: `AsyncMock().foo.return_value.get('x', 0)` is a coroutine. |

No guard asserts the fixture models the per-aggregate contract (one aggregate raises, the rest return **real dicts**). |
| **Proposed fix** | Test-only. Then assert the intended degradation: `raw_messages == 0` (the failed aggregate) while the others fall back cleanly to their `.get(cid, 0)` defaults and `coverage_percent == 0.0`. Optionally add a second case where the **coverage** aggregate is the one that raises, asserting raw/processed/topics keep their real values (mirrors the BUG-066 closure test suggestion). Do NOT touch `channel_service.py`. |
| **Workaround** | None needed operationally (prod path is correct). For a green local suite before this is fixed, the failure is a known-stale test — treat `channel_service`/`list_channels` changes with extra manual care until the fixture is repaired. |
| **Artifacts** | Repro: `.venv/bin/python -c "from unittest.mock import AsyncMock; print(type(AsyncMock().f.return_value.get('x',0)))"` → `<class 'coroutine'>`. Traceback tail: `channel_service.py:168 … TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'coroutine' and 'coroutine'`. |
| **Linked** | BUG-066 (the per-aggregate `try/except` refactor whose new shape the fixture never caught up to); BUG-008 (H1 — the batched grouped-aggregate rewrite this test originally guarded). |

### BUG-080 (Low/Medium — enhancement / reliability) — Switch topicization Anthropic generation to streaming so the httpx read timeout measures inter-chunk gaps (true stall-guard) instead of penalizing a slow-but-healthy full generation

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Low/Medium** (enhancement / reliability). Follow-up to **BUG-079**: the 150s per-attempt `anthropic_http_timeout_s` retune that resolved BUG-079 is a **correct-but-blunt** mitigation. Because topicization generation is **non-streaming**, the httpx read timeout measures *total time to the response headers* — which for a legitimate ~90s Sonnet generation is essentially the whole generation — so the timeout cannot distinguish a slow-but-healthy generation from a genuinely dead/stalled socket. The 150s value must be padded to the worst-case generation length, which weakens it as a stall-guard. This is not on fire (BUG-079 is resolved), so this is a structural improvement, not an incident. |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (2026-07-07) — the flag-gated streaming SSE path shipped (default OFF), deployed to prod FLAG-DARK + live-verified, then flipped ON and validated by a multi-chunk `murashko_med` drain with **ZERO** stalls. Streaming commit [`ec73dcf`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/ec73dcf) «fix(topicization): BUG-080 flag-gated Anthropic streaming SSE path (default OFF)»; deployed FLAG-DARK (worker boot echoed `anthropic_streaming_enabled=False`), then `.env` flipped `ANTHROPIC_STREAMING_ENABLED=true`, force-recreated, re-verified live. §5 fast-validation drain (2026-07-07) drove `murashko_med` chunks 4→5 with streaming ON and **0** `anthropic_network_error` / `LLMCallTimeoutError` / `AnthropicBillingError`. The prompt-caching no-op (⛔3) is explicitly NOT part of this win — it remains a separate open secondary finding. See **Update 2026-07-07 — RESOLVED** below. Was `open` (2026-07-06, filed as the BUG-079 long-term follow-up). `main`. |
| **Component** | `topicization` / `llm` — the `AnthropicClient` generation call (currently a non-streaming `messages.create`) and the per-attempt httpx read timeout (`anthropic_http_timeout_s`, now 150s post-BUG-079); the topicization batch generation path (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `max_tokens=8192`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-06 — during the BUG-079 root-cause reframe. The timed experiment proved non-streaming generations return headers only when the generation is essentially complete (TTFB≈total, ~87–90s), which is what forced the blunt 150s timeout. |
| **Symptoms** | None in prod (BUG-079 resolved). The latent limitation: a per-attempt read timeout on a non-streaming call cannot detect a mid-generation dead socket until the FULL worst-case generation window elapses; conversely, it must be sized to the slowest legitimate generation, so it can never be a tight stall-guard. |
| **Root cause** | Non-streaming Anthropic generation returns the HTTP response headers only once the model has essentially finished generating, so the httpx read timeout is a proxy for *total generation latency*, not *socket liveness*. There is no inter-chunk signal to time against. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | N/A — this is a design/enhancement item, not a defect. No test asserts stall-detection granularity because the current architecture cannot provide it. |
| **Proposed fix** | Switch topicization Anthropic generation to **streaming (`stream: true`)** so the httpx read timeout measures **inter-chunk gaps** (detecting a genuinely dead/stalled socket) instead of penalizing a slow-but-healthy full generation. This is the **structural** fix that BUG-079's 150s timeout only mitigates bluntly — with streaming, the per-attempt read timeout can be small again (e.g. back toward tens of seconds) as a TRUE stall-guard, because a healthy generation keeps emitting chunks well within any small inter-chunk window. **Minor secondary finding (not urgent):** the ~450-token topicization system prompt is BELOW Anthropic's 1024-token prompt-caching minimum, so the `prompt-caching` header is currently a **no-op** — a possible small optimization (e.g. batching more static context into the cached prefix, or dropping the header) but low value. |
| **Workaround** | None needed — BUG-079's 150/420 retune already makes topicization reliable (zero stalls in the airtight 3-chunk validation). This entry is the long-term structural improvement over that blunt mitigation. |
| **Artifacts** | BUG-079 Update 2026-07-06 (the timed experiment: 3 samples 89.09s / 89.59s / 87.06s, TTFB≈total, non-streaming; corrective retune commit `57d1bce`). |
| **Linked** | BUG-079 (origin — the network-stall reframe whose 150s timeout this streaming fix would let shrink back to a tight true stall-guard); BUG-068 (the adjacent Anthropic network-stall / no-effective-timeout class). |
| **Update 2026-07-07 — RESOLVED (flag-gated streaming shipped + deployed FLAG-DARK + live-verified + flipped ON + multi-chunk zero-stall drain)** | The structural streaming fix is **shipped, deployed, live-verified, and validated**. **CODE (commit [`ec73dcf`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/ec73dcf)):** a flag-gated streaming (`stream: true`) SSE code path in `AnthropicClient`, default **OFF** (`anthropic_streaming_enabled=False`) so processing/RAG/digest/resummarize keep the proven non-streaming path. The streamed path parses the `text/event-stream` (`message_start` input tokens → `content_block_delta` text → final `message_delta` cumulative output tokens + `stop_reason` → `message_stop`) and returns the IDENTICAL `LLMResponse(text, input_tokens, output_tokens, stop_reason)` contract, so token accounting / rate-limiter reconcile / truncation-detection are unregressed; the flag is mirrored into the `docker-compose.yml` `tg_parser` `environment:` allow-list (BUG-078 trap) and echoed at boot (`tg_parser/api/main.py`). **DEPLOY + LIVE-VERIFY (BUG-078 discipline):** deployed to prod **FLAG-DARK first** — the running worker echoed `anthropic_streaming_enabled=False` at boot (trusted the worker's own boot echo, NOT `docker compose exec … python -c`), confirming no regression on the non-streaming path; then prod `.env` flipped `ANTHROPIC_STREAMING_ENABLED=true`, force-recreated, and re-verified live ON. **FOLLOW-UP FIXES (same streaming session, hardening the SSE path):** (a) rate-limiter **refund-leak fix** — the reserved-token refund now fires on **every** httpx-error attempt (both the retry AND the terminal branch), not just some paths, so a stalled/aborted stream no longer leaks reserved capacity; (b) **truncated-stream detection** — a stream that ends WITHOUT a terminal `message_delta` (socket died mid-generation) now raises a retryable `httpx.RemoteProtocolError` instead of silently returning a partial card set; (c) SSE **`error`-event enrichment** — an inline SSE `error` event is surfaced with its payload instead of an empty error string; (d) the now-**unreachable `HTTPStatusError` refund branch was removed** (dead code under streaming). **TESTS:** 16 streaming unit tests + 92 related tests pass; `ruff` clean; **two Bugbot passes + two self-reviews clean**. **§5 FAST-VALIDATION DRAIN (2026-07-07):** drove `murashko_med` chunks **4→5** on demand via a one-off `run_full_topicization_resume_for_channel("murashko_med")` against the still-soft-deleted channel (the preserved checkpoint `fullrun_20260704_174420` advanced 3→4→5), **443→769 cards (+326)**, **663,488 new tokens**, ≈**$5–8**, ~**59 min**, with **0** `anthropic_network_error` / **0** `LLMCallTimeoutError` / **0** `AnthropicBillingError`. The only non-clean signal was **2 benign `topicization_generate_truncated` per chunk**, each self-healed via `shrink_split` (expected max_tokens-cap behavior, unrelated to streaming). 13 channels were isolated before the drain and all restored afterward. **HONEST CAVEATS:** (1) per-SSE-event timing is **not logged** — the PASS rests on **40 stall-free streamed generations**, not event-level inter-chunk traces; (2) the drain ran in a **one-off exec process**, so the worker's `tg_parser_llm_tokens_total` counter did NOT move — token accounting was verified via the **checkpoint card/token delta** instead. **PROMPT-CACHING (⛔3):** remains a documented **no-op** and is **NOT** claimed as part of this win — it stays a separate, open, low-value secondary finding. **REMAINING (bonus, separate step):** shrink the per-attempt read timeout toward a true inter-chunk stall-guard now that streaming is validated — see the §2.6 bonus row below. Status → `resolved`. |
| **Update 2026-07-07 — §2.6 bonus (DECOUPLED tight streaming read timeout; ✅ VALIDATED — deployed + live-verified + re-validation drain PASS)** | Now that streaming is validated, the per-attempt httpx read timeout was tightened toward a **true inter-chunk stall-guard**. **DESIGN CHOICE — a DECOUPLED new setting, NOT a global shrink (and WHY):** `AnthropicClient` is SHARED across ALL stages, and `anthropic_http_timeout_s` (150s) is the httpx read timeout for BOTH the streaming and non-streaming paths. A global 30s shrink would be safe ONLY while streaming is ON (30s = inter-EVENT gap); if streaming were ever flipped OFF, a 30s read timeout would re-introduce the exact **BUG-079** failure — guillotining the ~90s non-streaming generation before its headers return. So instead of shrinking the global knob, a NEW setting **`anthropic_streaming_read_timeout_s` (default 30.0s, `ge=1.0`)** is applied **ONLY on the streaming path**: the client keeps its base `timeout` (150s) as the httpx-client default and, on the `stream(...)` call, overrides **only the read timeout** via a per-request `httpx.Timeout(self._timeout, read=self._streaming_read_timeout)` (connect/write/pool stay at 150s). The non-streaming `post(...)` gets **no** per-request override, so it keeps the safe 150s. Net: flipping `ANTHROPIC_STREAMING_ENABLED=false` AUTOMATICALLY reverts to the BUG-079-safe read timeout — the shrink is **decoupled from the global flag** and a short read timeout can NEVER re-open BUG-079 on the non-streaming path. The aggregate `anthropic_call_timeout_s` (**420s**) is **unchanged**. **FILES:** `tg_parser/config/settings.py` (new `anthropic_streaming_read_timeout_s=30.0` field), `tg_parser/processing/llm/anthropic_client.py` (`__init__` stores `self._timeout` + `self._streaming_read_timeout`; the streaming `stream(...)` call passes the per-request `httpx.Timeout(150, read=30)`), `tg_parser/processing/llm/factory.py` (threads `streaming_read_timeout=settings.anthropic_streaming_read_timeout_s`), `docker-compose.yml` (BUG-078 mirror: `ANTHROPIC_STREAMING_READ_TIMEOUT_S=${…:-30}`), `tg_parser/api/main.py` (boot echo extended with the new knob). **TESTS:** `tests/test_anthropic_client_streaming.py` — the streaming request applies `httpx.Timeout(read=30, connect/write/pool=150)`, and the non-streaming `post` receives NO short read timeout (keeps 150); `tests/test_llm_clients.py` — factory threads the setting, kwarg override wins, `__init__` default is 30, the Field default is authoritative 30.0, and a non-streaming client keeps 150 regardless of the streaming knob; the pre-existing gap-stall test still proves a fast trip. **`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_anthropic_client_streaming.py tests/test_llm_clients.py -q` → 54 passed; `ruff check` on all changed files → clean.** **✅ VALIDATED (2026-07-07) — deployed to prod + live-verified + re-validation drain PASS.** **DEPLOY + LIVE-VERIFY:** §2.6 (the decoupled `anthropic_streaming_read_timeout_s=30`, streaming-path-only) was deployed to prod **2026-07-07** and live-verified — the worker boot echo read **`anthropic_streaming_read_timeout_s=30.0`**, streaming **ON**, and the aggregate/base timeouts **150/420 unchanged** (the shrink is confined to the streaming read timeout, exactly as designed). **RE-VALIDATION DRAIN (`murashko_med` chunk 6):** the preserved checkpoint advanced **5→6/37**, batches **100→120**, cards **769→850 (+81)**, across **42 healthy streamed generations** each ~**70–90s**, **+326,434 tokens** ≈**$2–4**, ~**21 min** — with **ZERO** `httpx.ReadTimeout` / **ZERO** `LLMCallTimeoutError` / **ZERO** `anthropic_network_error` / **ZERO** `AnthropicBillingError`. **VERDICT: PASS** — because SSE emits events continuously, the tight **30s window measures inter-event gaps, NOT total latency**, so healthy long generations (~70–90s) are **never guillotined**; no bump to 45–60s is warranted. The §2.6 bonus is therefore **done + validated**, superseding the earlier "committed LOCAL-ONLY, not deployed" caveat. |

### BUG-079 — Recurring Anthropic 300s aggregate-timeout network stalls in Sonnet topicization (persist even under full channel isolation)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High** (cost / reliability). During the 2026-07-04 BUG-076/077 controlled chunked validation the Sonnet topicization stage repeatedly stalled on 300s aggregate-timeout network reads to `api.anthropic.com`. It is NOT rate-limiting and NOT cross-channel contention (it recurred with all other channels paused). Impact: it wastes Sonnet tokens (chunk 2 of `murashko_med` burned ~809K tokens and persisted **0** cards) and makes multi-chunk full-run drainage unreliable — it is the reliability blocker that prevented an airtight full multi-chunk drain during the BUG-076/077 validation. |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (2026-07-06) — the root cause was REFRAMED and corrected: it was **never a network fault**. A controlled timed experiment (2026-07-06, prod host, real payload) proved that legitimate non-streaming Sonnet topicization generations take **~87–90s to return HTTP response headers**, and the per-attempt httpx read timeout was guillotining them — the earlier 300s-aggregate timeouts were a *config* artifact, not a broken egress path. The corrective retune raised `anthropic_http_timeout_s` 60→**150s** and `anthropic_call_timeout_s` 300→**420s** — commit [`57d1bce`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/57d1bce), pushed to `origin/main`; deployed to prod (file-sync deploy) + live-verified 2026-07-06. An airtight 3-chunk validation (2026-07-06, `murashko_med`) then drained end-to-end with **ZERO** `anthropic_network_error` / `LLMCallTimeoutError` across 40+ generations, and crash-resume-across-container-restart was **literally exercised** (chunk 3 mid-flight → `docker compose restart` → resumed from `chunks_done=2`, 0 committed chunks lost). **NOTE — the ORIGINAL start-prompt remediation direction was DISPROVEN by measurement:** the first hardening (commit [`9069396`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/9069396)) SHRANK the per-attempt httpx timeout 120s→60s to fail fast, which was WRONG and made it worse (it cut short the healthy ~90s generations even harder) — that shrink is reverted-in-spirit by the 150s retune. See **Update 2026-07-06 — RESOLVED** below. Was 🟡 `mitigated` (2026-07-06, hardening at `9069396`); was `open` (2026-07-04, filed at commit `1135882`). `main`. |
| **Component** | `topicization` / `llm` / `network` — the AnthropicClient httpx timeout config (per-attempt `timeout=120s` default, NOT passed by the client factory); the `anthropic_call_timeout_s=300.0` aggregate wall-clock wrapper (wraps acquire + retry + backoff around `generate_with_usage`); the network path from the tg_parser host to `api.anthropic.com` (read stall at HTTP response-header receipt); the topicization batch-fanout knobs `topicization_batch_concurrency=5` / `topicization_batch_size=50`. |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-04 — during the controlled chunked/resumable full-topicization exercise on prod (the BUG-076/077 validation). Observed on `murashko_med` chunk 1 (3× timeouts, all auto-recovered) and chunk 2 (multiple timeouts) EVEN with all 13 other channels paused, so cross-channel contention is not the sole cause. |
| **Symptoms** | Repeated `LLMCallTimeoutError: Anthropic generate_with_usage exceeded 300.0s aggregate wall-clock timeout`; the cancelled tracebacks unwind inside httpx `_receive_response_headers` (i.e. a network read stall waiting on response headers from `api.anthropic.com`), accompanied by `anthropic_network_error` events with **empty** error strings. This is explicitly NOT rate-limiting: the `anthropic_retryable` / HTTP 429 count on the Anthropic key was **0** throughout. Timeouts partially auto-recover per-attempt (chunk 1) but recur, and on chunk 2 they dominated the run (~809K Sonnet tokens burned, 0 cards persisted). |
| **Root cause (hypothesis — not yet code-pinned)** | A network read stall on the host↔`api.anthropic.com` path (the httpx client blocks in `_receive_response_headers`), amplified by the timeout configuration: the per-attempt httpx `timeout=120s` (AnthropicClient default, NOT overridden by the factory) means a single stalled read can hold a slot for up to 120s, and the `anthropic_call_timeout_s=300.0` **aggregate** wall-clock timeout wraps acquire + retry + backoff — so a sequence of stalled retries consumes the entire 300s budget before a healthy retry can complete, tripping `LLMCallTimeoutError`. Because it persists under full channel isolation, local cross-channel concurrency contention is ruled out as the sole cause — the stall originates on the network path (or Anthropic-side header latency), not from local queueing alone. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | The failure mode is a real network read stall against `api.anthropic.com` (header-receipt latency) — not reproduced by any unit/integration test; the interaction between the per-attempt httpx timeout and the `anthropic_call_timeout_s` aggregate wrapper (stalled-retry sequences consuming the whole budget) is untested against an injected slow/stalling transport. |
| **Proposed fix (suggestions — NOT done)** | (1) Reduce `topicization_batch_concurrency` 5→2 and `topicization_batch_size` 50→25 to lower simultaneous load / contention. (2) Shrink the per-attempt httpx read timeout (e.g. 120s→60s) so a stalled attempt fails FAST and a healthy retry still fits inside the aggregate budget; optionally raise the aggregate `anthropic_call_timeout_s` in tandem so several fast-failing attempts + one healthy retry fit. (3) Investigate the host↔Anthropic network path (DNS, egress, TLS, proxy, header-receipt latency). **CAVEAT:** these config knobs share the docker-compose environment allow-list gotcha from **BUG-078** — the `tg_parser` compose service uses an explicit `environment:` allow-list (OS-env priority over the bind-mounted `/app/.env`), so any new/changed knob MUST be mirrored into that service's `environment:` block to actually take effect in the running worker (otherwise it silently falls back to the code default, exactly the BUG-078 class). |
| **Workaround** | None robust. Timeouts partially auto-recover per attempt, so a run can limp forward, but tokens are wasted and multi-chunk drainage is unreliable; keep batch concurrency low and monitor `LLMCallTimeoutError` / `anthropic_network_error` rates until the remediation lands. |
| **Artifacts** | Controlled chunked validation, 2026-07-04. `murashko_med` chunk 1: 3× `LLMCallTimeoutError` (300.0s aggregate), all auto-recovered. `murashko_med` chunk 2: multiple timeouts, ~809K Sonnet tokens burned, 0 cards persisted. Anthropic key `anthropic_retryable`/429 count = 0 (not rate-limited). Tracebacks cancel inside httpx `_receive_response_headers`; `anthropic_network_error` with empty error strings. Recurred with all 13 other channels paused. |
| **Linked** | BUG-076 / BUG-077 (this network stall is the reliability blocker that prevented an airtight full multi-chunk drain during their 2026-07-04 controlled chunked validation); BUG-078 (the docker-compose `environment:` allow-list caveat the remediation config knobs share); BUG-068 (Processing-stage Anthropic call can hang with no effective timeout — the adjacent Anthropic network-stall / timeout class). |
| **Update 2026-07-06 — MITIGATED (hardening shipped + deployed + live-verified; empirical §7 validation still pending)** | The proposed remediation was **implemented, deployed, and live-verified** — commit [`9069396`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/9069396) «fix(topicization): BUG-079 network-stall hardening — httpx timeout + batch-fanout wiring», pushed to `origin/main`. **CODE change (per-attempt httpx timeout, knob #3):** new settings field `anthropic_http_timeout_s` (default **60.0**, `ge=5.0`) — the per-attempt httpx read timeout, formerly a hardcoded `120.0` in `AnthropicClient.__init__`, is now env-configurable and threaded through `factory.py` into `AnthropicClient(timeout=…)` so a stalled `_receive_response_headers` read fails FAST. The aggregate `anthropic_call_timeout_s` (knob #4) is kept at **300s** — correct, and valid ONLY in tandem with the per-attempt shrink that shipped (raising it alone would just let more stalled attempts pile up, ⛔ warning 3). **COMPOSE allow-list mirror (BUG-078 trap):** `docker-compose.yml` (~lines 94–97) now mirrors all four knobs — `TOPICIZATION_BATCH_CONCURRENCY`, `TOPICIZATION_BATCH_SIZE`, `ANTHROPIC_HTTP_TIMEOUT_S`, `ANTHROPIC_CALL_TIMEOUT_S` — so `.env` values actually reach the running worker instead of being shadowed by code defaults. **OBSERVABILITY:** startup-log echo extended + four new `/health` fields (`tg_parser/api/main.py`, `tg_parser/api/schemas.py`, `tg_parser/api/routes/health.py`) surfacing the effective knob values from the running singleton. **Bugbot-found bug (orphaned knobs on the BUG-079-implicated path):** `topicization_batch_concurrency` / `topicization_batch_size` were ORPHANED on the FULL topicization path — `TopicizationPipelineImpl.__init__` defaulted `batch_concurrency=5` and hardcoded `BATCH_SIZE=50`, and the 4 production constructions in `topicization_service.py` never passed the settings, so the FIRST deploy set the env values but they did NOT reduce fanout on the full path. **Fixed** by adding a `batch_size` constructor param and threading `batch_concurrency=settings.topicization_batch_concurrency` + `batch_size=settings.topicization_batch_size` into the full-topicization construction (`_topicize_channel_locked`); `topicization_batch_size` was already wired to the incremental-discover path (`:1328`) but not the full path. Live-verified via the worker startup log + `/health`: `{topicization_batch_concurrency:2, topicization_batch_size:25, anthropic_call_timeout_s:300.0, anthropic_http_timeout_s:60.0}` — and, post the wiring-fix redeploy, these values now actually reach the full topicization path. **NETWORK-PATH INVESTIGATION (§5, read-only from the prod host → `api.anthropic.com`):** DNS stable (single A record `160.79.104.10`, query 0–12ms, no flapping); TLS/TTFB normal on spot checks (appconnect 28–113ms, TTFB/starttransfer 140–219ms). Conclusion: no chronic broken egress path — the stall class (httpx `_receive_response_headers` blocking up to 120s with empty error strings) is likely intermittent path-side / Anthropic-side header latency under load, amplified by the old timeout config, now mitigated by the 60s per-attempt fail-fast. **METRICS CAVEAT:** no Prometheus counter exists for the stall class (they are log events only — `anthropic_network_error`, `LLMCallTimeoutError`), and the container restart reset counters, so a numeric before/after stall-rate comparison is **not yet available** — it must be observed on the next real multi-chunk topicization run. **STILL OPEN:** the airtight multi-chunk Phase 2 validation (§7) has NOT been run (funded, ~$20–30, needs explicit sign-off), so the observed stall-rate improvement is NOT yet measured against live traffic, and the residual BUG-076/077 crash-resume-across-container-restart caveat remains "proven-by-mechanism, not literally exercised." Therefore status is `mitigated`, not `resolved` — full `resolved` awaits near-zero stall events observed on a multi-chunk run per the start-prompt §9. |
| **Update 2026-07-06 — RESOLVED (root-cause REFRAME + corrective 150/420 retune + airtight 3-chunk zero-stall validation + crash-resume literally exercised)** | The `mitigated` remediation direction was **DISPROVEN by measurement** and the bug is now genuinely resolved. **ROOT-CAUSE REFRAME (the key insight):** BUG-079 was originally hypothesized as a network read stall amplified by timeout config, and the first remediation (commit [`9069396`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/9069396)) SHRANK the per-attempt httpx timeout 120s→60s to "fail fast." That was WRONG and made it WORSE. A controlled timed experiment (2026-07-06, prod host, real payload) proved that real non-streaming Sonnet topicization generations (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `max_tokens=8192`, `batch_size=25`, ~8.4k input tokens) take **~87–90s to return HTTP response headers** — 3 samples: **89.09s / 89.59s / 87.06s**, all HTTP 200, `stop_reason=end_turn` (TTFB≈total because a non-streaming response only returns headers once the generation is essentially complete). Meanwhile trivial empty-POST probes to `api.anthropic.com` stayed fast (0.18–0.25s) and a full §5 network diagnostic was CLEAN (stable DNS to `160.79.104.10`, 0/12 header stalls, 0% mtr loss, no proxy, conntrack 23/65536). **CONCLUSION: it was NEVER a network fault** — the 60s (and even the old 120s) per-attempt read timeout was guillotining legitimate ~90s generations, so all 4 retries were cut short and the 300s aggregate was exhausted → `LLMCallTimeoutError` with an empty-string `anthropic_network_error` (the `ReadTimeout` at the header-receipt stage). Experiment spend ≈ $0.34. **CORRECTIVE FIX (commit [`57d1bce`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/57d1bce), pushed to `origin/main`):** raised the authoritative defaults `anthropic_http_timeout_s` 60→**150s** (covers the measured ~90s + headroom toward the ~124s 8192-token worst case) and `anthropic_call_timeout_s` 300→**420s** (fits ~2 full 150s attempts + a 60s 429 retry-after); aligned the `AnthropicClient.__init__` fallback (120→150); updated the compose mirror defaults (`ANTHROPIC_HTTP_TIMEOUT_S:-150`, `ANTHROPIC_CALL_TIMEOUT_S:-420`); added lock-in tests (**34 passed**, `ruff` clean). Deployed to prod (file-sync, `.env` set to 150/420, force-recreate), live-verified via `/health` + startup echo (`anthropic_http_timeout_s=150.0`, `anthropic_call_timeout_s=420.0`, concurrency=2, batch_size=25). The earlier 60s shrink is thereby **reverted-in-spirit** by the 150s retune. **AIRTIGHT VALIDATION (2026-07-06, `murashko_med`, isolated, ~$10–15 spend):** with 150/420, **3 chunks drained end-to-end with ZERO `anthropic_network_error` and ZERO `LLMCallTimeoutError`** across 40+ generations (each completing ~69–90s, comfortably under 150s). Chunk 2: 20 batches → 208 cards. Chunk 3: 20 batches (one 8192-token-cap batch gracefully shrink-split 12/13 and re-generated under 150s) → 137 cards. Checkpoint advanced `chunks_done` 1→2→3. Direct contrast to the two earlier runs where every attempt was guillotined at exactly 60s. Channels restored (13 active, `murashko` soft-deleted). **CRASH-RESUME LITERALLY EXERCISED:** chunk 3 was mid-flight (3 uncommitted batches) → `docker compose restart tg_parser` → the Postgres checkpoint survived intact at `chunks_done=2` → re-trigger logged `full_run_resume chunks_done=2` (same `run_id`, NOT 0) → chunk 3 re-drained and committed to `chunks_done=3`, with **0 committed chunks lost** — this also upgrades the residual BUG-076/077 caveat from "proven-by-mechanism" to "literally exercised." The §7 empirical multi-chunk stall-rate concern from the `mitigated` row is thereby answered directly by live traffic. Status → `resolved`. |

See **Update 2026-07-04** below. `main`. |
| **Component** | `config` / `api` / `ops` — the live in-memory `settings = Settings()` module-level singleton (`tg_parser/config/settings.py:1705`) read once at import; the enable/verify procedure in the controlled-enable runbook §4b; the startup log site `tg_parser/api/main.py:150-154` ("Environment: LLM provider=%s, model=%s") and the `/health` route (`tg_parser/api/routes/health.py:24-40`, schema `HealthResponse` `tg_parser/api/schemas.py:62-68`) as the fix surfaces. | **Discovered** | 2026-07-02 — during the controlled first-enable exercise on prod (HEAD `4f8a326`). Enable sequence executed per the runbook: set `TOPICIZATION_FULL_RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET=450000` + `TOPICIZATION_FULL_RESUME_ENABLED=true` in prod `/home/user/TG_parser/.env`; force-recreated `tg_parser` (StartedAt advanced to `14:52:25Z`, PID changed); the §4b verify (`docker compose exec tg_parser python -c 'print(settings.topicization_full_resume_enabled, ...)'`) printed `True 450000`; resumed `murashko_med`. At `15:59:45Z` the scheduler escalated to FULL and ran the legacy monolithic path; at `16:58:47Z` it crashed on `AnthropicBillingError` ("credit balance too low") with 0 cards persisted. |
| **Symptoms** | A 0-card, large-backlog channel escalated to FULL topicization and — with the resume flag supposedly enabled — ran the **legacy monolithic all-or-nothing** run rather than the chunked/resumable path, then crashed on billing exhaustion having persisted **0 cards** (~430K tokens burned on the run; process-wide cumulative ~2.90M Sonnet). A near-exact replay of the original BUG-076 incident, on the very feature meant to prevent it. |
| **Monolithic-path proof (why we know the chunked path did NOT run)** | Three path-exclusive signals, all consistent: (1) the log line `tg_parser/processing/topicization.py:~376` "Large channel (17848 docs), 357 batches of 50" — emitted **only** on the legacy `else` batch loop, never on `_topicize_channel_chunked`; (2) **all 357 batches ran in ONE invocation** (the chunked path caps at `topicization_full_max_chunks_per_invocation=1` ≈ 20 batches/tick and halts durably); (3) **no** `tg_parser_topicization_full_run_*` metric samples were emitted (those series are chunked-path-exclusive) and **no** `topicization:full_checkpoint:murashko_med` row appeared in `processing_failures`. The gate at `topicization.py:334` therefore evaluated **False**. |
| **Root cause (pinned; the FLAG operand was False in the live worker — repo operand DEFINITIVELY ruled out)** | The gate `settings.topicization_full_resume_enabled and self.processing_failure_repo is not None` (`topicization.py:334`) fell through on the **flag** operand, not the repo operand. The `processing_failure_repo is None` hypothesis is **ruled out**: on the first-escalation path (`should_reescalate` → `run_topicization` at `topicization_service.py:1087-1095` → `_topicize_channel_locked`), `pipeline_failure_repo` is bound from the shared session at `topicization_service.py:553-557` and is **always non-None** (a `SATopicCardRepo` always exposes `.session`; the incremental path binds the same way at `:991-1003`). So the live in-memory `settings` singleton in the worker (PID 1) held `topicization_full_resume_enabled=False`. This is **NOT a code-routing gap** — the code would have taken the chunked branch had the flag been True in-process. |
| **The real gap — OBSERVABILITY / FALSE-GREEN VERIFY** | `settings = Settings()` (`tg_parser/config/settings.py:1705`) is a **module-level singleton read once at import**; a long-lived worker (PID 1) captures its value at process start and never re-reads `.env`. The runbook's §4b verify (`docker compose exec tg_parser python -c '...print(settings...)'`) spawns a **FRESH process** that re-parses the current `.env` (correctly printing `True 450000`) and does **NOT** reflect the running worker's in-memory value — so it is a **false-green** check that cannot detect the exact failure it is meant to guard against. Every read-only signal available (`.env` contains the flag; same inode host+container for the single-file bind mount; `.env` ctime `14:49:40Z` predates PID1 start `14:52:25Z`; correct F7 bytecode; no OS-env override; a fresh in-container parse returns `True`) says PID1 *should* have parsed `True` — yet it behaved as `False`. **The exact mechanism is UNRESOLVED by read-only means precisely because the live singleton value is unobservable** — which is itself the core finding: there is no way to observe the running worker's effective flag today. |
| **Kill-switch clobber caveat** | The first manual MCP `pause_channel` on `murashko_med` was **clobbered back to `active`** by the billing-backoff handler (`anthropic_billing_source_paused`, wrote `updated_at=16:58:53Z`, cooldown until `17:58:53Z`); a **second** pause held. Operational note for future kill-switch use: a manual pause issued while a billing-backoff cycle is in flight can be overwritten — re-verify the pause holds, or prefer `remove_channel`. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | This is not a code correctness bug — the unit/integration suites (BUG-076: 31 PG tests; BUG-077: 38 tests; combined 278; full repo 3662) all assert the chunked path's behaviour **assuming the flag is True in-process**, which is exactly the condition that silently did not hold in the live worker. No test (and no runtime signal) asserts that the running long-lived process's effective `settings.topicization_full_resume_enabled` matches what was written to `.env` — the singleton's live value is simply not surfaced anywhere. **Closure = the observability fix** (startup log echo + `/health` field), not a new unit test. |
| **Proposed fix** | **(1) Startup echo (primary).** Log the effective `settings.topicization_full_resume_enabled` + `settings.topicization_full_run_token_budget` at process start, next to the existing "Environment: LLM provider=%s, model=%s" line (`tg_parser/api/main.py:150-154`), so the FIRST log line of every boot records the singleton's actual import-time value. **(2) `/health` surfacing (recommended).** Add both fields to the `/health` payload (`tg_parser/api/routes/health.py:24-40` + `HealthResponse` in `tg_parser/api/schemas.py:62-68`) for on-demand read-only verification of the RUNNING process. **(3) CORRECTED enable/verify procedure** superseding runbook §4b: edit `.env` **in place** (append / `cat`, never `sed -i` or an editor atomic-save that changes inode and can orphan a single-file bind mount), `docker compose up -d --force-recreate tg_parser`, then verify via `docker logs tg_parser --since <StartedAt> \| grep topicization_full_resume_enabled` and/or the new `/health` field — **do NOT trust `docker compose exec ... python -c`** (false-green). Behavioural proof once genuinely live: the first escalation of a 0-card channel writes a `topicization:full_checkpoint:<channel>` row in `processing_failures` and emits `tg_parser_topicization_full_run_*` metrics. Per AGENTS.md this is a code change requiring explicit approval before commit; no `pyproject.toml`/`requirements.txt` edits. |
| **Corrective actions already taken (current prod state)** | (a) `murashko_med` **REMOVED** via `remove_channel` (soft-delete; `deleted_at` set; data preserved; out of scheduler) — judged low expert value, not worth further spend. (b) `@Docma_ru` **ADDED** via `add_channel` (`status=active`, `created=true`); will begin RAW Telegram ingestion (no Anthropic calls). (c) Prod `.env` **STILL** contains `TOPICIZATION_FULL_RESUME_ENABLED=true` + `TOPICIZATION_FULL_RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET=450000` (backup `.env.bak_bug077_enable_20260702_174927`); this flag is treated as **UNRELIABLE / unverified-live**. (d) The Anthropic balance is **EXHAUSTED**, which is the current **de-facto safety gate** — processing and topicization both require the API, so nothing can burn or escalate while the balance is empty (do NOT top up until the flag is verified live in the worker). |
| **Workaround** | Do not top up the Anthropic balance until the startup-echo fix is deployed and the flag is verified live in the running worker (the empty balance is the safety net against a monolithic re-burn on `@Docma_ru` or any other 0-card channel). Keep `budget=450000` as an auditable kill-switch. The controlled first exercise must be re-run per the BUG-076 runbook once the flag is genuinely live. |
| **Artifacts** | Prod HEAD `4f8a326` (BUG-077/F7 tip). Incident timeline (2026-07-02): enable at `.env` ctime `14:49:40Z`; force-recreate StartedAt `14:52:25Z` (PID changed); §4b verify printed `True 450000`; FULL escalation `15:59:45Z`; billing crash `16:58:47Z` (0 cards; ~430K tokens on the run; process-wide ~2.90M Sonnet); billing-backoff pause-clobber `updated_at=16:58:53Z` (cooldown to `17:58:53Z`). Backup: `/home/user/TG_parser/.env.bak_bug077_enable_20260702_174927`. Runbook executed: [`START_PROMPT_SESSION_BUG076_077_CONTROLLED_ENABLE_MURASHKO_MED_2026-07-02.md`](START_PROMPT_SESSION_BUG076_077_CONTROLLED_ENABLE_MURASHKO_MED_2026-07-02.md). Fix handoff: [`START_PROMPT_SESSION_BUG078_FLAG_LIVE_OBSERVABILITY_AND_SAFE_REENABLE_2026-07-02.md`](START_PROMPT_SESSION_BUG078_FLAG_LIVE_OBSERVABILITY_AND_SAFE_REENABLE_2026-07-02.md). |
| **Linked** | BUG-076 (the crash-safe/resumable full-topicization feature this exercise was meant to prove; the incident is a replay of BUG-076's original monolithic 0-card burn); BUG-077 (the residual token-leak hardening whose F7 tip `4f8a326` was live in prod; the controlled first exercise it gates was the operation that failed); the controlled-enable runbook (whose §4b false-green verify is superseded by this entry's Proposed fix). |
| **Update 2026-07-04 — RESOLVED (root cause pinned + corrective fix live-verified)** | The §2 observability fix was implemented and deployed — a startup log echo in `tg_parser/api/main.py` plus two optional fields on `/health` (`HealthResponse` in `tg_parser/api/schemas.py` + `tg_parser/api/routes/health.py`); commits [`338b0d8`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/338b0d8) (code) + [`94404c4`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/94404c4) (docs); Bugbot clean, ruff clean, 15 health tests passed. **Deploying it reproduced the puzzle live**: the running worker echoed `topicization_full_resume_enabled=False, topicization_full_run_token_budget=0` in BOTH the startup log and `/health`, despite prod `.env` having `TOPICIZATION_FULL_RESUME_ENABLED=true` / `=450000`. **ROOT CAUSE (now pinned, no longer "unresolvable"):** the `tg_parser` compose service uses an explicit `environment:` allow-list (NOT `env_file: .env`), and pydantic-settings gives OS-env priority over the bind-mounted `/app/.env`; the `TOPICIZATION_FULL_*` family was never mirrored into that allow-list (unlike the `RESUMMARIZE_*` family, whose identical gotcha was already documented in `docker-compose.yml`), so the long-lived worker fell back to code defaults (`False`/`0`). The §5 "process read False" puzzle is thereby RESOLVED — the mechanism was the compose allow-list omission (an OS-env-vs-bind-mounted-`.env` precedence issue), exactly the class the startup echo was designed to disambiguate. **BUG-076 / BUG-077 remain `open`** until the controlled chunked first-exercise actually succeeds with a funded balance. |

### BUG-077 — Residual token-leak hardening of the committed BUG-076 resumable full topicization (no-progress drip, reconcile double-spend, read-error fresh-start, broad stale wipe)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High** (cost / unproductive-spend). Adversarial audit of the committed BUG-076 fix (`596fe30`) found six residual spend surfaces. Two are **deterministic and MUST be closed before `topicization_full_resume_enabled` is ever flipped ON**: **F1** — the resume driver retries a live checkpoint EVERY tick with the BUG-071 cooldown deliberately disarmed, so a chunk that keeps failing WITHOUT advancing `chunks_done` (constraint-violating card, always-truncating batch, malformed merge) re-burns generate+merge tokens each tick with no backoff/counter — the only UNBOUNDED leak; **F4** — the BUG-075 reconcile hook doesn't know about a live full checkpoint, so after chunk 1 commits it feeds up to `topicization_reconcile_max_docs=200` of the not-yet-done chunks' docs into Phase-2 discover EVERY tick — guaranteed cold-start double-spend + fragmented duplicate cards.
