| **Discovered** | 2026-07-02 — deliberate adversarial token-leak audit of the just-committed BUG-076 feature (session `START_PROMPT_SESSION_BUG076_TOKENLEAK_HARDENING_IMPL_2026-07-02.md`), before any thought of enabling the flag. |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced in the start-prompt)** | The BUG-076 design intentionally disarms the BUG-071 re-escalation cooldown while a live checkpoint exists (partial progress ≠ failed escalation) and drives the resume EVERY tick — correct for a progressing run, but with **no progress-detection**: nothing distinguished "advanced a chunk" from "spent tokens and halted at the same chunk again" (the driver's summary even reported the stale PRE-invocation `chunks_done`). The reconcile hook (BUG-075) and the full-run machinery (BUG-076) were designed independently and shared no liveness signal. `_read_full_checkpoint` swallowed ALL read exceptions to `None` (= "absent"). The stale-restart wipe predated any per-run card ownership marker (cards carried an unmatchable per-card `run_<now>` stamp from `_build_topic_card`). |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | **F1 (enable-blocker) — no-progress circuit-breaker.** Checkpoint gains `consecutive_noprogress_resumes` + `last_noprogress_at` (legacy-safe defaults). The resume driver re-READS the checkpoint post-invocation: progress = `chunks_done` advanced / `final_merge_done` flipped / row cleared / `run_id` re-pinned → any stale non-zero counter repaired to 0; NO progress → counter += 1 via a standalone failure-path checkpoint write (preserves `chunks_done`/`attempts`/pinned plan — the atomic commit by definition never ran); a `0x70C1` lock-skip is NEUTRAL (no increment, no reset); an exception is bookkept then re-raised; an unreadable post-state never increments (unknown ≠ stalled). Shared predicate `noprogress_circuit_open` gates BOTH entries (driver pre-lock + pipeline resuming-branch — the latter covers the 0-card `should_reescalate` escalation path that bypasses the driver): closed below `noprogress_limit` (default **3**, 0=disabled); open → 0-token skip (`skipped_reason="noprogress_circuit_open"` + `noprogress_skip_total` metric); after `noprogress_cooldown_s` (default **3600**, 0=hard-open) ONE probe runs — a failing probe re-arms the TTL, so steady-state leak ≤ 1 chunk-attempt/hour; a durable chunk commit implicitly resets (fresh checkpoint, counter 0). **F2 (folded into F1)** — malformed merge reply (string group ids → `TypeError`/`AttributeError` in the group-id loop) is now a clean resumable halt (chunk NOT committed, merge failed-batch + `reason=malformed_merge`) instead of an uncaught crash re-driven bare every tick. **F4 (enable-blocker) — reconcile deferral.** `run_reconciliation_for_channel` hard-skips (`skipped_reason="full_run_in_progress"`, `deferred=True`) BEFORE candidate selection while `_has_live_full_checkpoint` is True — DEFER not abandonment (the gate re-arms automatically when the checkpoint clears; the full run + the next reconcile tick cover everything); flag OFF ⇒ helper returns False ⇒ gate dark. **F9 — observability.** New counter `full_run_chunk_failed_total{reason=merge_halt\|malformed_merge\|empty_after_failure\|commit_failed}` + the failed chunk's PRE-commit token spend now emitted to `full_run_tokens_total`; an in-process atomic-commit failure is a clean counted halt (`topicization_commit` failed-batch stage) instead of an uncaught crash; 3 new Prometheus alerts (resume-rising-while-chunks-flat, chunk-failed-sustained, circuit-open). **F3 — read-error ≠ absent.** `_read_full_checkpoint` raises `FullCheckpointReadError` on transport errors → pipeline aborts the invocation benignly at 0 cost (never a fresh pinned run); the driver returns `skipped_reason="checkpoint_read_error"`; a resume whose checkpoint VANISHED under the lock (read/clear race) is a no-op, never a fresh corpus re-burn (force=True unaffected). **F7 — re-enable hygiene.** A successful legacy monolithic run (≥1 card) best-effort-deletes the channel's leftover checkpoint marker (supersedes the stale plan); `_topicize_channel_locked` now always binds the shared-session failure repo so the clear works on the production path (dark-safe: with the flag off the pipeline uses that repo ONLY for this delete); runbook §10 documents the inspect/clear SQL for the pre-enable checklist. **F5 — scoped stale wipe.** `_commit_chunk_atomically` stamps every card's `metadata.topicization_run_id` with the CHECKPOINT's pinned `fullrun_*` id (overwriting the unmatchable per-card `run_<now>` stamp); checkpoint gains `cards_stamped` (True for fresh runs, carried forward on resume); the stale-restart wipe deletes ONLY the prior run's stamped cards+bundles — BUG-075 incremental/discover cards survive; a pre-fix checkpoint (`cards_stamped=False`) falls back to the broad `delete_by_channel` so the duplicate-card protection cannot regress. New settings (defaults need user confirmation): `topicization_full_resume_noprogress_limit=3`, `topicization_full_resume_noprogress_cooldown_s=3600`. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | The BUG-076 suite asserted the halt/resume semantics of each failure class but never asserted the AGGREGATE spend of a permanently-stalled run across ticks (no test drove the resume driver N times against a never-advancing checkpoint), never ran the reconcile hook against a live checkpoint, never made `list_failures` raise (vs return-empty), and never asserted which OTHER cards survive a stale wipe. **Closure:** `tests/test_bug077_tokenleak_hardening.py` — 38 tests (30 initial + 2 round-1 HIGH follow-up + 2 round-2 HIGH follow-up + 4 round-3 follow-up [1 HIGH + 1 MEDIUM]): breaker predicate semantics (below-limit/disabled closed, cooldown-0 hard-open, TTL open→probe, bad/missing/future timestamp never strands); driver counter increments on stalled resume (failure-path write preserves plan/`chunks_done`/`attempts`) and monotone across ticks; stale counter reset on advance; lock-skip neutral; circuit-open skip at 0 cost + metric (run_topicization NOT invoked); probe after TTL (failing probe re-arms); exception bookkeeps-then-reraises; driver pre-read error benign skip; post-read error = no counter write; pipeline-side gate blocks the escalation entry at 0 LLM calls (and closed-breaker still advances — no false trip); E2E malformed-merge through the REAL `_merge_topics` (string group ids) = clean halt + `malformed_merge` metric; pipeline read-error aborts-not-fresh-start; resume-vanished no-op; force-still-fresh regression guard; merge-halt emits chunk-failed + pre-commit tokens; empty-after-failure metric; commit-failure clean counted halt (checkpoint NOT advanced, `record_topic_created` NOT called for rolled-back cards); cards stamped with checkpoint `run_id`; scoped wipe preserves foreign/incremental cards; pre-fix `cards_stamped=False` broad-wipe fallback; legacy success clears leftover marker / 0-card legacy run preserves it; reconcile deferred while live (gate fires BEFORE corpus read, 0 LLM), gate releases after clear, complete-checkpoint ≠ live, gate dark when flag OFF; **(Bugbot round-1 HIGH follow-up)** escalation-then-driver same-tick sequence with an at-limit/TTL-elapsed checkpoint yields exactly ONE chunked attempt (one batch generated) and the driver's `run_topicization` is never awaited; a driver-invoked REAL failing pipeline increments the counter exactly once (no double-write); **(Bugbot round-2 HIGH follow-up)** a REAL pipeline run against a checkpoint with `chunks_done == chunks_total` (all chunks already durable) makes zero LLM calls, confirms `full_run_halted is False` / `full_run_all_chunks_done is True`, then a simulated `_finalize_full_run` failure propagates through the driver — the counter stays at **0** (not incremented) and `last_noprogress_at` stays `None`; a 5-tick repeated-finalize-failure loop confirms the breaker NEVER opens from finalize failures alone; **(Bugbot round-3 follow-up)** a REAL pipeline run whose OWN internal checkpoint read fails mid-invocation (distinct from the driver's own successful pre-read) confirms `full_run_checkpoint_read_aborted is True` / `full_run_halted is True` / zero chunks touched, then the driver's post-invocation classification confirms the counter stays at **0**; a checkpoint-read error injected directly into the reconcile gate's OWN liveness read confirms the tick DEFERS (`skipped_reason="full_run_in_progress"`, zero LLM spend, `run_incremental_topicization` never awaited) and a SUBSEQUENT tick with a working read proceeds normally (not sticky); the BUG-071 cooldown-arming wrapper (`_has_live_full_checkpoint`) is separately verified to still fail OPEN (`False`) on the SAME read-error shape, proving the two callers now have independent, correct policies; the raising core (`_read_full_checkpoint_liveness`) is verified to propagate `FullCheckpointReadError` rather than swallow it. **Verified UNDER POSTGRES** (`tg_parser_postgres` pgvector:pg17): BUG-071..077 combined = **278 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (071+072+073+074+075+076+077+017+018+023+topicization+incremental+cross-channel suites); BUG-077 suite standalone = **38 passed**; FULL repo suite = **3662 passed, 20 skipped, 0 failed** (3 pre-existing known-unrelated deselected/skipped). `ruff` clean. |
| **Verified NON-issues (audit)** | (1) *Escalation + resume double-drive in one tick* — bounded by design: both go through the non-blocking `0x70C1` lock sequentially; worst case two chunks advance in one tick (speeds convergence, never storms). **Refined by the Bugbot HIGH follow-up below:** this holds for the ADVANCING case, but the original NO-PROGRESS bookkeeping had a gap when the SAME tick's two callers both hit a FAILING chunk — see the review row. (2) *`record_topic_created` double-count on the full path* — the wrapper emit is guarded off by `full_run_active` (BUG-076); re-verified with the commit-failure test (rolled-back cards emit nothing). |
| **Bugbot review round 1 — 1× HIGH FIXED (uncommitted)** | **HIGH — F1 probe doubled via the escalation path.** The no-progress counter (`consecutive_noprogress_resumes`) was written ONLY inside `run_full_topicization_resume_for_channel`'s post-invocation bookkeeping. But the pre-existing `should_reescalate` branch (0-card + new docs, `topicization_service.py` ~`:1044`) ALSO drives a chunked attempt directly via its own `run_topicization` call — gated by the SAME `noprogress_circuit_open` predicate, but writing NOTHING back on failure. Since the scheduler runs incremental topicization (containing the escalation branch) BEFORE the resume driver every tick, once the cooldown window opened for a probe, BOTH could independently fire a full chunked attempt in the SAME tick: the escalation branch's failed attempt left the checkpoint counter untouched, so the driver's own pre-invocation check — reading the SAME still-unincremented row — saw a closed breaker and fired a SECOND, independent chunked attempt. Net: up to 2× generate+merge spend per probe window instead of the intended "exactly one probe per cooldown window". **Fix**: moved the counter-increment write to the SINGLE choke point both callers actually funnel through — the chunked pipeline itself. New `TopicizationPipelineImpl._record_noprogress_resume` (`processing/topicization.py`) is invoked at the end of `_topicize_channel_chunked` whenever an invocation halts (`halted=True`) with ZERO durable progress THIS invocation (`processed_this_invocation == 0`) against a checkpoint that ALREADY existed (`resuming=True` — i.e. genuinely continuing a live pinned plan, not a fresh run or a stale-restart re-pin under a new `run_id`); it preserves `chunks_done`/`batches_done`/the pinned plan and only bumps the breaker fields + cumulative tokens. Because this fires INSIDE whichever caller's invocation actually executed the failing attempt, the FIRST caller to fail (escalation or driver, whichever runs first that tick) closes the breaker BEFORE the second caller even reads the checkpoint — bounding spend to exactly one probe attempt per cooldown window regardless of entry-point ordering. The driver's OWN post-invocation write (`run_full_topicization_resume_for_channel`) is now a **fallback only**: it detects the pipeline's write via `post.consecutive_noprogress_resumes != checkpoint.consecutive_noprogress_resumes` (the pre- vs post-invocation snapshot) and skips its own increment when the pipeline already bumped it — so a driver-triggered failure is still counted exactly once, not twice; the driver still increments as a last resort for the narrow case where `run_topicization` raises BEFORE ever reaching the chunked pipeline (e.g. LLM client construction failing), which the pipeline-level write cannot observe. The "progressed → reset stale counter" branch is unchanged. No behavior change to the ADVANCING case (escalation kicks off chunk 1 + the driver picks up chunk 2 in the same tick remains intentional and unaffected — verified by the existing `test_pipeline_breaker_closed_lets_escalation_advance` / `test_driver_resets_stale_counter_when_resume_advances`). **Tests added:** `test_escalation_and_driver_share_bookkeeping_only_one_probe_per_tick` (an at-limit, TTL-elapsed checkpoint; a REAL escalation-style `pipeline.topicize_channel` call fails and bumps the counter to 4 with a fresh timestamp; the driver invoked immediately after in the SAME test sees the now-open breaker and skips — `run_topicization` never awaited, exactly one batch generated total) and `test_driver_invoked_real_pipeline_failure_counted_once_not_twice` (the driver invokes a REAL failing pipeline directly — no separate escalation call — and the counter still lands at exactly 1, proving the driver's fallback correctly no-ops when the pipeline already wrote). **Verified UNDER POSTGRES:** BUG-071..077 = **156 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (up from 154 — the 2 new tests); adjacent suites = **159 passed** (unchanged). `ruff` clean on both edited files. |
| **Bugbot review round 2 — 1× HIGH FIXED (uncommitted)** | **HIGH — finalize failure trips the chunk-generation breaker.** The round-1 fix's driver-side FALLBACK branch (meant strictly for "`run_topicization` raised BEFORE ever reaching the chunked pipeline") had an unguarded blind spot: when a checkpoint's `chunks_done == chunks_total` PRE-invocation (every chunk already durable, only the free cross-chunk `_finalize_full_run` merge remains), `_topicize_channel_chunked`'s per-chunk loop range (`range(chunks_done, chunks_total)`) is EMPTY — the pipeline runs, does nothing (0 LLM calls), `halted` stays `False`, and `TopicizationPipelineImpl._record_noprogress_resume` correctly never fires (there was no halt to bookkeep). Control then returns to `_topicize_channel_locked`, which calls `_finalize_full_run` — pure Jaccard/cosine consolidation over PERSISTED cards, **zero LLM calls, zero token cost**. If THAT raises, the exception propagates out of `run_topicization` to the driver exactly like a genuine chunk-generation stall would. The driver's `progressed` check (higher `chunks_done` / flipped `final_merge_done` / changed `run_id`) correctly finds no progress (none of those fields could have changed — finalize failed before committing anything), and the "already bookkept by the pipeline" check also finds the counter unchanged (correctly — the pipeline never touched it) — so control fell through to the FALLBACK branch, which incremented `consecutive_noprogress_resumes` for a failure that had **nothing to do with chunk generation**. Repeated finalize failures (e.g. a transient DB hiccup during the merge, or an embedding-repo blip) would eventually OPEN the F1 circuit and make the driver skip even ATTEMPTING the free finalize pass for a full cooldown window (default 1h) — stalling completion of an otherwise 100%-chunked run for a token-cost reason that never existed. This defeats F1's actual purpose (throttling EXPENSIVE repeated LLM spend, not gating a free consolidation retry). **Fix** (`run_full_topicization_resume_for_channel`, `topicization_service.py`): the driver now computes `pre_all_chunks_done = checkpoint.chunks_total > 0 and checkpoint.chunks_done >= checkpoint.chunks_total` and the same for the post-read (`post_all_chunks_done`); when neither `progressed` nor the pipeline already bookkept it, a NEW `finalize_only_failure = not progressed and pre_all_chunks_done and post_all_chunks_done` check intercepts BEFORE the fallback branch — on a finalize-only failure the driver logs (`bug077_resume_finalize_failed_no_chunk_breaker_trip`) and re-raises without touching the checkpoint at all: no counter change, no `last_noprogress_at` write. Only when chunks were genuinely still outstanding pre-invocation (`pre_all_chunks_done=False`) does an unexplained failure still fall through to the fallback increment — preserving the ORIGINAL protection for "`run_topicization` raised before the pipeline ever ran" and for any REAL chunk-generation stall. Deliberately NOT a separate counter/threshold for finalize (per the finding's stated options) — since finalize is free, idempotent, and a fixpoint, an uncounted retry-next-tick-without-backoff is the correct (and simplest) posture; no new setting needed. **Tests added:** `test_finalize_only_failure_does_not_trip_chunk_generation_breaker` (seeds `chunks_done == chunks_total == 1`, `final_merge_done=False`; a REAL pipeline run confirms `full_run_halted is False` / `full_run_all_chunks_done is True` / zero cards generated, THEN a simulated `_finalize_full_run` raise propagates through the driver — asserts `consecutive_noprogress_resumes == 0`, `last_noprogress_at is None`, checkpoint otherwise untouched) and `test_repeated_finalize_failures_never_open_chunk_breaker` (5 successive ticks of the same finalize-failure shape — the breaker predicate stays closed and the counter stays at 0 throughout, proving no accumulation). **Verified UNDER POSTGRES:** BUG-077 standalone = **34 passed** (up from 32); BUG-071..077 + adjacent suites (071/072/073/074/075/076/077/017/018/023/topicization/incremental/cross-channel) = **274 passed, 0 failed**; FULL repo suite = **3658 passed, 20 skipped, 0 failed**. `ruff` clean on both edited files. |
| **Bugbot review round 3 — 1× HIGH + 1× MEDIUM FIXED (uncommitted)** | **HIGH — F4 reconcile gate fails OPEN on a checkpoint-read error.** `_has_live_full_checkpoint` (the F4 gate's liveness check) swallowed ANY `list_failures` transport/read error to `False` ("no live checkpoint") — correct for its ORIGINAL caller (the BUG-071 cooldown-arming crash/0-card-outcome handling, which wants to preserve arm-on-uncertainty), but WRONG for the NEW F4 reconcile-gate caller: a transient DB read failure was treated as "safe to proceed," so reconcile ran Phase-2 LLM discover on that tick even though a resumable full run might genuinely be live — the EXACT double-spend F4 exists to prevent, just triggered by a read hiccup instead of the normal case. Contrast: the resume driver's own checkpoint pre-read correctly fails CLOSED (aborts) on a read error (F3) — the reconcile gate did the opposite. **Fix:** split the liveness check into a RAISING core, `_read_full_checkpoint_liveness` (propagates `FullCheckpointReadError` on a transport error instead of swallowing it — same exception class F3 already uses for the pipeline's own checkpoint read), and TWO independent callers apply their OWN correct policy on top: (1) `_has_live_full_checkpoint` — a thin fail-OPEN wrapper, UNCHANGED behavior, used unmodified at BOTH original BUG-071 cooldown-arming call sites (`topicization_service.py` — the `should_reescalate` crash handler and the persisted-0-cards outcome handler); (2) `run_reconciliation_for_channel`'s F4 gate — calls the raising core DIRECTLY and on `FullCheckpointReadError` sets `live_full_run = True` (fail CLOSED: treat "unknown" as "assume live, defer"), logs (`bug077_reconcile_gate_read_error_deferring_closed`), and returns the SAME `deferred=True, skipped_reason="full_run_in_progress"` shape as a confirmed-live checkpoint — a DEFER, not abandonment: best-effort, no crash, no `stage_errors` pollution, automatically retried next tick (the SAME `reconcile_only` incremental path already treats a defer as a normal per-tick outcome, so there is no spin/loop risk — a persistent read failure just means reconcile stays deferred every tick until reads recover, exactly as intended). **Tests added:** `test_reconcile_defers_closed_on_checkpoint_read_error` (a `FlakyReadRepo` failing on the gate's OWN first read → asserts `skipped_reason="full_run_in_progress"`, `deferred=True`, zero LLM spend, THEN a subsequent tick on the SAME repo — whose transient failure has passed — proceeds normally to `no_docs`, proving the fail-closed defer is not sticky); `test_has_live_full_checkpoint_still_fails_open_on_read_error` (the SAME read-error shape against the unchanged BUG-071 wrapper still resolves to `False`, proving the two callers now have independent, correct, non-regressed policies); `test_read_full_checkpoint_liveness_raises_on_read_error` (the raising core propagates `FullCheckpointReadError` rather than swallowing it). **MEDIUM — driver counts a zero-cost F3 read-abort as a no-progress stall.** When the DRIVER's own Phase-A pre-read succeeds but the CHUNKED PIPELINE then hits its own internal F3 checkpoint-read-error abort MID-invocation (a distinct, later read — e.g. a transient DB blip that resolves between the driver's read and the pipeline's read, or vice versa), `_topicize_channel_chunked` returns `[]` and `run_topicization` completes NORMALLY (no exception) with the checkpoint UNCHANGED — 0 LLM calls, 0 chunks touched, 0 token cost. The driver's post-invocation classification had no way to distinguish this from a genuine (costly) chunk-generation stall — `progressed` is False (nothing changed) and the "already bookkept by the pipeline" check is also False (the pipeline correctly never touches the counter on this path — there was no halt to bookkeep) — so it fell through to the FALLBACK branch and incremented `consecutive_noprogress_resumes` for an event that spent ZERO tokens and attempted ZERO chunks. Repeated transient read blips (unrelated to any real LLM/chunk problem) could accumulate toward opening the F1 circuit and throttling genuinely healthy resumes. **Fix:** `TopicizationPipelineImpl` gained `full_run_checkpoint_read_aborted: bool` (reset per invocation, set `True` exactly at the F3 abort site in `_topicize_channel_chunked`); `_topicize_channel_locked` forwards it through the `run_topicization` summary dict as `checkpoint_read_aborted`; the driver computes `checkpoint_read_aborted = bool(summary and summary.get("checkpoint_read_aborted", False))` and inserts a new branch — checked before the finalize-only-failure and fallback branches — that logs (`bug077_resume_checkpoint_read_aborted_no_chunk_breaker_trip`) and skips the counter write entirely when set. **Test added:** `test_pipeline_checkpoint_read_abort_does_not_trip_chunk_breaker` — a `FlakyReadRepo` configured so the driver's OWN Phase-A pre-read (call 1) succeeds but the REAL pipeline's internal `_read_full_checkpoint` (call 2, DURING the invocation) fails, confirming `full_run_checkpoint_read_aborted is True` / `full_run_halted is True` / zero cards generated, then asserting the driver's post-invocation counter stays at **0** (not incremented) — distinct from (and complementary to) the existing `test_driver_pre_read_error_is_benign_skip` (which covers the DRIVER's OWN pre-read failing, a different code path). **Verified UNDER POSTGRES:** BUG-077 standalone = **38 passed** (up from 34); BUG-071..077 + adjacent suites = **278 passed, 0 failed**; FULL repo suite = **3662 passed, 20 skipped, 0 failed** (up from 3658 — the 4 new tests). `ruff` clean on all edited files. |
| **Workaround** | None needed — the feature is DARK (`topicization_full_resume_enabled=False`) and `murashko_med` stays paused; the legacy path is unchanged. Do NOT enable the flag before this entry is resolved (F1+F4 are the enable-blockers) and the runbook §10 pre-enable checkpoint-hygiene check is run. |

### BUG-076 — FULL topicization persists cards only at an atomic END-merge → a crash at `_merge_topics` vaporizes the whole run (0 cards for millions of tokens); cold-start 0-card channels are a refill-trap

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Critical** (cost / crash-safety / correctness). A single legitimate FULL re-topicization of `murashko_med` (0 topic cards + ~15.5K-doc backlog, ~353 batches, ~6M+ Sonnet tokens) ran to completion of the batch-generation phase, then CRASHED at the final `_merge_topics` consolidation on `AnthropicBillingError` and persisted **ZERO** topic cards — ~6.6M tokens burned for 0 cards. Any future refill that cannot fund the ENTIRE monolithic run in ONE pass is re-vaporized identically (a refill-trap). Distinct from the BUG-071..075 token-burn class: this is NOT a re-burn / storm bug — it is a **crash-safety / incremental-persistence / budget-awareness** gap in the full-topicization path. |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (2026-07-04) — the crash-safe/resumable full-topicization path was **exercised end-to-end in a controlled production validation** (three runs, 2026-07-04: `Docma_ru` full chunked run to completion; `murashko_med` chunk-1 atomic commit + resume-across-invocations; clean resumable halts on billing / token-budget caps with committed work preserved), closing the crash-safety / incremental-persistence gap this bug described — a mid-run failure no longer vaporizes the whole run. Crash-resume-across-container-restart was originally **proven-by-mechanism** (the Postgres `processing_failures` checkpoint survives restart + resume-from-checkpoint demonstrated across separate invocations) but not literally exercised — **UPGRADED 2026-07-06 to literally exercised** (during the BUG-079 airtight validation: `murashko_med` chunk 3 mid-flight → `docker compose restart tg_parser` → resumed from `chunks_done=2`, 0 committed chunks lost; see BUG-079 Update 2026-07-06). See **Update 2026-07-04 — RESOLVED (controlled chunked exercise performed)** below. Historic (2026-07-02): fix + tests **COMMITTED [`596fe30`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/596fe30)** «fix(topicization): checkpoint/resumable per-chunk persistence for full topicization (BUG-076)» and **PUSHED to `origin/main`** (2026-07-02 status refresh; the previous "UNCOMMITTED / local HEAD `d41a3dd`" text predated the commit). All six mandatory pillars (a–f) + four Bugbot review rounds included. **NOT yet deployed to prod** (prod HEAD `b7285d7` per the watch runbook) and the feature ships **DARK** behind `topicization_full_resume_enabled=False` (legacy monolithic path byte-for-byte unchanged). Remaining before the flag can be ENABLED: the **BUG-077** residual token-leak hardening (F1 circuit-breaker + F4 reconcile gating are MUST-before-enable — see the BUG-077 row above) + deploy + the controlled first exercise per [`POST_REFILL_WATCH_RUNBOOK_2026-06-30.md`](POST_REFILL_WATCH_RUNBOOK_2026-06-30.md). Design note: [`DESIGN_BUG076_CHECKPOINT_TOPICIZATION_2026-07-01.md`](DESIGN_BUG076_CHECKPOINT_TOPICIZATION_2026-07-01.md). Rollback ref `23764b7`. `main`. |
| **Component** | `topicization` — `tg_parser/processing/topicization.py` (`TopicizationPipelineImpl.topicize_channel` batch loop `:282-362`, `_merge_topics` `:570-725`, the single atomic persistence loop `:391-399`); `tg_parser/services/topicization_service.py` (`run_topicization` / `_topicize_channel_locked` `:367-523`, the `should_reescalate` 0-card→full trigger `:697`, its BUG-071 cooldown + crash-arm `:711-799`); `tg_parser/processing/llm/errors.py` (`AnthropicBillingError`, a direct `Exception` subclass `:4`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-07-01 — post-refill watch (`docs/notes/POST_REFILL_WATCH_RUNBOOK_2026-06-30.md`). After the Anthropic balance was refilled, the first legitimate `murashko_med` full re-topicization burned the balance in ~2h and ended with 0 persisted cards. The BUG-071..075 fixes all HELD (single escalation, cooldown armed, shrink-split, R1=0, reconcile bounded) — so the burn was PRODUCTIVE work, not a storm; yet it durably persisted nothing. This also produced the `TopicizationBurnNoProgress` false-positive (see observability row). |
| **Symptoms** | A long (~2h) full re-topicization of a cold-start 0-card channel spends millions of Sonnet tokens across hundreds of batches, then a single failure at the FINAL merge (billing exhaustion / timeout) ends the run with `stages_failed=['incremental_topicization'] outcome=degraded` and **0 topic cards written**. On the next tick the BUG-071 cooldown gate correctly suppresses an immediate re-storm — but the channel is still at 0 cards, so the trap is merely deferred, not escaped: the next unthrottled attempt (or a partial refill) re-runs from batch 1 and re-vaporizes. `tg_parser_topics_created_total` stays flat at 0 for the whole run. |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced)** | **Full topicization is all-or-nothing: cards persist ONLY at an atomic END-merge, after every batch has completed.** `topicize_channel` (`processing/topicization.py`) loads ALL docs into memory (`:261`), builds `candidates` for the whole corpus (`:270-280`), fans out ALL batches (`BATCH_SIZE=50`, `:283`) via `asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)` under a concurrency semaphore (`:337-340`) accumulating `all_batch_topics` **in memory** (`:342-354`), then calls `_merge_topics(all_batch_topics, candidates)` (`:356-357`) — a FINAL single LLM consolidation call. Only AFTER merge returns does Step 6 (`:391-399`) loop `topic_card_repo.upsert(card)` — the **one and only** persistence point. `_merge_topics`'s LLM call (`:632`) is guarded only by `except json.JSONDecodeError` and `except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError)` (`:667`, `:683`); `AnthropicBillingError` is a **direct `Exception` subclass** (`llm/errors.py:4`) → NOT caught → it propagates out of `_merge_topics` → out of `topicize_channel` → the Step 6 persistence loop at `:391` is **never reached** → every batch's work (all ~353 batches held in `all_batch_topics`) is discarded. **Not restartable:** `topicize_channel` holds no checkpoint state; a re-run reloads the full corpus and regenerates from batch 1 (the re-escalation calls `run_topicization(force=False)`, service `:762`, but with 0 cards there is nothing to skip). **Not fundable incrementally:** there is NO per-run/per-tick token budget cap anywhere in `settings.py` (only `topicization_batch_size=50`, `topicization_batch_concurrency=5`, `topicization_reconcile_max_docs=200`, `topicization_reescalation_cooldown_s=3600`, `scheduler_source_timeout_s=1800` — none is a token kill-switch), so a run cannot stop cleanly at a durable boundary when the balance is low. Cold-start 0-card channels are the worst case: they have the largest backlog, the highest merge cost, and (being at 0 cards) are exactly what the `should_reescalate` trigger (`topicization_service.py:697`) routes into the monolithic full run. |
| **Irony / the safe pattern already exists** | The BUG-075 incremental/reconcile path is the OPPOSITE of the full path and is already crash-safe: `_run_incremental_topicization_locked`'s batch loop persists **per batch** (`topicization_service.py:995-996` inline comment "Batch checkpoint: persist each successful batch immediately, so later-batch failures do not erase already discovered progress" → `_update_bundles_for_assignments` `:997` + `topic_card_repo.upsert(card)` `:1010` inside the loop), marks progress at-most-once via the `discover_attempted` synthetic marker (`:150-221`), caps per-tick work (`topicization_reconcile_max_docs`, `:1336-1339`), and converges over standing ticks losing nothing on a crash (`run_reconciliation_for_channel` `:1209+`). The fix is to bring the full path up to this same standard. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test crashes a multi-batch full run at `_merge_topics` (or between generate and persist) and asserts that already-generated batch topics are durably persisted / resumable. Existing BUG-071 tests cover truncation-drops and the re-escalation cooldown, but all assert on the RETURN of `topicize_channel`; none injects a mid-run `AnthropicBillingError` at the merge site and checks the persisted card count. The `_merge_topics` exception surface (`AnthropicBillingError` slipping past `except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError)`) is untested. **Closure (deferred to the fix):** a crash-mid-run → resume → cards-persist test under `TEST_POSTGRES=1`, a budget-cap-halts-cleanly test, a no-duplicate-cards-on-resume test, and a cold-start convergence test (see the design note test plan). |
| **Observability gap (root of the false-positive)** | `record_topic_created` (`api/metrics.py:681`) is called on the full path ONLY from the `run_topicization` wrapper (`topicization_service.py:463-466`), AFTER `topicize_channel` RETURNS. During the entire long run — and on a merge crash (no return) — `tg_parser_topics_created_total` is never incremented, so it reads flat 0 while Sonnet completion tokens climb → the `TopicizationBurnNoProgress` alert (`docker/prometheus/alerts.yml:343-353`) fires as a FALSE-POSITIVE on a legitimately-productive run. Compounding it: `tg_parser_topicization_failed_batches_total` documents "only `topicization_generate` is emitted today" (`api/metrics.py:147-148`), so a **merge**-stage crash is invisible to `TopicizationFailedBatchesHigh` too. What the full path DOES emit today: `tg_parser_llm_truncation_total{stage}`, `tg_parser_topicization_failed_batches_total{stage=topicization_generate}`, and token totals — but only on the success return dict. |
| **Current mitigation / workaround** | `murashko_med` preventively **paused** (`sources.status='paused'`) so the scheduler skips it (scheduler runs only `status='active'` sources) — this stops the trap from re-triggering until the fix lands. No durable code-level mitigation exists: the moment the channel is resumed with credit that cannot fund the whole run, the vaporization repeats. General mitigation: keep cold-start large-backlog 0-card channels paused until BUG-076 ships, or ensure the balance can fund the ENTIRE run before resuming. |
| **Proposed fix (FINAL — see design note)** | **Full multi-chunk resume** (decided 2026-07-01; hybrid "A-seed + reconcile-converge" considered and REJECTED for lower quality — reconcile is attempt-convergent, not coverage-complete). Chunk the corpus; per chunk generate → merge-within-chunk → **ATOMICALLY co-commit** the chunk's card upserts + a resumable checkpoint (synthetic `processing_failures` ref `topicization:full_checkpoint:<channel>`, no migration) in ONE transaction (atomicity is required because card ids are LLM-derived `make_topic_id(primary_anchor_ref)` and shift on re-run → a non-atomic partial chunk would duplicate cards). Add an **explicit checkpoint-driven resume trigger** in `_process_source` (mandatory: `should_reescalate` fires only at 0 cards, so after chunk 1 nothing else re-invokes the full path) with a **per-invocation chunk cap** (also the missing wall-clock bound — the 1800s watchdog does NOT wrap the topicization stage). Add a **per-run token-budget kill-switch** (coupled to the sequential-chunk refactor — a single `asyncio.gather` can't be interrupted) that halts cleanly at a chunk boundary. Add a **checkpointed, idempotent cross-chunk merge** for quality parity. Observability: wire per-chunk `record_topic_created` INTO the full path AND remove/guard the wrapper emit `:463-466` (else double-count); emit merge-stage `failed_batches`. Must NOT regress BUG-071..075 (`0x70C1`/`0x70C2` locks, cooldown+crash-arm, `reconcile_only`, `discover_attempted`, no-storm). Full detail + test plan in the design note. |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | All six mandatory pillars, behind additive settings whose defaults leave behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged (master switch `topicization_full_resume_enabled=False`). **(a) Resume driver** — `run_full_topicization_resume_for_channel` (`topicization_service.py`) wired into `_process_source` (`scheduler_service.py`) on EVERY tick, ordered BEFORE the BUG-075 reconcile hook, best-effort (never pollutes `stage_errors`, never crashes the tick). Gated on a live `topicization:full_checkpoint:<channel>` marker; a no-checkpoint / disabled call is a no-op (cold 0-card channels stay escalation's job → no double-drive); a live checkpoint drives ONE bounded `run_topicization(resume=True)` under `0x70C1`. **(b) Chunked full run** — `TopicizationPipelineImpl._topicize_channel_chunked`: corpus sorted by `source_ref` → 50-doc batches → `topicization_full_chunk_batches` batches/chunk; per chunk generate → merge-within-chunk → build cards → `_commit_chunk_atomically` co-commits (card upserts + bundle upserts + checkpoint advance) in ONE txn on the shared processing session (a real `AsyncSession` → `commit=False` staging + single `session.commit()`; no shared session → per-write commit fallback for mock/DI). Atomicity converts "partial chunk" → "chunk not started" (LLM-derived ids can't duplicate on resume). Bounded per invocation by `topicization_full_max_chunks_per_invocation`. **(c) Budget kill-switch** — `topicization_full_run_token_budget` (0=off) checked at chunk boundaries (pre- and post-commit); on trip: clean halt at the last durable boundary, `topicization_full_run_budget_halt` log, `..._budget_halt_total` metric, benign partial result — `failed_batches` NOT inflated. **(d) Cross-chunk merge** — `_finalize_full_run` (`topicization_service.py`): idempotent same-channel cosine+Jaccard consolidation (weights reused from `topic_linking_service`; dedicated higher threshold `topicization_full_merge_threshold=0.6` because it DELETES the loser) over the persisted card set once all chunks land; folds loser anchors into the lexicographically-lowest-id survivor, rebuilds the survivor bundle, deletes loser card+bundle, sets `final_merge_done`, then clears the checkpoint (crash between commit and clear → resume sees `final_merge_done=True` → clears, no re-merge). Re-run is a hard no-op. **(e) Observability** — per-chunk `record_topic_created` (once per persisted card) inside the atomic path; the wrapper emit at `topicization_service.py:463-466` is now GUARDED (`if not full_run_active`) so no double-count; a merge-stage billing/timeout halt records a `topicization_merge` failed batch. Four new metrics: `tg_parser_topicization_full_run_tokens_total`, `..._chunks{kind=done\|total}`, `..._budget_halt_total`, `..._resume_total`. **(f) No migration** — checkpoint is a synthetic `processing_failures` row (`topicization:full_checkpoint:<channel>`, `error_class=TopicizationFullCheckpoint`) carrying `{run_id, corpus_fingerprint, chunks_total, chunks_done, batches_done, tokens_spent_cumulative, final_merge_done, last_chunk_at}`; `attempts`=last completed chunk; cleared only on FULL completion; collision-safe with `tg:` doc refs and the BUG-071/075 markers. `AnthropicBillingError` + `LLMCallTimeoutError` caught at the merge site as clean resumable halts. New module `tg_parser/processing/topicization_checkpoint.py` (constants + `FullRunCheckpoint` + `parse_checkpoint` + `corpus_fingerprint`, dependency-light to avoid an import cycle). Repo commit-kwargs added (`topic_card_repo.upsert`/`delete_by_id`, `topic_bundle_repo.upsert`/`delete_by_topic_id`, `processing_failure_repo.record_failure`/`delete_failure`) — `ports.py` ABCs untouched (concrete SA repos add kwargs; mocks accept anything). Chosen defaults: `full_resume_enabled=False`, `full_chunk_batches=20` (~1000 docs/chunk), `full_max_chunks_per_invocation=1`, `full_run_token_budget=0`, `full_merge_threshold=0.6`. |
| **Tests (this session — NOT committed)** | `tests/test_bug076_checkpoint_topicization.py` — **20 non-PG tests PASS + 1 PG-gated SKIPPED** (no local Postgres): checkpoint collision-safety / roundtrip / graceful-degrade / fingerprint; chunked run bounded by max-chunks; crash-mid-run→resume→persist with NO duplicate cards; budget kill-switch clean halt (no failed-batch inflation, halt metric +1); merge `AnthropicBillingError` = clean resumable halt (chunk not committed, merge failed-batch recorded, no exception); per-chunk `record_topic_created` exactly once per card; stale-fingerprint fresh restart; cross-chunk merge dedup + idempotency; finalize no-op when `final_merge_done`; resume-driver gating (disabled / no-checkpoint no-op / drives `resume=True` / reports locked skip); wrapper skips `record_topic_created` on the full path + drives finalize; **(Bugbot F1) genuinely-empty chunk advances+converges vs empty-after-batch-failure does NOT advance; (Bugbot F2) stale-fingerprint restart clears prior-run cards/bundles**. PG-gated `test_atomic_chunk_no_duplicate_cards_on_resume_pg` (HIGHEST-RISK: simulated crash mid chunk-commit → only atomic chunk 0 persists → resume completes with no duplicate ids) is SKIPPED locally (set `TEST_POSTGRES=1` to run). Regression: `test_bug071..075` = **82 passed, 11 skipped** (PG-gated), no regressions. `ruff` clean on all edited files. |
| **Bugbot review round 1 — 2× HIGH FIXED (uncommitted)** | **F1 — empty chunk wrongly advanced the checkpoint.** The chunked path only halted-without-advancing when EVERY batch RAISED; a chunk whose batches succeeded but yielded no topics, or whose built cards were all quality-rejected, still ran `_commit_chunk_atomically` with an empty card list and bumped `chunks_done` — so a resume (and the 0-card `should_reescalate` path) permanently skipped that chunk even while the channel had 0 cards. **Fix** (`processing/topicization.py`): after building a chunk's cards, distinguish GENUINELY-empty (`chunk_failed == 0` — clean generate+merge, docs simply uncoverable / quality-rejected → **advance** with an empty card set so cold-start runs converge and terminate) from FAILED/HALTED-empty (`chunk_failed > 0` → **halt cleanly WITHOUT advancing**, resumable). Card-build exceptions (deterministic malformed output) are treated as genuine/advance to avoid a halt-loop; the BUG-075 reconcile hook re-covers those docs. Replaced the narrow "every batch failed" early-break with this correct post-build check. **F2 — stale-fingerprint restart left prior cards/bundles.** When `corpus_fingerprint` no longer matched, the stale-restart branch deleted ONLY the synthetic checkpoint row, so a fresh chunk-0 pass ran against the changed corpus with the prior partial run's cards still present (orphans/duplicates, since ids are LLM-derived and shift). **Fix**: the stale-restart branch now `delete_by_channel` on bundles + cards (mirroring force-mode reset) BEFORE clearing the checkpoint and restarting. Both fixes stay behind `topicization_full_resume_enabled=False`, preserve the atomic per-chunk commit discipline, no migration. **Tests added:** `test_genuinely_empty_chunk_advances_and_converges`, `test_empty_chunk_after_batch_failure_does_not_advance`, `test_stale_fingerprint_restart_clears_prior_run_cards`. |
| **Bugbot review round 2 — 1× HIGH + 2× MEDIUM + 1 test-harness FIXED (uncommitted)** | **F1 (HIGH) — active ingestion reset resume progress.** The old `corpus_fingerprint` (`count + max(processed_at)`) was recomputed from the LIVE corpus each resume; because the scheduler runs processing BEFORE the BUG-076 resume hook, a single new `ProcessedDocument` per tick changed the fingerprint → the stale branch `delete_by_channel`'d all partial-run cards+bundles and restarted at chunk 0 EVERY tick, so an active source could never accumulate multi-chunk progress. **Fix** (`processing/topicization.py` + `topicization_checkpoint.py`): a run now **pins its planned corpus** at start via a **watermark** = `max(processed_at)` (`plan_watermark`) + `planned_doc_count`. On resume the plan is rebuilt from ONLY the docs with `processed_at <= plan_watermark` (`frozen_corpus`), so docs ingested AFTER start (pure appends) are excluded and NEVER shift chunk boundaries or trigger a wipe — the run accumulates progress across ticks while the source keeps ingesting; the new docs are covered by the normal incremental/BUG-075 reconcile path (or a later full run). Only a genuine SHRINK of the frozen set below `planned_doc_count` (a planned doc deleted / re-processed past the watermark) is treated as material change → clean stale restart (with the F2 card-cleanup). **F3 (MEDIUM) — chunk plan not pinned.** Resume position was keyed on `chunks_done` recomputed against the LIVE `topicization_full_chunk_batches`; changing that setting between invocations re-interpreted `chunks_done` against a different partition (skipped/dropped batches or false "complete"). **Fix**: the checkpoint now stores `chunk_batches` and a resume rebuilds the partition with the PINNED span (the live setting only affects the NEXT fresh run) — non-orphaning, no restart needed. **F2 (MEDIUM) — partial run armed the re-escalation cooldown.** A 0-card chunked tick that durably advanced `chunks_done` was recorded as a failed escalation (`_arm_reescalation_marker`), suppressing the resume driver for the TTL. **Fix** (`services/topicization_service.py`): new `_has_live_full_checkpoint` — when a live (in-progress, not-`is_complete`) `topicization:full_checkpoint:` marker exists, a 0-card return is PARTIAL PROGRESS → do NOT arm (and do NOT clear); with NO live checkpoint the original BUG-071 arm-on-0-cards behavior is preserved. **F4 (test-harness) — PG atomicity test failed pre-assertion.** `_make_pipeline` passed no `model_id`, so `self.model_id` was an `AsyncMock` and the real PG bundle repo's `stable_json_dumps(metadata)` raised `TypeError` at chunk-0 upsert. **Fix**: pass `model_id="test-model"`. **Semantics doc**: appends after run start are ignored by the plan (steady-state paths handle them); deletions/reprocessing that shrink the planned set trigger a clean restart; the chunk-batch span is immutable for the life of a run. ### BUG-073 — Processing stage + incremental-topicization stage lack a cross-entrypoint per-channel lock → concurrent scheduler/dispatch/CLI runs re-burn the same docs (F1 + F3)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High** (token-burn / cost). Residual concurrency gaps surfaced while landing BUG-072 (which only guarded the FULL-topicization funnel). Two distinct re-burn classes: **F1** — a scheduled tick + a manual `trigger_pipeline` for the SAME channel run `run_processing` concurrently, sending up to `processing_tick_batch_size` (300) raw messages to Sonnet TWICE; **F3** — a CLI `run_incremental_topicization_for_uncovered` (entire uncovered backlog, NOT tick-local) runs Phase-2 LLM discover concurrently with another incremental run, double-billing the same docs. |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (F1 + F3 advisory-lock fixes + tests — committed [`bbd7c35`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/bbd7c35) «fix(pipeline): per-channel advisory locks for processing + incremental topicization (BUG-073)» and deployed to prod; LIVE at prod HEAD `e0f517d`. The uncovered-coverage reconciliation subsystem was DESCOPED to BUG-075 and removed before this ship — see the DESCOPED row below). |
| **Component** | `processing` / `topicization` — `tg_parser/services/processing_service.py` (`run_processing` funnel + new `channel_pipeline_lock` / `_locked_skip_processing_result` / `_run_processing_locked`); `tg_parser/services/topicization_service.py` (`run_incremental_topicization` wrapper + new `channel_incremental_topicization_lock` / `_run_incremental_topicization_locked`); shared helper `tg_parser/services/advisory_lock.py` (`channel_advisory_lock`). Entry paths funnelled: `pipeline_service.py` (`run_full_pipeline` → `run_processing`), `pipeline_dispatch_service.py` (`full_pipeline` job), `scheduler_service.py` (`_process_source` → `run_full_pipeline` → `run_processing`; + `run_incremental_topicization`), and the CLI `tg-parser run` / `tg-parser process` / `tg-parser topicize` processes. |
| **Discovered** | 2026-06-28 — read-only token-burn hardening review on top of the BUG-071/072 work. The BUG-072 lock only covered FULL topicization; the processing stage (F1) and the incremental Phase-1/2 stage (F3) had no cross-process per-channel guard. |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced)** | **F1:** the scheduler tick (`run_incremental_for_all_sources` → `run_full_pipeline(skip_topicize=True)`) takes ONLY `SCHEDULER_SOURCE_LOCK_NS=0x5C40` (scheduler-only, keyed by `source_id`); a dispatched `full_pipeline` job or a CLI `tg-parser run`/`process` takes NEITHER `0x5C40` NOR the in-process-only `_running_channel_jobs` set in `pipeline_dispatch_service.py`. The only remaining dedup is a load-time `processed_doc_repo.exists()` evaluated before either run persists (TOCTOU). **F3:** `run_incremental_topicization` only entered an advisory lock via the BUG-072 re-escalation sub-call (full lock 0x70C1); the normal Phase-1/2 path was unlocked, and `run_incremental_topicization_for_uncovered` (CLI) was fully unlocked. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test ran two concurrent processing/incremental runs for the same channel asserting the second is skipped/deferred, and no guard existed. **Closure:** `tests/test_bug073_pipeline_concurrency.py` — (non-PG) namespaces are distinct (0x9C40 / 0x70C2 vs 0x5C40 / 0x70C1); both locks degrade to "acquired" with no DB; the processing skip sentinel is caller-compatible; `run_processing` returns the sentinel WITHOUT running the inner body when the lock is held and runs it when acquired; the incremental backlog-fill (defer) skips the inner body on contention while the scheduler tick PROCEEDS anyway (no abandonment); (PG-gated `TEST_POSTGRES=1`) a second concurrent acquire on the same channel is refused, a different channel is not blocked, the lock releases on exit, the scheduler/dispatch/CLI paths contend on the SAME normalized key (`chx`/`@chx`), the incremental lock is DISTINCT from the full lock (a held full lock does NOT block the incremental tick → no abandonment), and incremental-vs-incremental mutually exclude (backlog defers, tick proceeds). |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | **F1 — per-channel processing advisory lock.** New reusable `channel_advisory_lock(channel_id, *, namespace, engine_attr, label)` (`advisory_lock.py`) generalising the proven `_source_processing_lock`/`channel_topicization_lock` pattern (session-scoped `pg_try_advisory_lock` on a DEDICATED connection, unlock+close in `finally`, degrade-to-acquired with no DB). `channel_pipeline_lock` (`processing_service.py:50`) pins namespace **`PIPELINE_LOCK_NS = 0x9C40`** (`:47`) + the `processing_storage_engine` (the engine `run_processing` already uses → all contenders share one DB → the lock is mutually visible). `run_processing` (`:102`) is now a thin wrapper: on contention it logs `processing_run_skipped_already_in_flight` and returns `_locked_skip_processing_result()` (`:68`, a zeroed stats dict shaped like a real "no work" return: `processed_count`/`failed_count`/`total_tokens` for `run_full_pipeline`; `total_count`/`skipped_count`/`raw_total_count`/`attempted_count`/`billing_blocked_count` for the scheduler; `skipped_locked=True`); the real body moved verbatim into `_run_processing_locked` (`:153`). A processing skip is SAFE (the lock-holder works the same bounded backlog; anything unreached stays unprocessed for the next tick — no abandonment, unlike tick-local topicization). All three entry paths funnel through `run_processing` keyed by `hashtext(normalize_channel_id(channel_id))`, so scheduler + dispatch + CLI mutually exclude per channel. **F3 — incremental topicization advisory lock in a SEPARATE namespace.** `channel_incremental_topicization_lock` (`topicization_service.py:142`) under **`INCREMENTAL_TOPICIZATION_LOCK_NS = 0x70C2`** (`:139`) — DISTINCT from the full lock 0x70C1 ON PURPOSE: it must contend incremental-vs-incremental (stop the CLI backlog-fill double-billing Phase-2) but NOT incremental-vs-full (so the BUG-072 re-escalation fall-through keeps covering the tick's `new_doc_refs`; the nested re-escalation `run_topicization` still takes 0x70C1 independently → no self-deadlock). `run_incremental_topicization` (`:427`) is now a thin wrapper around `_run_incremental_topicization_locked` (`:493`) with a `defer_if_locked` flag: the CLI backlog-fill (`run_incremental_topicization_for_uncovered`, `:929`) passes `defer_if_locked=True` → BENIGN skip on contention (uncovered set recomputed next run → not abandoned); the scheduler tick path (default `defer_if_locked=False`) NEVER skips — it acquires when free (excluding a concurrent backlog-fill) but PROCEEDS on contention so its TICK-LOCAL new docs are never abandoned (bounded duplicate work, strictly cheaper than abandonment — mirrors the BUG-072 fall-through philosophy). |
| **No-abandonment proof (F3)** | The dangerous scenario is the BUG-072 one: a long full run holding 0x70C1 + a scheduler tick with new docs. Because the incremental lock is a SEPARATE namespace (0x70C2), the full run does NOT block the tick's incremental — it acquires, runs Phase 1/2, and covers the new docs (`tests/test_bug073_pipeline_concurrency.py::test_full_run_in_flight_does_not_abandon_incremental_tick`). The only contention for the incremental lock is incremental-vs-incremental; there the backlog-fill (idempotent, recomputed) defers while the tick-local path proceeds unconditionally — so no doc is ever permanently abandoned (`::test_incremental_vs_incremental_mutually_exclude`). |
| **Self-review (deadlock / leak / caller-compat / abandonment)** | **Deadlock:** a scheduler tick can transiently hold `0x5C40` (ingestion engine, source_id) + `0x9C40` (processing engine, channel_id) + `0x70C2` (processing engine, channel_id) sequentially-nested, plus the re-escalation's `0x70C1` — ALL are non-blocking `pg_try_advisory_lock` (return immediately, never wait), DIFFERENT namespaces/keys/connections, so no lock-ordering cycle is possible. **Leak:** the dedicated connection is unlocked (guarded by `acquired` + its own `try/except`) and closed in `finally`; the degraded no-DB path takes no connection. **Caller-compat:** the processing skip sentinel keys verified against `run_full_pipeline` (direct reads) + scheduler (`.get`) + dispatch (ignores return); the incremental defer returns a default `IncrementalTopicizeResult`. **Abandonment:** see the dedicated proof row. **No migration:** advisory locks are runtime-only. |
| **Follow-up — Bugbot finding "Defer skip masks pending backlog" (medium; this WIP NOT committed)** | **Finding:** the F3 backlog-fill defer (`run_incremental_topicization` with `defer_if_locked=True`) returned a DEFAULT empty `IncrementalTopicizeResult` with no indicator. Since `run_incremental_topicization_for_uncovered` had already confirmed uncovered refs exist, the CLI then printed a green "✅ завершён, 0 assigned / 0% coverage" — an operator could wrongly believe the backlog was handled. **Fix (uncommitted):** added a typed `deferred_locked: bool = False` field to `IncrementalTopicizeResult` (`tg_parser/domain/models.py:367`; mirrors the `skipped_locked` dict-sentinel convention). The defer branch now returns `IncrementalTopicizeResult(deferred_locked=True)` (`topicization_service.py:481`); it propagates unchanged through `run_incremental_topicization_for_uncovered` to the CLI. `_print_incremental_stats` (`tg_parser/cli/app.py:595`) checks it FIRST and prints a DISTINCT, clearly-worded "⏭️ deferred — another topicization run holds the channel lock; uncovered backlog was NOT processed this run; it will be retried on the next run" line instead of the success banner. A defer is benign/expected, so it is NOT a hard error / non-zero exit (no crash) — just a prominent line. The scheduler tick path (`defer_if_locked=False`) never defers, so `deferred_locked` stays `False` there; the BUG-071 Fix-2 cooldown marker is untouched on the defer (the branch returns before any marker code). All other `IncrementalTopicizeResult` constructors/consumers are unaffected (new field defaults `False`). **Tests:** `tests/test_bug073_pipeline_concurrency.py` — `test_incremental_defer_skips_inner_when_lock_held` asserts `deferred_locked is True` on the defer (inner not run); `test_incremental_tick_proceeds_despite_contention` asserts a proceeding run is `False`; `test_uncovered_backlog_fill_propagates_deferred_locked` proves the CLI uncovered path propagates the flag when uncovered refs exist; `test_cli_reports_deferred_outcome_distinctly` asserts the CLI prints the deferred line (not the success banner) for a deferred result and the success banner for a normal one. |
| **Follow-up — 2nd Bugbot pass: "Contended incremental holds idle DB connection" (MEDIUM) — KEPT** | On the proceed-without-lock branch (`defer_if_locked=False` + contention) `_run_incremental_topicization_locked` previously ran INSIDE the `async with channel_incremental_topicization_lock(...)`, so the dedicated advisory-lock connection stayed checked out of the pool for the WHOLE Phase 1/2 LLM run even though no lock was held. **Fix (uncommitted):** `run_incremental_topicization` (`topicization_service.py`) now branches inside the lock context — the acquired branch returns the run INSIDE the context so the lock is HELD for the run's duration, the defer branch returns `deferred_locked=True` inside, and ONLY the proceed-without-lock branch falls OUT of the `async with` (releasing the connection) before running `_run()`. Degrade-to-acquired (no DB) takes no connection anyway, so its behaviour is unchanged. **Proof:** `tests/test_bug073_pipeline_concurrency.py::test_incremental_proceed_without_lock_releases_connection_before_run` (spy lock CM: the inner body observes the context CLOSED) + `::test_incremental_acquired_holds_connection_during_run` (acquired path keeps it OPEN during the run). |
| **Follow-up — Bugbot finding "Multi-agent processing bypasses F1 lock" (MEDIUM) — FIXED** | **Finding:** F1 wrapped only `run_processing` in `channel_pipeline_lock` (0x9C40), but `run_multi_agent_processing` (CLI `tg-parser process --multi-agent`) is ALSO a live per-channel processing funnel — it loads + LLM-processes the same bounded backlog — and took NO lock. A concurrent scheduler tick / dispatch job / normal `run_processing` could hold the per-channel lock while a multi-agent run double-processed the SAME backlog → the exact TOCTOU double-billing F1 prevents. **Fix (uncommitted):** `run_multi_agent_processing` (`tg_parser/services/processing_service.py:486`) is now a thin wrapper that takes the SAME `channel_pipeline_lock(channel_id)` (`PIPELINE_LOCK_NS = 0x9C40`, keyed by `hashtext(normalize_channel_id(channel_id))` — IDENTICAL to `run_processing`, so the two funnels mutually exclude per channel); the real body moved verbatim into `_run_multi_agent_processing_locked` (`:538`). On contention it logs `multi_agent_processing_run_skipped_already_in_flight` and returns the SAME `_locked_skip_processing_result()` sentinel (caller-compatible: the CLI `process` command reads `processed_count`/`skipped_count`/`failed_count`/`total_count`/`total_tokens`, all present in the sentinel). The CLI (`tg_parser/cli/app.py`) now checks `stats.get("skipped_locked")` FIRST and prints a DISTINCT "⏭️ Processing пропущен — другой процесс уже обрабатывает этот канал" line instead of the "✅ завершён" success banner (so a skip is not misread as a successful no-op) for BOTH the multi-agent and normal paths. The same BUG-075 benign-skip abandonment caveat comment is carried at the multi-agent skip site. **Tests:** `tests/test_bug073_pipeline_concurrency.py::test_run_multi_agent_processing_returns_sentinel_when_lock_held` (held lock → sentinel, inner not run), `::test_run_multi_agent_processing_runs_inner_when_lock_acquired` (acquired → delegates), and PG-gated `::test_multi_agent_contends_with_run_processing_on_same_key` (a held `channel_pipeline_lock` skips multi-agent for the SAME channel + a normalized alias, while a DIFFERENT channel runs). Both processing funnels (`run_processing` + `run_multi_agent_processing`) are now F1-locked. |
| **Follow-up — Bugbot finding "F1 skip sentinel mis-reported as success across consumers" (2× MEDIUM) — FIXED comprehensively** | **Finding:** the F1 `skipped_locked` processing sentinel was produced but not surfaced/handled in every consumer, so a benign lock-skip looked like a successful run: (1) CLI `run` never checked it → printed "Pipeline завершён успешно!" and `run_full_pipeline` proceeded to topicization/export on stale state; (2) the API background job (`process.py`) set `JobStatus.COMPLETED` + `status="completed"` webhook with 0 processed as if work happened. **Enumerated EVERY processing-result consumer** (`run_processing` / `run_multi_agent_processing` / `run_full_pipeline` / the stats dict): CLI `process` + `process --multi-agent` (already done last round), CLI `run` (`app.py`), CLI `scheduler run-once --source` (`scheduler_cmd.py`), API job `_run_processing_job` (`api/routes/process.py`), `run_full_pipeline` itself (`pipeline_service.py`), scheduler `_process_source` (`scheduler_service.py`) + `run_incremental_for_source` (benign passthrough to the CLI), dispatch `full_pipeline` job (`pipeline_dispatch_service.py`); the topicization 0x70C1 `skipped_locked` at `topicization_service.py:710` is a SEPARATE sentinel (out of scope). **Fixes (uncommitted), each making a skip a DISTINCT benign (non-success, non-error) outcome:** (a) **`run_full_pipeline` short-circuit** (`pipeline_service.py`, processing block): when `process_stats.get("skipped_locked")` it sets top-level `stats["skipped_locked"]=True`, SKIPS topicization/export (another run owns the channel end-to-end; topicization has its own 0x70C1 lock so this is purely about not doing useless work / not reporting false success) and returns the benign skip. (b) **CLI `run`** prints a distinct "⏭️ Pipeline пропущен" line + returns instead of the success banner. (c) **CLI `scheduler run-once --source`** prints a distinct skip line + returns. (d) **API job** keeps terminal `COMPLETED` (a skip is not an error; deliberately NO new `JobStatus` enum value) but annotates `job.result` with `skipped_locked` + a clear `message`, sets `job.progress["skipped_locked"]`, and emits the webhook with `status="skipped"` (not `"completed"`) carrying the flag. (e) **scheduler `_process_source`** records only `ingest` in `stages_ok` on a lock-skip (NOT `process`/`export`) and logs `source_processing_skipped_lock_held`; the downstream new_doc_refs incremental naturally no-ops (0 new docs), and the degraded-ratio check no-ops (attempted=0) — benign, not a failed stage. (f) **dispatch `full_pipeline`** captures the result, records `result="skipped"` (not `success`/`failed`), logs `pipeline_trigger_skipped_lock_held`, and SKIPS the embedding step. A skip never crashes, is never counted as a failed stage / error metric, and never looks like a successful full run. **Tests (`tests/test_bug073_pipeline_concurrency.py`):** `test_run_full_pipeline_short_circuits_on_processing_skip` (topicize/export NOT awaited + `skipped_locked` returned), `test_cli_run_reports_processing_skip_distinctly` (distinct line, no success banner), `test_api_processing_job_represents_lock_skip_distinctly` (COMPLETED + result/progress `skipped_locked` + webhook `status="skipped"`), `test_dispatch_full_pipeline_records_skip_distinctly` (metric `skipped`, embedding not run). |
| **DESCOPED to BUG-075 — uncovered-coverage reconciliation (HIGH abandonment-recovery; REMOVED from this ship)** | The 2nd Bugbot pass also raised a HIGH "Processing lock skip abandons incremental topicization": with F1's benign processing skip, a scheduler tick's TICK-LOCAL `new_doc_refs` may not include docs the lock-holder persists, and a processing-only / `skip_topicize` holder never topicizes them → processed-but-untopicized. Three successive attempts to close this with a per-tick recovery (skip-locked recovery hook → standing reconciliation + per-doc `discover_attempted` idempotency marker → generalised marker invariant) each drew a further HIGH Bugbot finding, culminating in the discovery that **any** reconciliation that calls `run_incremental_topicization` can itself trigger the BUG-071 zero-card FULL re-escalation on quiet ticks — reintroducing the very token-burn this work is meant to fix. **Decision (2026-06-28):** the entire reconciliation subsystem (scheduler hook, the `topicization:discover_attempted:<ref>` marker infra, the `reconcile`/`max_docs`/`mark_unassignable` plumbing) was REMOVED; the scheduler reverts to its baseline tick-local incremental behaviour and **F1+F3+F2 ship alone**. The coverage-convergence work — and the now-slightly-WIDENED but pre-existing tick-local abandonment window — is deferred to **BUG-075** with a full design handoff (`docs/notes/START_PROMPT_SESSION_BUG075_TOPICIZATION_COVERAGE_RECONCILIATION_2026-06-28.md`, capturing the 5 hard-won design learnings). F1's skip site carries an inline `BUG-075` caveat comment (`processing_service.py`, `run_processing` lock-contention branch). The narrow gap is acceptable for this ship: it is essentially the pre-existing scheduler property and the common holders (dispatch `full_pipeline` / scheduler tick) topicize their own docs. |
| **Workaround** | None durable pre-fix; avoid manual `trigger_pipeline` / CLI `process` / `topicize uncovered` while a scheduler tick could process the same channel. |
| **Artifacts** | Tests: `tests/test_bug073_pipeline_concurrency.py` (F1 + F3 lock layers + the defer-observability + connection-release follow-ups). Namespace map: `0x5C40` scheduler source, `0x70C1` full topicization, `0x70C2` incremental topicization (F3), `0x9C40` processing (F1). The uncovered-coverage reconciliation + per-doc idempotency marker were descoped to BUG-075 (see the DESCOPED row above). |
| **Linked** | BUG-072 (the full-topicization lock this extends to the processing + incremental stages; same token-burn class); BUG-068 Fix 4 / BUG-070 (the `_source_processing_lock` session-advisory-lock-on-dedicated-connection pattern generalised into `channel_advisory_lock`); BUG-074 (the JSON-repair token-burn fix landed in the same hardening pass); BUG-069 (the bounded processing window the F1 skip leaves intact for the next tick). |

### BUG-075 — Topicization coverage is tick-local → processed-but-never-topicized docs stay permanently uncovered (convergent coverage reconciliation)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High** (correctness — silent permanent abandonment of processed docs; AND token-burn — the naïve fix re-burns Sonnet). Carved out of the BUG-073 F1+F3 ship (DESCOPED row above). Coverage is tick-local: the scheduler feeds ONLY each tick's `docs_after − docs_before` to `run_incremental_topicization`, so a doc persisted by a path that never topicizes it (CLI `process`, a `skip_topicize` run, a crash between processing/topicization, or the F1 lock-skip widening) is never in any tick's `new_doc_refs` and never becomes covered. |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (design + fix + tests + observability follow-ups — committed on `main`: [`c99b4b5`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/c99b4b5) «fix(topicization): convergent coverage reconciliation hook (BUG-075)», [`73d9a58`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/73d9a58) «fix(topicization): observability for discover_attempted marker-write failures + R3 won't-fix note (BUG-075)», [`b7285d7`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/b7285d7) «feat(observability): reconcile-discover counter + post-refill monitoring package (BUG-075)»). Built per the binding start-prompt `docs/notes/START_PROMPT_SESSION_BUG075_TOPICIZATION_COVERAGE_RECONCILIATION_2026-06-28.md` against prod HEAD `e0f517d`. |
| **Component** | `topicization` / `scheduler` / `config` — `tg_parser/services/topicization_service.py` (new `run_reconciliation_for_channel` standing hook + `discover_attempted` marker helpers + `reconcile_only` flag threaded through `run_incremental_topicization` → `_run_incremental_topicization_locked`); `tg_parser/services/scheduler_service.py` (`_process_source` per-tick reconciliation hook, mirroring the F5-C / F11 hook contract); `tg_parser/config/settings.py` (`topicization_reconcile_max_docs`, default 200). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-06-28 — HIGH "Processing lock skip abandons incremental topicization" surfaced during the BUG-073 F1+F3 token-burn hardening; the reconciliation subsystem was descoped (it kept re-drawing HIGH findings, each a new constraint) and re-designed deliberately here. |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced)** | `scheduler_service._process_source` derives `new_doc_refs` from a single per-tick `docs_after − docs_before` snapshot (`:496-500`) and feeds only those to `run_incremental_topicization`. There is NO standing recovery for docs that are PROCESSED (`processed_documents`) but never COVERED (in a `topic_bundle`). F1's benign processing skip slightly WIDENS this pre-existing window. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test exercised a processed-but-uncovered doc converging without manual intervention, nor asserted the no-re-burn / no-storm invariants. **Closure:** `tests/test_bug075_topicization_reconciliation.py` (non-PG: flag threading, candidate selection `uncovered − attempted`, the `unassigned_refs − covered_after` marker invariant incl. the raised-batch-not-marked case, no-storm on a 0-card channel, no-re-burn steady state, defer-is-retried, candidate-session-closed-before-LLM-run, and the source-level hook contract; PG-gated `TEST_POSTGRES=1`: the real `0x70C2` defer-on-contention). |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | A **STANDING per-channel reconciliation hook** in `_process_source` (runs on EVERY tick, after the F11 watchlist hook; never pollutes `stage_errors`, never crashes the tick — a failure, INCLUDING billing, is a silent `logger.exception`). It calls `run_reconciliation_for_channel` (`topicization_service.py`): (1) computes candidates = uncovered (`processed − covered`) MINUS docs carrying a `discover_attempted` marker, in a SHORT-LIVED repo session that is CLOSED before the LLM run (learning 4); (2) caps the feed at `settings.topicization_reconcile_max_docs` (default 200) so one tick stays under the `scheduler_source_timeout_s = 1800` watchdog (backlog drains over multiple standing ticks); (3) feeds the slice to `run_incremental_topicization` with **`reconcile_only=True`** (forces `should_reescalate=False` in `_run_incremental_topicization_locked` — learning 5, NEVER a full re-escalation, BUG-071 cooldown marker untouched) and `defer_if_locked=True` (reuses the `0x70C2` incremental lock; a defer is retried next tick — learning 1; NEVER takes `0x70C1` / never calls `run_topicization`). After a COMPLETED Phase 2, `_run_incremental_topicization_locked` marks `unassigned_refs − covered_after` (docs sent to Phase-2 discover that did not become covered; EXCLUDES Phase-1 keyword-assigned docs) so each uncovered doc consumes AT MOST ONE discover call ever → steady-state cost ~0 (learnings 2/3); a discover batch that RAISES propagates before the marker write, so its docs stay unmarked and retry next pass. |
| **Marker storage decision** | **Synthetic `processing_failures` ref `topicization:discover_attempted:<source_ref>` — NO migration** (the same pattern as the BUG-071 `_reescalation_marker_ref`). Collision-safe: a real doc ref is `tg:<channel>:<type>:<id>` and the per-tick processing skip (`pipeline._should_skip_failed`) matches the REAL ref, so a `topicization:discover_attempted:…` row is loaded into `failure_map` but NEVER matched → it can NEVER cause a doc to be skipped from PROCESSING. **Trade-off (Bugbot may flag):** unlike BUG-071 (one row/channel) this writes one row PER uncovered-after-discover doc, modestly inflating the per-tick `failure_map` load and CLI failure reports for channels with a large perpetually-unassignable set; chosen over a dedicated column/table to keep deploy a NO-OP (no migration) and reuse the proven pattern, per the start-prompt default. |
| **New / changed signatures** | `run_incremental_topicization(..., reconcile_only: bool = False, ...)` and `_run_incremental_topicization_locked(..., reconcile_only: bool = False, ...)` (default `False` → byte-for-byte unchanged for all existing callers — scheduler tick + CLI backlog-fill). New `run_reconciliation_for_channel(*, channel_id, max_docs=None, cross_channel=None, processed_repo=None, topic_card_repo=None, topic_bundle_repo=None, failure_repo=None) -> dict`. New setting `topicization_reconcile_max_docs: int = 200` (`ge=0`, 0 disables the cap). |
| **Accepted trade-off** | At-most-one discover attempt per doc: a doc unassignable at attempt time is NOT retried later even if new topics would now fit it. Strictly better than the current tick-local behaviour (which gives missed docs ZERO attempts) and bounds steady-state cost to ~0. A future "retry when the card set materially changed" must be an explicit, bounded, separately-designed trigger (e.g. invalidate `discover_attempted` on a full re-topicization), NOT an unconditional sweep. |
| **Follow-up — Bugbot medium "Capped reconcile can starve tail backlog" — FIXED** | **Finding:** the hook fed `candidates[:max_docs]` in stable `source_ref` order. A candidate can stay uncovered WITHOUT earning a `discover_attempted` marker — markers cover only Phase-2 `unassigned_refs`, so a keyword-assigned-but-bundle-write-failed doc (in `assignments`, never in `unassigned_refs`) or a doc whose discover batch RAISED (a non-completed attempt, intentionally retried) is uncovered+unmarked. Under the stable cap such a doc permanently occupies the head and the TAIL of a backlog > `max_docs` would NEVER be reconciled (a convergence gap contra the DoD). The 0-card case itself is NOT the gap (with `reconcile_only=True`, Phase-2 still runs and marks unassignable docs → they converge); the gap is purely the stable-order + cap interaction with unmarkable docs. **Fix (uncommitted):** when `len(candidates) > max_docs`, feed a UNIFORM RANDOM sample (`_RECONCILE_RNG.sample(candidates, max_docs)`; module-level RNG so tests patch a seeded `random.Random`) instead of the stable head — every candidate gets a fair chance each tick so the tail converges. This preserves "at-most-one COMPLETED discover per doc, ever": a doc that completes a discover is marked → leaves `candidates` permanently; the only re-fed docs are ones that did NOT complete a discover (keyword-only docs cost 0 LLM; raised-batch docs are the intended learning-3 retry) → no re-burn, L2/L3 intact, L5 untouched (`run_topicization` / `0x70C1` never reached). **Test:** `tests/test_bug075_topicization_reconciliation.py::test_capped_backlog_does_not_starve_tail_under_unmarkable_head` (backlog 5 > cap 2, 2 perpetually-unmarkable head docs + 3 markable tail docs; asserts every tail doc is eventually fed and each consumes exactly one discover). Convergence now holds for the capped-backlog + unmarkable-head case (almost-surely fair across ticks); the happy path still converges deterministically via the marker in `ceil(backlog / max_docs)` ticks. |
| **Follow-up — token-burn audit R1 "marker-write failure was invisible" — observability hardening (uncommitted)** | **Finding (R1, optional):** `_mark_discover_attempted` swallows marker-write errors (a hiccup must never mask the caller's outcome). But if the marker write fails PERSISTENTLY while the discover LLM call SUCCEEDS, the doc stays unmarked → re-fed to Phase-2 next tick → **bounded re-burn** (capped by `topicization_reconcile_max_docs=200` + the random anti-starvation sampling, so NOT a storm, NOT abandonment) — and it was only visible at `logger.debug`, i.e. effectively invisible. **Change (observability ONLY — loop behaviour UNCHANGED: cap, sampling, marker semantics, `reconcile_only` all identical):** the marker-write failure path in `_mark_discover_attempted` now (1) logs at **`warning`** (it is the only quiet path to bounded re-burn → genuinely actionable) and (2) increments a new Prometheus counter `tg_parser_topicization_discover_attempted_mark_failed_total{channel_id}` (defined in `tg_parser/api/metrics.py` next to `tg_parser_topicization_failed_batches_total`, same `channel_id` cardinality convention; emitted via `record_discover_attempted_mark_failed`). Still strictly best-effort — the metric emit is itself `contextlib.suppress`-wrapped so the marker loop / reconcile hook can NEVER crash the tick or pollute `stage_errors`. Degrades to bounded re-feed, never to abandonment/unbounded burn. Kept as a sub-note under BUG-075 (no new ENH/BUG id — pure observability follow-up on the same fix). **Test:** `tests/test_bug075_topicization_reconciliation.py::test_mark_discover_attempted_failure_emits_metric_warns_and_does_not_crash` (forced `record_failure` raise: asserts +1 counter per failed ref, a `warning` log, and no exception) + `…::test_mark_discover_attempted_success_does_not_emit_failure_metric` (control). **Deploy note:** the metric only appears in prod after a deploy. |
| **Follow-up — token-burn audit R3 "reconcile discover passes `cross_channel=True`" — accepted / won't-fix** | **Finding (R3):** the reconcile path passes `cross_channel=True` (the uniform default) into discover, raising the question of whether reconcile-triggered discover should disable cross-channel work to save tokens. **Decision: leave as-is (won't-fix).** Rationale: (1) Phase-3 cross-channel linking is embedding/cosine + Jaccard, **NOT** an LLM call — disabling it saves **zero** LLM tokens; (2) the only real token cost (unbounded cross-channel topic-card context in the discover prompt) occurs only on transient backlog-drain ticks and is ~zero in steady state, because reconcile short-circuits before discover via the at-most-one-discover marker; (3) there is a minor correctness/latency nuance — cards created by reconcile discover would lose their per-tick cross-links, recoverable only via the manual/cron full `link_topics` — so flipping it is **not** strictly loss-free; (4) `cross_channel=True` is the uniform default across settings / normal-tick / CLI, so flipping only the reconcile path adds inconsistency. **Net:** low upside vs small real downside → accepted/won't-fix. Kept as a sub-note under BUG-075 (no new ENH/BUG id — audit disposition on the same fix). |
| **Workaround** | Pre-fix: manually run `tg-parser topicize uncovered` (CLI `run_incremental_topicization_for_uncovered`) — but that is manual (not convergent) and, on a 0-card channel, goes through the re-escalation path (NOT safe unattended). The BUG-075 hook supersedes it for the convergent case. |
| **Artifacts** | Tests: `tests/test_bug075_topicization_reconciliation.py` (21 tests green incl. PG-gated with `TEST_POSTGRES=1` and the anti-starvation follow-up; full regression across `test_incremental_topicization` / `test_scheduler_service` / `test_f11_scheduler_hook` / `test_f5c_scheduler_hook` / `test_bug071*` / `test_bug072*` / `test_bug073*` / `test_bug074*` — 158 passed, no regressions). Namespace map unchanged (`0x5C40` / `0x70C1` / `0x70C2` / `0x9C40` all distinct, all non-blocking try-locks). No migration. |
| **Linked** | BUG-073 (the DESCOPED row above — F1+F3 shipped without this; F1's skip site carries the `BUG-075` caveat comment); BUG-071 (the zero-card full re-escalation path `reconcile_only` HARD-DISABLES — learning 5 — and the `_reescalation_marker_ref` synthetic-ref pattern this reuses); BUG-072 (the `0x70C1` full lock reconciliation must NEVER take); BUG-074 (JSON-repair, same hardening lineage). |
