### BUG-074 — Topicization JSON-parse retries re-burn the full batch up to 3× and never call `repair_json` (F2)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High/Medium** (token-burn / cost). On an HTTP-200 reply with `stop_reason != "max_tokens"` but invalid JSON (the BUG-065 class — unescaped inner quotes / trailing commas), the three large-prompt topicization stages looped up to `max_json_retries = 3` RE-ISSUING the entire oversized prompt and NEVER called the cheap deterministic `repair_json` the per-message processing path already uses. |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (F2 fix + tests — committed [`e0f517d`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/e0f517d) «fix(topicization): repair malformed JSON instead of re-issuing the batch (BUG-074)» and deployed to prod; LIVE at prod HEAD `e0f517d`). |
| **Component** | `topicization` — `tg_parser/processing/topicization.py` (`_generate_topics_batch`, `_merge_topics`, `_discover_single_batch`; new helper `_loads_topicization_json_with_repair` + constant `_TOPICIZATION_MAX_JSON_RETRIES`). Reuses `tg_parser/processing/pipeline.py::repair_json` (BUG-065). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-06-28 — read-only token-burn hardening review. The per-message path (`pipeline.py`) repairs invalid JSON in place before counting an attempt failed; the three topicization parse sites did not. |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced)** | At each of the three parse sites the recovery was `json.loads(cleaned)` inside a `for attempt in range(1, max_json_retries+1)` loop whose `except json.JSONDecodeError` branch re-issued the identical large prompt (charged Sonnet call) up to 3× before giving up — with no `repair_json` pass. The BUG-065 unescaped-quote class is deterministically repairable, so every one of those re-issues was avoidable spend. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test fed an invalid-but-repairable JSON reply to the topicization stages and asserted the prompt is NOT re-issued. **Closure:** `tests/test_bug074_topicization_json_repair.py` — a trailing-comma reply is repaired + parsed on the FIRST attempt for all three stages (generate/merge/discover) with `generate_with_usage` called exactly ONCE; a genuinely unrepairable reply still fails gracefully after the REDUCED cap (2, not 3) — generate raises `RuntimeError`, discover marks the batch unassignable; the truncation path (`stop_reason == "max_tokens"`) still routes to the BUG-071 shrink/scale handler (NOT repair); a guard test confirms the "repairable" fixture is genuinely invalid JSON until repaired. |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | Added `repair_json` to the topicization imports + a shared helper `_loads_topicization_json_with_repair(cleaned, *, stage)` (`topicization.py:66`) mirroring the per-message path: it tries `json.loads`, and on `JSONDecodeError` applies `repair_json` and re-parses the repaired text BEFORE the exception propagates (so a recoverable reply is parsed on the FIRST attempt, no re-issue); only if the repaired text ALSO fails does the `JSONDecodeError` reach the existing retry/fallback handler. Wired into all three parse sites (`:486` generate, `:664` merge, `:1411` discover). Lowered the per-stage cap `3 → 2` via `_TOPICIZATION_MAX_JSON_RETRIES = 2` (`:63`; applied at `:448`/`:619`/`:1363`) — with repair handling the common case, at most one corrective re-issue is warranted. Truncation handling (BUG-071, `stop_reason == "max_tokens"`) is checked BEFORE the parse helper at every site, so F2 is strictly the non-truncated invalid-JSON path and leaves truncation behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged. |
| **Self-review (truncation-unaffected / fallback-preserved)** | **Truncation unaffected:** the `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` branch precedes `_loads_topicization_json_with_repair` at all three sites, so a truncated reply never reaches repair — verified by `test_generate_batch_truncation_path_unaffected_by_repair`. **Fallback preserved:** the helper RE-RAISES `JSONDecodeError` when the repaired text still fails, so the existing per-stage terminal contracts (generate → `RuntimeError`/`TopicizationBatchTruncatedError`; merge → return unmerged `all_batch_topics`; discover → mark unassignable) are unchanged, just reached one re-issue sooner. One pre-existing test (`test_incremental_topicization.py::TestDiscoverHandlesJsonParseError`) was updated to assert the new cap (2). |
| **Workaround** | None durable pre-fix; the only mitigation was avoiding topicization on channels whose replies frequently emit unescaped-quote JSON. |
| **Artifacts** | Tests: `tests/test_bug074_topicization_json_repair.py`. Reuses `repair_json` (BUG-065). |
| **Linked** | BUG-065 (`repair_json` — the deterministic repair pass reused here); BUG-019 (the JSON-retry hint preserved at each site); BUG-071 (the truncation `stop_reason` handling this fix is careful not to disturb); BUG-073 (the concurrency hardening landed in the same pass). |

### BUG-072 — No cross-process concurrency guard around FULL topicization → two runs of the same channel execute concurrently and multiply Sonnet spend

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High** (token-burn / cost: a single full re-topicization of a heavy channel is hundreds of charged Sonnet batches; running it TWICE concurrently for the same channel multiplies that spend. Observed live 2026-06-28 — `mediamedics` topicized TWICE concurrently, an MCP-triggered `full_pipeline` overlapping a scheduler incremental→full re-escalation, with no dedup). |
| **Status** | **`resolved`** (Option (a) advisory-lock fix + tests; commits `bdca97f`, `4e8a8ce`, `c3f8710`, `7ad3264`, `23764b7`). Carved out of the BUG-071 "Deferred follow-up — concurrent-run dedup" row. The residual processing-stage + incremental-stage concurrency gaps surfaced on top of this work are tracked + fixed under BUG-073 (F1 + F3). |
| **Component** | `topicization` — `tg_parser/services/topicization_service.py` (`run_topicization` funnel + new `channel_topicization_lock` / `_locked_skip_result` / `_topicize_channel_locked`; re-escalation branch in `run_incremental_topicization`). Entry paths funnelled: `tg_parser/services/pipeline_service.py` (`run_full_pipeline` → `run_topicization`), `tg_parser/services/pipeline_dispatch_service.py` (`full_pipeline` + `topicization` jobs), `tg_parser/services/scheduler_service.py` (`_process_source` → `run_incremental_topicization` re-escalation + `_retopicize_source`), and the CLI `tg-parser run` process. |
| **Discovered** | 2026-06-28 — during BUG-071 Fix-2 failure-path validation. Two independent callers (an MCP `full_pipeline` and a scheduler re-escalation) ran `topicize_channel` for the SAME channel at the same time with no coordination. |
| **Symptoms** | Duplicate concurrent full topicization of one channel: two overlapping hundreds-of-batch Sonnet runs, doubling token spend for zero extra value (both produce the same cards; the loser's work is wasted). |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced)** | NO cross-process concurrency guard existed around full topicization of a channel. `run_topicization` (`topicization_service.py`) → `TopicizationPipelineImpl.topicize_channel` (`processing/topicization.py`, BATCH_SIZE=50) is the single expensive funnel, reached by THREE uncoordinated callers: (1) scheduler incremental tick re-escalation (`run_incremental_topicization` escalates a 0-card-but-new-docs channel to a full `run_topicization`); (2) MCP/API `full_pipeline` + `topicization` dispatch jobs; (3) the separate CLI `tg-parser run` OS process. The two pre-existing guards are DISJOINT and neither covers path-1-vs-path-2 overlap: the scheduler's `_source_processing_lock(source_id)` (`scheduler_service.py`, namespace `SCHEDULER_SOURCE_LOCK_NS=0x5C40`) is taken ONLY on the scheduler path and keyed by `source_id`; the dispatch `_running_channel_jobs: set[str]` (`pipeline_dispatch_service.py`) is in-process only and keyed by normalized channel, disjoint from the advisory lock and useless across processes. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test ran two concurrent `run_topicization` for the same channel and asserted the second is skipped, and no guard existed to test. **Closure:** `tests/test_bug072_topicization_concurrency.py` — (non-PG) the guard degrades to "acquired" with no DB / no DB-context; the benign skip sentinel shape is caller-compatible; `run_topicization` returns the sentinel WITHOUT running the inner funnel when the lock is held, and delegates to the inner funnel when acquired; a lock-skip does NOT arm the BUG-071 Fix-2 cooldown marker while an acquired 0-persisted-card run STILL arms it (interplay guard); a lock-skipped re-escalation FALLS THROUGH to the cheap incremental Phase 1/2 (does NOT run the full funnel, does NOT abandon the tick's new docs — Bugbot follow-up guard); the lock namespace differs from `SCHEDULER_SOURCE_LOCK_NS`. (PG-gated `TEST_POSTGRES=1`) a second concurrent acquire on the same channel is refused, a different channel is not blocked, the lock releases on context exit; end-to-end through `run_topicization` a held lock skips the funnel for that channel while a different channel runs; and the scheduler/dispatch/pipeline paths all contend on the SAME normalized key (`chx` and `@chx` collide). |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | **Option (a) — a non-blocking Postgres advisory lock keyed by channel, wrapping `run_topicization`.** Generalised the proven scheduler `_source_processing_lock` pattern into a reusable `channel_topicization_lock(channel_id)` async-context-manager (`topicization_service.py:136`) under a NEW distinct int4 namespace **`TOPICIZATION_LOCK_NS = 0x70C1`** (`:132`; distinct from `SCHEDULER_SOURCE_LOCK_NS=0x5C40` so the two guards never collide in the shared `pg_advisory_lock` keyspace). It takes a SESSION-scoped `pg_try_advisory_lock(:ns, hashtext(:cid))` on a DEDICATED `processing_storage_engine` connection (held for the whole run — a full run spans many transactions/batches, so an xact-scoped lock can't cover it), then `pg_advisory_unlock` + close the connection in `finally`. The key is `hashtext(normalize_channel_id(channel_id))` so every entry path (which all identify the channel by its normalized id) contends on the SAME lock. It DEGRADES to "acquired" (`yield True`) when the DB/engine is unavailable (or `Database.get_instance` raises) so non-PG unit tests never block. `run_topicization` (`:228`) is now a thin wrapper that acquires the lock and, if NOT acquired (another full run owns the channel), logs `topicization_run_skipped_already_in_flight channel=…` and returns a BENIGN no-op sentinel `_locked_skip_result()` (`:197`) — it does NOT raise; the real body moved verbatim into `_topicize_channel_locked` (`:267`). **BUG-071 Fix-2 interplay (critical):** a lock-skip is NOT a failed 0-card attempt, so the re-escalation branch in `run_incremental_topicization` (`:557`) checks `full.get("skipped_locked")` and, on a skip, leaves the cooldown marker UNTOUCHED (neither arms nor clears — the run that holds the lock owns that bookkeeping) and **falls through to the cheap incremental Phase 1/2 path** (see the Bugbot follow-up row below — it does NOT abandon the tick's new docs and does NOT return early). The acquiring run keeps the existing Fix-2 arm/clear-on-persisted-cards behaviour unchanged. The sentinel is shaped exactly like a real return (all counts zeroed + `skipped_locked=True`) so every caller (`run_full_pipeline` reads `topics_count`/`bundles_count`/`total_tokens`; `_retopicize_source` reads `topics_count`/`bundles_count`; the re-escalation reads `total_tokens`) handles it without a `KeyError`. |
| **Self-review (deadlock / leak / caller-compat / Fix-2)** | **Deadlock:** a scheduler tick holds BOTH `_source_processing_lock(source_id)` (ingestion engine) AND the new `channel_topicization_lock(channel_id)` (processing engine) — DIFFERENT namespaces, DIFFERENT keys, DIFFERENT connections, and BOTH are non-blocking `pg_try_advisory_lock` (return immediately), so no lock-ordering cycle is possible. **Leak:** the dedicated connection is unlocked + closed in `finally` (unlock guarded by `acquired`, its own `try/except`); the degraded no-DB path takes no connection. **Caller-compat:** sentinel shape verified against all funnel callers (above). **Fix-2:** lock-skip path is exception-free and marker-neutral; crash-path arming (BUG-071 Fix-2 failure-path) is unaffected because a skip returns normally rather than raising. **No migration:** advisory locks are runtime-only. |
| **Follow-up — Bugbot finding "Lock skip abandons new doc refs" (medium; this WIP NOT committed)** | **Finding:** the first cut of the lock-skip re-escalation branch returned a benign `IncrementalTopicizeResult` immediately, so it never ran incremental Phase 1/2 for the tick's `new_doc_refs`. **Evidence it was a real abandonment (investigated this session):** `new_doc_refs` is tick-local (`scheduler_service.py:481-485` = docs_after − docs_before for THIS tick; later ticks only pass freshly-processed refs and there is NO scheduler-side uncovered-doc recovery — `_retopicize_source` has zero production callers and `run_incremental_topicization_for_uncovered` is CLI-only). The in-flight full run that holds the lock loads its corpus snapshot fresh at the START of `topicize_channel` (`processing/topicization.py:225`) and then holds the lock for hundreds of batches; so in the dominant long-run case its snapshot EXCLUDES docs the scheduler persists during the run. If that run then SUCCEEDS, the channel transitions to >0 cards and no future re-escalation fires → those docs are permanently uncovered. (Pre-BUG-072, the concurrent full re-escalation DID cover them — at the cost of the double-spend BUG-072 fixes — so the early-return was a coverage regression.) **Decision: fall through (Option C), not return.** The branch now logs and sets `should_reescalate = False`, falling through to the cheap incremental Phase 1/2 path EXACTLY like the BUG-071 cooldown fall-through (Bugbot Finding 1). **Why this does NOT re-introduce BUG-072 / why the Phase-2 "race" is immaterial:** the fall-through runs only a CHEAP, tick-local incremental (a single small batch over `new_docs`), NOT a second full hundreds-of-batch corpus run — so the dual-full-run spend BUG-072 targets is still suppressed. And the duplicate-topic risk is INVERSELY correlated with run length: a long in-flight run (the case BUG-072 matters for) has a snapshot that EXCLUDES these late docs, so the incremental Phase 2 covers a DISJOINT doc set with distinct LLM-generated topic ids (no duplicate topics, no DB conflict); only a SHORT in-flight run whose snapshot already includes these docs can produce minor duplicate work, bounded to one incremental batch — strictly cheaper than the abandonment it prevents. The cooldown marker stays UNTOUCHED on the skip (skip ≠ failure). **Code (final anchors):** `tg_parser/services/topicization_service.py:557` — `if full.get("skipped_locked"): … should_reescalate = False` then fall through; the marker arm/clear + early `return` were moved into the `else:` branch so they only run on a genuine (non-skipped) escalation outcome. **Tests:** `tests/test_bug072_topicization_concurrency.py::test_lock_skip_falls_through_to_incremental_not_abandoned` (asserts the expensive `_topicize_channel_locked` body does NOT run, but Phase 1 `assign_documents_to_topics` + Phase 2 `_discover_single_batch` DO run on the new docs, and the marker is untouched); `test_lock_skip_does_not_arm_fix2_marker` updated to stub the incremental phase offline. Focused run (`TEST_POSTGRES=1`): bug072+bug071+incremental+service_di+scheduler = **120 passed**. |
| **Workaround** | None durable pre-fix; the only mitigation was avoiding manual `full_pipeline`/`topicization` triggers while a scheduler tick could re-escalate the same channel. |
| **Artifacts** | Prod evidence (2026-06-28): `mediamedics` full topicization ran twice concurrently (MCP `full_pipeline` + scheduler incremental→full re-escalation) with no dedup. Anchors verified this session at the current tree. Tests: `tests/test_bug072_topicization_concurrency.py`. |
| **Linked** | BUG-071 (this is the carved-out "Deferred follow-up — concurrent-run dedup" item from the Fix-2 failure-path row; same token-burn class); BUG-070 / BUG-068 Fix 4 (the `_source_processing_lock` session-scoped advisory-lock-on-dedicated-connection pattern that `channel_topicization_lock` generalises); F5-C resummarize (the two-key `pg_advisory_*` precedent). |

### BUG-071 — Topicization burns Sonnet tokens on charged-but-truncated (`stop_reason=max_tokens`) replies + a latent per-tick full re-escalation re-burn loop

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High** (token-burn / cost: one full re-topicization of `murashko_med` burned ~2.38M Sonnet tokens with 328/334 batches failing and **0 topic cards saved**; the latent re-escalation loop would re-burn the full run EVERY scheduler tick once processing is unblocked). |
| **Status** | **`resolved`** (Fixes 1–3 + the Fix-2 failure-path follow-up + tests; commits `bdca97f`, `4e8a8ce`, `c3f8710`, `7ad3264`, `23764b7`). The residual "JSON-parse retries skip `repair_json` and re-burn the full batch" gap is tracked + fixed under BUG-074 (F2). |
| **Component** | `topicization` / `processing.llm` — `tg_parser/processing/topicization.py` (`_generate_topics_batch`, `_merge_topics`, `_discover_single_batch`), `tg_parser/processing/llm/anthropic_client.py` (`LLMResponse` construction), `tg_parser/processing/ports.py` (`LLMResponse`), `tg_parser/services/topicization_service.py` (`run_incremental_topicization` re-escalation branch), `tg_parser/api/metrics.py`. |
| **Discovered** | 2026-06-27 — read-only root-cause during the post-BUG-069/070 production watch (handoff `START_PROMPT_SESSION_BUG071_TOPICIZATION_TOKEN_BURN_2026-06-27.md`). Symptom paradox: `processed_documents` flat yet Anthropic balance still draining. |
| **Symptoms** | `processed_documents` count flat while Anthropic credit kept being deducted. Topicization sends 50-doc batches to `claude-sonnet-4-6` with `max_tokens=8192`; the topic JSON routinely EXCEEDS 8192 output tokens → Anthropic returns **HTTP 200 (CHARGED) but TRUNCATED** mid-string → `json.loads` raises `Unterminated string` → `repair_json` cannot fix length-truncation → the call is retried 3× (each a full charged Sonnet call) then discarded. Metrics: `tg_parser_llm_tokens_total{model="claude-sonnet-4-6"}` rising; completion÷successful-call ≈ 8097 ≈ the 8192 cap (i.e. essentially every call maxed its output budget). |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced)** | (A) `stop_reason` was NOT surfaced to callers — `LLMResponse` (`ports.py`) had no `stop_reason` field, and `anthropic_client._extract_text_content` only LOGGED `stop_reason` in the empty-content branch (never fires on a `max_tokens` truncation, where content is non-empty). So the three topicization JSON-retry loops treated a truncation identically to a transient parse error and re-issued the **identical oversized request** up to `max_json_retries=3` times — all charged, all truncating identically, all discarded. (B) `run_incremental_topicization` (`topicization_service.py:216`, `if len(existing_cards) == 0 and len(new_docs) > 0`) re-escalates to a FULL run when a channel has 0 cards + new docs. Because (A) guarantees 0 cards are ever saved, the channel stays at 0 cards forever, so the scheduler re-escalates the full ~hundreds-of-batch Sonnet run on EVERY tick that has new docs. Currently DORMANT only because processing is billing-blocked (no new docs → branch not taken); restoring credit re-arms it. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test exercised a `max_tokens`-truncated LLM reply (`stop_reason="max_tokens"` with non-empty body) — mocks returned either valid JSON or a `JSONDecodeError`-class body, both of which exercise the parse-retry path, not truncation. No test asserted the re-escalation branch is bounded across ticks. **Closure:** `tests/test_bug071_topicization_truncation.py` — (a) a truncated full batch is split, the identical oversized request is issued exactly ONCE (not 3×), the JSON-repair path is NOT taken, and `tg_parser_llm_truncation_total` increments; (b) a single-candidate truncation scales `max_tokens` (capped) without re-issuing the same budget; (c) the re-escalation cooldown gate escalates once, is skipped within the TTL, then allowed after the TTL, and a successful (>0 PERSISTED card) escalation clears the marker; (d) Bugbot guards — while in cooldown the cheap incremental Phase 1/2 still runs on new docs (full re-escalation suppressed), and the marker stays ARMED when `topics_count>0` but 0 cards actually persisted; (e) Bugbot BUG-018 guard — a multi-batch run where every batch truncation-drops reports `failed_batches == total_batches` (systemic-fail, not 0), a single-batch drop sets `failed_batches=1` without crashing, and a partial salvage does not raise (14 tests total + the existing 12 BUG-018 tests still pass). |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | **Fix 1 — detect truncation, shrink instead of re-issuing.** Added `stop_reason: str \| None = None` to `LLMResponse` (`ports.py`), populated from `data.get("stop_reason")` in `anthropic_client.generate_with_usage` (other providers default `None`; `InstrumentedLLMClient` returns the inner result unchanged so it propagates). In the three topicization loops a `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` is now NON-retryable: `_generate_topics_batch` splits the candidate batch in half and re-generates each half (recursively; a single candidate scales `max_tokens` 8192→16384→32768 capped via module-level `_TRUNCATION_MAX_TOKENS_CAP`, then drops the batch — never a 3× identical re-burn); `_merge_topics` grows `max_tokens` once (capped) and otherwise falls back to its existing "return all batch topics unmerged" contract (the merge LLM returns only compact group-ID arrays, so it can't be split); `_discover_single_batch` splits the doc batch (threading first-half new topics into the second half's dedup context) and, for a single un-splittable doc, falls back to its existing "mark unassignable" contract. The JSON-repair retry path (BUG-019 hint + `record_llm_json_parse_retry`) is preserved unchanged for genuine `JSONDecodeError`s. **Bugbot follow-up (1 MEDIUM — BUG-018 regression, fixed):** the generate-stage truncation-drop originally returned `[]`, so `topicize_channel` (which only bumps `failed_batches` on a raised exception) could finish a channel-wide run with 0 cards yet `failed_batches=0` — regressing the BUG-018 systemic-fail exit-code-2 into the misleading "insufficient data" hint. Fixed by raising a dedicated `TopicizationBatchTruncatedError` (direct `Exception` subclass, so it bypasses `_generate_topics_batch`'s `except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError)`) when a batch is *completely* lost to truncation: the multi-batch `asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True)` site counts it as a failed batch automatically, and the single-batch path catches it to record `failed_batches=1` + return `[]` (no CLI crash). A *partial* salvage (one split half still yields topics) is NOT a failure — it returns the salvaged topics. No re-introduction of the 3× re-burn and the Fix-1 shrink ladder is unchanged. **Fix 2 — break the re-escalation re-burn loop.** Gated the full re-escalation behind a persisted cooldown (new setting `topicization_reescalation_cooldown_s`, default **3600s** ≈ one tick). **Persistence decision: reuse the existing `processing_failures` table (NO migration)** via `SAProcessingFailureRepo`, keyed by a synthetic, clearly-namespaced `source_ref = topicization:reescalation:<channel_id>` (can never collide with a real `tg:<ch>:<type>:<id>` doc ref). After a 0-card escalation the marker is (re)armed (attempts bumped); a recovered escalation deletes it. While the marker is within TTL the full re-escalation is SKIPPED with a `topicization re-escalation skipped (cooldown)` log; after the TTL one more attempt is allowed so a real prompt/model fix can recover the channel. The marker repo is bound on the production processing session (`run_incremental_topicization` owns the repos); injectable for tests. **Bugbot follow-up (2 MEDIUM, both fixed):** (1) while in cooldown the gate now suppresses ONLY the expensive full re-escalation and FALLS THROUGH to the cheap incremental Phase 1/2 path (keyword-assign + Fix-1 batch-split LLM discover) so new docs are still processed during the TTL window instead of being abandoned; (2) marker-clearing is gated on the ACTUAL PERSISTED card count (re-query `topic_card_repo.list_by_channel` after the run), not the in-memory `full["topics_count"]` — `topicize_channel` swallows `SQLAlchemyError` on each upsert, so the in-memory list can be non-empty while 0 cards persisted; clearing on that would defeat the cooldown entirely. An errored recount is treated as 0 (arm the cooldown, the safe side). **Fix 3 — observability.** New Counter `tg_parser_llm_truncation_total{provider,model,stage}` + `record_llm_truncation(...)` (`metrics.py`), incremented at each topicization site when a truncation is detected (modeled on `BOT_GEMINI_EMPTY_PARTS_TOTAL` / `record_bot_gemini_empty_parts`). |
| **Persistence rationale (Fix 2)** | Option (c) from the handoff (reuse cooldown settings + a channel-keyed marker, no migration) was chosen over (a) a new `topicization_failures` table or (b) a `sources` column. Justification: it is persistence-backed (survives restart — important because the loop re-arms on every restart otherwise), needs no Alembic migration (no PG/Docker available in this environment to verify a migration applies cleanly, and the handoff explicitly allows (c)), and reuses the proven `record_failure`/`list_failures`/`delete_failure` infra. The synthetic key never matches a real doc `source_ref`, so neither the processing `_load_failed_lookup` skip-set nor the `raw_message_repo` `NOT EXISTS` cooldown anti-join is affected. Minor accepted trade-off: one synthetic row per stuck channel is visible to the `failures` CLI report (bounded by channel count, arguably informative). |
| **Workaround** | Pre-fix: none durable; the only thing keeping the loop dormant is the Anthropic billing block (do NOT top up credit until this ships — per the handoff operational warning). |
| **Artifacts** | Prod evidence (2026-06-27, 09:21–10:19 UTC): one `murashko_med` re-topicization = 334 batches, 328 failed, 0 cards, ~2.38M Sonnet tokens (1.56M prompt / 0.82M completion); completion÷successful-call ≈ 8097 ≈ 8192 cap. Anchors verified at HEAD `61637d1` (no drift this session). Tests: `tests/test_bug071_topicization_truncation.py` (10 tests). |
| **Linked** | BUG-067 B2b (the `processing_failures` cooldown pattern reused/mirrored by Fix 2); BUG-019 (the JSON-repair hint/retry path preserved by Fix 1); BUG-065 (`repair_json` — confirmed it cannot fix a length-truncated reply, only unescaped quotes / trailing commas). |
| **Follow-up — post-top-up observability (committed `4e8a8ce`; this WIP NOT committed)** | Provisioned the 4 approved Prometheus alert rules (group `tg_parser_bug071_topicization` in `docker/prometheus/alerts.yml`) + promtool tests + monitoring plan `docs/notes/MONITORING_PLAN_BUG071_POST_TOPUP_2026-06-27.md` (commit `4e8a8ce`). **Then closed the last observability gap (uncommitted WIP — awaiting Bugbot + gated full-suite):** added a REAL Prometheus Counter `tg_parser_topicization_failed_batches_total{stage, channel_id}` (`tg_parser/api/metrics.py`, helper `record_topicization_failed_batch`) incremented at the exact `failed_batches` sites in `topicize_channel` (`topicization.py:262/270/310` → generate stage only; merge/discover use different terminal contracts and don't count failed batches). It counts BOTH truncation-drops (corroborating `tg_parser_llm_truncation_total`) AND genuine non-truncation batch failures. Upgraded the alert with a direct-signal rule `TopicizationFailedBatchesHigh` (warning, `sum(rate(...[15m])) by (stage) > 0.05`, for 15m), keeping `TopicizationBurnNoProgress` as a backstop. Tests: `tests/test_bug071_topicization_truncation.py::TestFailedBatchesMetric` (4: multi-batch truncation-drop per-batch count, single-batch drop once, multi-batch non-truncation RuntimeError, single-batch RuntimeError+re-raise). `promtool check rules` (20 rules) + `promtool test rules` green; BUG-071+BUG-018+BUG-023 suites 48 passed; `ruff` clean. |
| **Follow-up — Fix-2 FAILURE-PATH gap (prod-discovered 2026-06-28; this WIP NOT committed)** | **Gap:** live prod validation (HEAD `c3f8710`) showed Fix 2's cooldown marker was armed/cleared ONLY after `run_topicization(...)` returned NORMALLY. But `run_topicization` (→ `topicize_channel`) RE-RAISES on failure (its only protection is `finally: llm_client.close()`), so when a 0-card re-escalation died by exception — mass 300s `LLMCallTimeoutError` / `AnthropicBillingError` — the exception propagated out of `run_incremental_topicization` BEFORE the marker-arming code ran. No marker was written, so the next scheduler tick re-escalated the SAME 0-card channel to another full hundreds-of-batch Sonnet run: the exact re-burn loop Fix 2 exists to break, NOT broken on the crash path. **Empirical proof (this session):** `mediamedics` (222 batches, 20:46) + `murashko_med` (349 batches, 20:50) both ended `stages_failed=['incremental_topicization'] outcome=degraded` via raised exception, ZERO marker writes / "skipped (cooldown)" lines, ~12.1M Sonnet tokens burned, 0 cards. **Patch (uncommitted):** restructured the re-escalation branch in `run_incremental_topicization` (`topicization_service.py`) — the `run_topicization(...)` call is now wrapped in `try/except Exception`: on raise it ARMS the marker (treating a crashed re-escalation as a failed 0-card attempt, bumping `attempts`) and then RE-RAISES so the scheduler's existing `stages_failed`/degraded handling is preserved (the error is NOT swallowed). The clean-completion path is unchanged in semantics: >0 PERSISTED cards → clear marker; 0 persisted → arm. Extracted two best-effort helpers `_arm_reescalation_marker` / `_clear_reescalation_marker` (each swallows its OWN errors) so a marker-store failure can never mask the original re-escalation exception or crash the tick. `except Exception` (not `BaseException`) so `asyncio.CancelledError` on shutdown is not turned into a cooldown arm. Net effect: a crashed re-escalation now arms the cooldown, so the next tick is gated (skips the full run, falls through to the cheap incremental Phase 1/2 path). Tests (`TestReEscalationFailurePathArmsMarker`, 3): exception arms marker + re-raises; the next tick is skipped by the gate (full run not re-attempted, incremental runs instead); a marker-WRITE failure does not mask the original error. BUG-071 suite 21 passed; adjacent topicization-service/incremental/bug018/bug023 suites 121 passed; `ruff` clean. **Deferred follow-up (NOT implemented — out of scope/not localized): concurrent-run dedup.** This session `mediamedics` topicized TWICE concurrently (an MCP-triggered `full_pipeline` + a scheduler incremental→full-rebuild) with no dedup, multiplying spend. There is NO existing guard around topicization (BUG-070's lock covers only the Telethon ingestion session, not `topicize_channel`; no advisory lock or in-flight check exists in `topicization_service`). A correct fix needs cross-process coordination (e.g. a Postgres advisory lock keyed by channel around the full run, or an in-flight marker) touching the production run path — broader than this hotfix and warranting its own design + tests. Recommended as a SEPARATE follow-up. |

### BUG-070 — Concurrent Telethon clients on one non-WAL session sqlite → persistent `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` (zero ingestion)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High** (persistent ingestion outage, NOT a restart artifact: 6–13 of 13 sources fail EVERY hourly tick with `database is locked`; raw ingestion stuck — zero new messages collected in ~10h. Self-inflicted regression enabled by the BUG-068 A3 concurrency bump 1→2.) |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (fix Part 1 + Part 2 + H1/N2 review hardening — committed [`61637d1`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/61637d1) «fix(ingestion): serialize Telethon session access + WAL/busy_timeout to stop concurrent 'database is locked' (BUG-070)»; on `main`). |
| **Component** | `ingestion` / Telethon session sqlite — scheduler fan-out `tg_parser/services/scheduler_service.py` (`asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)` `:204`, `asyncio.gather(*[_process_source(s) …])` `:756`); per-source client build `tg_parser/services/ingestion_service.py` `run_ingestion` (`TelethonClient(settings)` → `connect()`); client `tg_parser/ingestion/telegram/telethon_client.py` (`TelegramClient(session=telegram_session_name, …)`); shared session file `data/sessions/tg_parser_session.session` (`TELEGRAM_SESSION_NAME`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-06-27 — read-only diagnosis during the post-BUG-068 production watch. Persisted across the hourly schedule (not cleared by restart), distinguishing it from a one-off lock. |
| **Symptoms** | Most sources fail every incremental tick with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` recorded in `sources.last_error`; `processed_documents`/`raw_messages` flat (zero new ingestion for ~10h). Concentrated on the ingestion stage (Telethon `connect()` / session writes), not processing. |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced)** | INTRA-PROCESS self-contention on the single Telethon session sqlite. The scheduler fans sources out `scheduler_max_concurrent_sources`-wide (default **2** since BUG-068 A3 bumped 1→2 in commit `1ed86ac`). Each `_process_source` → `run_full_pipeline` → `run_ingestion` builds its OWN `TelethonClient` ([`ingestion_service.py:46`](../../tg_parser/services/ingestion_service.py)) and `connect()`s, opening `TelegramClient(session=self.settings.telegram_session_name, …)` ([`telethon_client.py:55-59`](../../tg_parser/ingestion/telegram/telethon_client.py)). All clients point at ONE shared session file. Telethon's `SQLiteSession` opens its own sqlite connection in **default rollback-journal mode with NO `busy_timeout`**, and writes to it both on `connect()` AND throughout the client's lifetime (`process_entities` / `set_update_state` while iterating messages). Two concurrent connect()/session writes therefore collide → instant `database is locked` (no wait). **Latent cross-container risk:** the bot/mcp containers share the same session volume — in this incident only `tg_parser` used Telethon (bot/mcp logged zero Telethon activity), but a future concurrent Telethon writer in another container could trip the same lock. |
| **Independence from BUG-069** | Unrelated to BUG-069 (the processing-stage `pgsql_tmp` DiskFull on Postgres `raw_messages`). This bug is on the **Telethon session sqlite** at the **ingestion** stage. The only link is BUG-068 A3 (1→2 concurrency) being the common enabler — it widened ingestion fan-out, which surfaced the pre-existing non-WAL/no-busy_timeout session as a hard contention point. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test ran two concurrent ingestions against a shared Telethon session, and no test asserted the session sqlite uses WAL / a busy_timeout. Existing `test_telethon_client.py` / `test_e2e_pipeline.py` mock `TelethonClient` and never exercise real concurrent session access. **Closure**: tests that (a) prove the in-process lock serializes the session critical-section (no overlap) and releases on exception, and (b) assert `journal_mode=wal` + the configured `busy_timeout` on the session connection (added this session). |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | **Part 1 — in-process session serialization.** New process-wide `asyncio.Lock` `_SESSION_LOCK` + accessor `telethon_session_lock()` in [`telethon_client.py`](../../tg_parser/ingestion/telegram/telethon_client.py) (home chosen there because it guards the Telethon **session resource**, a Telethon concern). `run_ingestion` ([`ingestion_service.py`](../../tg_parser/services/ingestion_service.py)) wraps the **whole client lifetime** — `connect()` → `orchestrator.ingest_source()` (message iteration) → `disconnect()` — in `async with telethon_session_lock():`. Scope is the full lifetime (not just `connect()`) because Telethon persists entity/update state to the session sqlite throughout iteration, so a connect-only lock would not prevent mid-iteration write collisions. `async with` guarantees release even when a source raises. Only **ingestion** is serialized; the downstream LLM-bound **processing/topicization** stages run after `run_ingestion` returns and stay parallel — so `scheduler_max_concurrent_sources` is **left at 2** (UNCHANGED). **Part 2 — WAL + busy_timeout (defense-in-depth, also partially mitigates the latent cross-container risk).** New `_WALSQLiteSession(SQLiteSession)` subclass overrides `_cursor()` to apply `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` (persisted in the DB header) and `PRAGMA busy_timeout=<ms>` (per-connection, re-applied on reopen) the first time each connection opens; `TelethonClient.connect()` now passes a `_WALSQLiteSession` instance (Telethon accepts a `Session` object in place of the bare filename). With WAL + busy_timeout a brief concurrent writer **waits** up to the timeout instead of erroring instantly. **New setting:** `telegram_session_busy_timeout_ms` (default **5000**; env `TELEGRAM_SESSION_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`) threaded `Settings` → `connect()` → `_WALSQLiteSession`. **Telethon version:** `1.43.2` (`requirements.txt`) — its `SQLiteSession._cursor()` lazily `sqlite3.connect(self.filename, check_same_thread=False)`, so the override applies PRAGMAs cleanly at connection creation. **BUG-069 processing code UNTOUCHED.** **Tests:** `tests/test_telethon_session_lock.py` (6): `test_ingestion_serializes_concurrent_session_access` (two concurrent `run_ingestion` → peak in-section concurrency == 1), `test_session_lock_released_on_exception` (connect raising still releases the lock + lock reusable after), `test_wal_session_applies_pragmas`, `test_wal_session_reapplies_busy_timeout_after_reopen`, `test_connect_builds_wal_session_from_setting` (setting threaded → PRAGMAs on the real connection), `test_busy_timeout_setting_default_and_override`. |
| **Review hardening (this session — NOT committed)** | **H1 (High) — lock-wait must not be mislabeled `pipeline_timeout`.** Pre-hardening the `async with telethon_session_lock()` was entered INSIDE the per-source watchdog (`scheduler_service._process_source` wraps the whole `run_full_pipeline` in `asyncio.wait_for(timeout=scheduler_source_timeout_s=1800)`), so a sibling source merely WAITING for the session lock burned its watchdog budget and a benign wait could surface as a `pipeline_timeout` FAILURE. **Design chosen (preferred option):** acquire the lock with an EXPLICIT separate budget. New `telethon_session_lock_guard(wait_timeout_s)` async-context-manager ([`telethon_client.py`](../../tg_parser/ingestion/telegram/telethon_client.py)) does `await asyncio.wait_for(lock.acquire(), timeout=wait_timeout_s)`; on elapse it raises a dedicated `SessionLockContentionError` (subclasses `RuntimeError`). `run_ingestion` now uses the guard with the new `scheduler_session_lock_wait_timeout_s` setting (default **900s**, env `SCHEDULER_SESSION_LOCK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_S`). `pipeline_service` re-raises `SessionLockContentionError` UN-wrapped at the ingest stage (its broad `except RuntimeError` would otherwise mask the type). `scheduler_service._process_source` catches it and records a DISTINCT, BENIGN outcome **`session_lock_contention`** — counted in the new `aggregate["sources_lock_contended"]`, NOT `sources_failed`/`sources_degraded`, and WITHOUT a `record_attempt` (no `fail_count` bump, no `last_error` pollution, no `last_success_at` advance — mirrors the rate-limited / already-in-flight benign-skip precedent), so the source simply retries next tick. **Why this is the cleaner option (vs. moving the watchdog after lock acquisition):** the watchdog is at the scheduler layer while the lock is acquired deep inside `run_ingestion`; threading "watchdog starts after acquire" through that boundary is invasive, whereas a bounded acquire + distinct exception is a local, well-contained change. **Watchdog interaction — ACCEPTED + MONITORED design point:** `scheduler_session_lock_wait_timeout_s` (900s) is deliberately sized BELOW `scheduler_source_timeout_s` (1800s) so contention is classified as `session_lock_contention` BEFORE the outer watchdog could fire `pipeline_timeout`. The lock is held ONLY during a source's Telethon fetch (processing/topicization run after the lock releases), and a pathological holder is still bounded by its OWN per-source watchdog, so worst-case lock-wait is bounded. The residual corner — a source that waits a long time AND then does heavy post-lock work, eating the remaining outer-watchdog budget — is accepted and made observable: lock-wait duration is logged (`telethon_session_lock_contention` / `telethon_session_lock_acquired`) and exported on the new `tg_telethon_session_lock_wait_seconds{outcome=acquired\|contention}` histogram + `sources_lock_contended` in the tick summary, so rising contention is watchable post-deploy and the budget can be re-tuned. **N2 (nit):** `telegram_session_busy_timeout_ms` Field constraint tightened `ge=0` → `gt=0` (default still 5000) so `0` (= the pre-fix instant-fail behaviour) can't be configured. **N1 / optional WAL read-back:** NOT applied — left as low-priority follow-ups (N1: factor the duplicated WAL/busy_timeout PRAGMA strings into a constant; optional: assert WAL is actually active by reading back `journal_mode` after open). **M1 (deploy-verified prerequisite, see Workaround):** the WAL `-wal`/`-shm` sidecar files require the `data/sessions/` volume to be LOCAL storage (not NFS/networked — WAL shared-memory is unsupported on many network FS) and all containers sharing the volume to run as the same UID. This is a PRE-DEPLOY GATE verified on prod (`df -h`/mount type + container UID), NOT a code change. **Tests (this session):** `tests/test_telethon_session_lock.py` — `test_busy_timeout_setting_rejects_zero` (N2), `test_session_lock_guard_raises_contention_on_wait_timeout`, `test_session_lock_guard_acquires_when_free`, `test_run_ingestion_raises_contention_when_session_busy` (H1 — aborts before `connect()`), `test_session_lock_released_on_cancellation` (M2a — cancel while holding the lock → released), `test_processing_runs_in_parallel_while_session_lock_held` + `test_processing_topicization_modules_do_not_import_session_lock` (M2b — processing not serialized by the session lock), plus an autouse `_reset_session_lock` fixture (M3 — rebind the loop-bound module `asyncio.Lock` per test); `tests/test_scheduler_service.py::test_h1_session_lock_contention_recorded_as_benign_not_failure` (H1 outcome: `sources_lock_contended=1`, `sources_failed=0`, no `record_attempt`). |
| **Workaround** | None durable pre-fix; a `tg_parser` restart does NOT clear it (persistent). Temporary mitigation would be reverting `scheduler_max_concurrent_sources` to 1 (re-serializing ingestion the blunt way), but that reintroduces the BUG-068 starvation the A3 bump fixed — hence the targeted in-process lock instead. **M1 deploy-verified prerequisite:** before deploying the WAL change, confirm `data/sessions/` on prod is LOCAL (not NFS/networked) storage and that every container sharing the session volume runs as the same UID — WAL's `-wal`/`-shm` shared-memory sidecars are unsafe on networked FS / across mismatched UIDs. If storage is networked OR UIDs differ, STOP before deploying (the in-process lock Part 1 still holds, but the WAL Part 2 must not be shipped onto unsafe storage). |
| **Artifacts** | Prod evidence (2026-06-27): 6–13/13 sources with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` in `sources.last_error` each hourly tick; raw ingestion flat ~10h. Code refs verified this session: `scheduler_service.py:197-204` + `:756`, `ingestion_service.py:46-58`, `telethon_client.py:54-58`; session in rollback-journal mode / no busy_timeout (Telethon `1.43.2` `SQLiteSession`). |
| **Linked** | BUG-068 (A3 concurrency 1→2 in `1ed86ac` is the enabler that surfaced this contention); BUG-069 (same dogfooding watch / same `1ed86ac` deploy, but a DIFFERENT db — Postgres `raw_messages` vs Telethon session sqlite — and a DIFFERENT stage — processing vs ingestion; independent). |

### BUG-069 — Un-paginated full-backlog load + sort spills to `pgsql_tmp` → transient `DiskFullError: No space left on device` on heavy channels

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **Medium** (transient / self-recovering so far: a single processing tick can intermittently fail on the heaviest channels when the full-backlog `ORDER BY` sort spills to Postgres temp files under low disk headroom, but later ticks succeed and the backlog resumes draining. Latent **outage risk** — as backlogs grow and disk headroom shrinks the spill gets larger and the transient failure can become persistent.) |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (v1 fix + B2 bounded-load — committed [`1809795`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/1809795) «fix(processing): bound per-tick raw load via NOT EXISTS + cooldown anti-join (BUG-069, B2)»; on `main`, in the `e0f517d` prod deploy). |
| **Component** | `pipeline` (processing) / `storage` — call site `tg_parser/services/processing_service.py` `run_processing` (`:113-114`); SQL `tg_parser/storage/sqlalchemy/raw_message_repo.py` `list_by_channel` (`:155-184`, `ORDER BY date ASC` at `:182`); Postgres temp-file spill (`pgsql_tmp`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-06-26 — during post-deploy verification of the BUG-067/068 fix (commit `1ed86ac`). Prod scheduler tick at ~2026-06-26T17:51Z logged `DiskFullError: No space left on device` in `sources.last_error` for `murashko_med` and `mediamedics` during a `raw_messages` sort (pgsql_tmp). It did **NOT** recur — later writes (17:53→18:02Z) succeeded and the backlogs resumed draining (murashko 11384→12165, mediamedics 9514→10070). Disk was 63% used / 6.7G free; ~24GB reclaimable Docker build cache was identified and is being cleared as an immediate mitigation. |
| **Symptoms** | Intermittent `DiskFullError: No space left on device` recorded in `sources.last_error` during a processing tick on the heaviest channels (`murashko_med`, `mediamedics`), surfacing while Postgres materializes a large sort to `pgsql_tmp`. Self-recovers on subsequent ticks (no persistent outage observed yet); backlogs continue draining. Correlated with low disk headroom (63% used / 6.7G free at the time). |
| **Root cause (HYPOTHESIS — code-traced, confirm under prod load)** | The processing stage loads the **ENTIRE** raw backlog for a channel with no pagination: `run_processing` calls `raw_messages = await raw_repo.list_by_channel(channel_id)` with **no `limit`** ([`processing_service.py:113-114`](../../tg_parser/services/processing_service.py)). The `limit` parameter exists on `run_processing` but the scheduler never passes it, and even when set it is applied in Python **after** the full query returns ([`processing_service.py:125-126`](../../tg_parser/services/processing_service.py)) — so it does NOT bound the DB-side load/sort. The repo SQL ([`raw_message_repo.py:155-184`](../../tg_parser/storage/sqlalchemy/raw_message_repo.py)) ends in `ORDER BY date ASC` (`:182`) with `LIMIT` appended **only** when `limit` is passed (`:175`); on the heaviest channels (murashko ~33k raw, mediamedics ~11k) that `ORDER BY` materializes a large sort that spills to Postgres temp files (`pgsql_tmp`), and under low disk headroom the spill throws `DiskFullError`. **Amplified by the same mechanism behind the BUG-067 token burn:** because failed/unpersisted docs are re-attempted every tick, the full backlog is re-loaded and re-sorted **every hour**, so the large sort recurs each tick rather than shrinking. (Confidence: code path confirmed; the `pgsql_tmp` spill itself is inferred from the prod `DiskFullError` during a `raw_messages` sort + the un-paginated `ORDER BY` — confirm with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` / `log_temp_files` under prod scale.) |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test exercises `list_by_channel` / `run_processing` at backlog scale or under constrained disk, so the un-paginated full-sort-and-materialize cost (and its `pgsql_tmp` spill under low headroom) is never reproduced. Existing coverage uses small fixtures where the sort fits in `work_mem`. **Closure**: add a test/load-check that asserts the processing load is bounded (paginated/seek) rather than a single full `ORDER BY` materialize, and operationally enable `log_temp_files` to surface spilling sorts before they hit `DiskFullError`. |
| **Intersection with deferred B2 (BUG-067)** | B2 (bounded retry + cooldown / limiting how much of the backlog is re-attempted each tick) was **deferred for a design discussion** under BUG-067. It directly reduces the re-read/re-sort volume, so it **partially** mitigates this bug — **BUT** B2b (already implemented this session via `failure_repo` cooldown) only skips *failed* docs; it does **NOT** cap the load of not-yet-attempted docs, and the sort still materializes over the full unprocessed set. A complete fix likely needs **EITHER** pagination/`limit` on the processing load (batch the backlog) **OR** ordering/indexing that avoids the large `pgsql_tmp` sort — to be decided in the joint B2 design discussion. |
| **Proposed fix (do NOT implement)** | **(1)** Pass a `limit`/batch size into `run_processing` from the scheduler so each tick processes a bounded slice (composes with the chunked persistence already shipped in BUG-067). **(2)** Ensure the `list_by_channel` query can stream / seek-paginate (keyset on `date`) instead of a full sort-and-materialize. **(3)** Operational: monitor/alert on disk headroom + `pgsql_tmp`; keep the Docker build cache pruned. **(4)** Cross-reference: revisit alongside the deferred B2 design (BUG-067). |
| **Fix implemented (v1 + B2, this session — NOT committed)** | **Core mechanism:** push the `NOT EXISTS(processed_documents)` filter AND the `LIMIT` into a single bounded raw query so Postgres only sorts a small window (no full-backlog `ORDER BY` → no `pgsql_tmp` spill / DiskFull) and already-processed docs are never re-sent to the LLM (kills the B2 token re-burn). **No per-source cursor** (deliberately dropped for v1 — `NOT EXISTS + LIMIT` already bounds the sort and guarantees forward progress; the old `sources`-cursor idea was unreachable because `run_processing` is keyed by `channel_id`). No schema change, no `Source`/`sources` change. **(1) Repo:** new CONCRETE (non-abstract) method `RawMessageRepo.list_unprocessed_by_channel(channel_id, limit)` ([`ports.py`](../../tg_parser/storage/ports.py) default body delegates to `list_by_channel` so test doubles don't break) + optimized SQLAlchemy override ([`raw_message_repo.py`](../../tg_parser/storage/sqlalchemy/raw_message_repo.py)): `SELECT … FROM raw_messages r WHERE r.channel_id=:channel_id AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM processed_documents p WHERE p.source_ref=r.source_ref) ORDER BY r.date ASC, r.source_ref ASC LIMIT :limit`. `list_by_channel` left UNTOUCHED (many callers/test doubles). **(2) Setting:** `processing_tick_batch_size` (default **300**, sized against the `scheduler_source_timeout_s` 1800s watchdog). **(3) Wiring:** `run_processing` normal/scheduler path now loads via `list_unprocessed_by_channel(channel_id, limit=processing_tick_batch_size)`; removed the redundant Python `limit` slice + the secondary `processed_repo.exists()` re-scan on the normal path. `force=True` keeps the full `list_by_channel` load (must reprocess existing docs); `retry_failed` keeps its failed-source_ref load + its exists() skip accounting UNCHANGED; CLI `--limit` overrides the per-tick bound. `run_multi_agent_processing` got the same bounded load (force-exempt). **(4)** The per-message `exists()` filter in `pipeline.py` is kept (still needed for `force`/agent callers; a cheap no-op on the bounded window). **(5) Coverage fix (B3):** `run_processing` now surfaces the true backlog size as `raw_total_count` (`count_by_channel`); `scheduler_service` coverage gauge uses it as the denominator instead of the process stage `total_count` (which post-fix is the bounded window → would give ratios >1 + false `channel_coverage_low`). **Tests:** `test_storage_integration.py::TestRawMessageRepo` (3 new: NOT EXISTS skip / LIMIT+ordering tie-break / empty-when-all-processed — Postgres-gated); `test_service_di.py` (bounded load used; `force`→full load; `retry_failed` unchanged; `raw_total_count` surfaced); `test_scheduler_service.py::test_bug069_coverage_uses_raw_total_not_bounded_window`. |
| **Follow-up fix (Option A cooldown anti-join — head-of-line/starvation regression caught in review, this session — NOT committed)** | **Regression (HIGH, found by Bugbot + self-review):** the bounded `NOT EXISTS(processed_documents)` window filters only on *processed* docs. A permanently/temporarily FAILING oldest message only ever gets a `processing_failures` row (never a `processed_documents` row); once its cooldown expires it re-enters the window at the FRONT every tick, and once the stuck failing prefix reaches `processing_tick_batch_size` it **starves** all newer unprocessed messages (no forward progress). **Fix (Option A):** extend `list_unprocessed_by_channel` with a SECOND anti-join `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM processing_failures f WHERE f.source_ref=r.source_ref AND f.last_attempt_at IS NOT NULL AND f.last_attempt_at::timestamptz <= :now AND f.last_attempt_at::timestamptz > :now - (CASE WHEN f.error_class='AnthropicBillingError' THEN <billing_s> WHEN f.error_class='LLMJsonParseError' AND f.attempts >= <parse_max> THEN <parse_s> ELSE <default_s> END) * INTERVAL '1 second')` so refs still inside their cooldown are excluded and the window fills with genuinely-actionable docs. The `CASE`/predicate **mirrors `pipeline._should_skip_failed` EXACTLY** (same category→TTL map: billing→`failure_billing_cooldown_s`, parse-after-`failure_parse_max_attempts`→`failure_parse_cooldown_s`, in-budget-parse/other→`failure_default_cooldown_s`; `last <= now` is the future-date clamp = the Python `age_s < 0` guard; strict `>` = `age_s < TTL`). No permanent-skip state exists in `_should_skip_failed` (exhaustion only swaps to a longer TTL), so "in cooldown OR exhausted" collapses to this one predicate. TTL ints are inlined as literals (validated settings, not user input) because a bind param used only as a `CASE` branch result is typed `text` by asyncpg (→ `text * interval` error). `processing_failures.source_ref` PK backs the anti-join — **no new index, no migration**. **Gating:** new keyword-only `failure_cooldown_enabled` param (default `False` = behaviour identical to pre-Option-A); `run_processing` + `run_multi_agent_processing` pass `settings.failure_cooldown_enabled`. `force=True` (`list_by_channel`) and `retry_failed` are UNCHANGED — they never route through this anti-join. The Python `failure_map`/`_should_skip_failed` filter in `pipeline.py` STAYS (still source of truth for force/agent/retry paths; now a near no-op on the normal path). **MEDIUMs also fixed:** (a) `run_multi_agent_processing` now surfaces `raw_total_count` (coverage denominator correct on the agent path too); (b) `scheduler_service` coverage ratio clamped to `min(1.0, processed/raw_total)` so a pruned/stale raw denominator can't emit ratio>1 / false `channel_coverage_low`. **Tests:** `test_storage_integration.py::TestRawMessageRepo` (2 new, Postgres-gated): `test_list_unprocessed_cooldown_prefix_does_not_starve_newer` (poison-pill prefix at batch size → newer docs surface with cooldown ON; legacy prefix-included behaviour with cooldown OFF) and `test_list_unprocessed_cooldown_predicate_matches_should_skip_failed` (SQL ↔ `_should_skip_failed` parity for billing/parse-in-budget/parse-exhausted/other/expired/future-dated cases); `test_service_di.py` updated to assert `failure_cooldown_enabled` is threaded into the bounded load. Full run (`TEST_POSTGRES=1`): `test_service_di.py` + `test_scheduler_service.py` + `test_processing_pipeline.py` + `test_storage_integration.py` = **142 passed**; `ruff check` clean. |
| **Workaround** | Immediate mitigation in progress: clear ~24GB reclaimable Docker build cache to restore disk headroom (disk was 63% used / 6.7G free). The error is transient/self-recovering, so no per-tick manual action is needed yet; keep disk headroom above the spill size as backlogs grow. |
| **Artifacts** | Prod evidence (2026-06-26): `DiskFullError: No space left on device` in `sources.last_error` for `murashko_med` + `mediamedics` at ~17:51Z during a `raw_messages` sort (pgsql_tmp); recovered 17:53→18:02Z (murashko 11384→12165, mediamedics 9514→10070). Disk 63% used / 6.7G free; ~24GB reclaimable Docker build cache. Code refs verified this session: `processing_service.py:113-114` + `:125-126`, `raw_message_repo.py:155-184` (`ORDER BY date ASC` `:182`). |
| **Linked** | BUG-067 (deferred **B2** bounded-retry design — directly reduces the per-tick re-read/re-sort volume; B2b cooldown only skips *failed* docs and does not cap the not-yet-attempted load); BUG-068 (same processing call site / serial scheduler; A2 watchdog bounds a stuck tick but does not address the disk spill); BUG-065 / BUG-066 (same 2026-06-25/26 dogfooding watch). |

### BUG-068 — Processing Anthropic call can hang with no effective timeout → stalls the entire serial scheduler indefinitely (no self-recovery)

| Поле | Значение |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | **High** (a single hung processing LLM call → total ingestion/processing pipeline outage with **NO self-recovery**: requires a manual `tg_parser` container restart. Silent — the APScheduler daemon, health checks and `incremental_embedding` keep passing, so monitoring looks green while every scheduled `incremental_pipeline` tick is skipped for hours.) |
| **Status** | ✅ **`resolved`** (fix A1+A2+A3 + review-round-2 hardening — committed [`1ed86ac`](https://github.com/AlexEfimov/TG_parser/commit/1ed86ac) «fix(pipeline): bound LLM hangs, surface degraded ticks, cap token re-burn (BUG-067, BUG-068)»; on `main`, in the `e0f517d` prod deploy). |
| **Component** | `pipeline` (processing LLM client) / `scheduler` — `tg_parser/processing/llm/anthropic_client.py` `generate_with_usage`; processing call site `tg_parser/processing/pipeline.py` `_process_single_message` (`:579-585`) reached via `_process_batch_parallel` (`:1020-1109`); serial single-slot semaphore + job config in `tg_parser/services/scheduler_service.py` (`:105`) and `tg_parser/services/background_scheduler.py` (`:39-46`). |
| **Discovered** | 2026-06-25 — root-caused via prod logs during the BUG-065 / BUG-066 dogfooding watch. |
| **Symptoms** | All sources' `last_attempt_at` frozen; per-channel processed counts flat; APScheduler logs `Execution of job "incremental_pipeline ..." skipped: maximum number of running instances reached (1)` once per interval; the `tg_parser` container stays **healthy** (health_check every 5 min, `incremental_embedding` keeps running) but the pipeline makes **zero** progress. Only a container restart clears it. |
| **Root cause (HIGH confidence — code-traced + prod logs 2026-06-25)** | The processing-stage Anthropic call can hang with **no effective wall-clock bound on the overall call**, and the scheduler is structurally unable to recover from one stuck source. (1) **No effective timeout:** the call site [`pipeline.py:579-585`](../../tg_parser/processing/pipeline.py) `await self.llm_client.generate_with_usage(...)` has **no `asyncio.wait_for` / cancellation guard**. The only bound is the httpx transport timeout `timeout: float = 120.0` → `httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=timeout)` ([`anthropic_client.py:64,74`](../../tg_parser/processing/llm/anthropic_client.py)), and the factory [`factory.py:112-121`](../../tg_parser/processing/llm/factory.py) does **not** override it. That 120s is **per-HTTP-attempt only** and does NOT bound the whole call: the rate-limiter gate `await self.rate_limiter.acquire(in_est, out_est)` ([`anthropic_client.py:150-151`](../../tg_parser/processing/llm/anthropic_client.py)) is **unbounded** (it can block indefinitely waiting for token-bucket capacity, esp. while billing-blocked / rate-limited), and the `max_retries=5` loop with 429 `retry-after` (default 60s, [`anthropic_client.py:27-43`](../../tg_parser/processing/llm/anthropic_client.py)) + 5xx exp-backoff sleeps multiply wall-clock with no aggregate ceiling. (2) **Serial single-slot scheduler can't self-recover:** the scheduler runs sources under `asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)` with `scheduler_max_concurrent_sources` default **1** ([`scheduler_service.py:105`](../../tg_parser/services/scheduler_service.py), [`settings.py:518-522`](../../tg_parser/config/settings.py)), and the `incremental_pipeline` APScheduler job runs under `job_defaults={"coalesce": True, "max_instances": 1, ...}` ([`background_scheduler.py:39-46`](../../tg_parser/services/background_scheduler.py)). So ONE hung processing coroutine holds the single semaphore slot and keeps the job "running" forever → every subsequent tick is skipped (`maximum number of running instances reached (1)`) and the pipeline stalls indefinitely. |
| **Why CI didn't catch** | No test simulates a hanging LLM HTTP call (or a hanging `rate_limiter.acquire`) through the processing call site, and there is no per-call wall-clock timeout / per-tick (or per-source) watchdog to assert against. Existing coverage exercises retry/billing/parse paths that all **return**, never an indefinitely-pending call. **Closure**: add a test that makes the processing LLM call hang and asserts the call (and/or the per-source tick) is bounded/cancelled rather than wedging the scheduler; assert a per-request timeout actually fires. |
| **Proposed fix (do NOT implement)** | Add a hard **per-request wall-clock timeout** to the processing Anthropic client (and the other providers) — bound the whole `generate_with_usage` (including `rate_limiter.acquire` and the retry loop), not just the per-attempt httpx transport timeout — so a hung call fails fast. Complement with a **per-tick / per-source watchdog or cancellation** (e.g. `asyncio.wait_for` around each `_process_source`) so one stuck source can't wedge the whole scheduler, and reassess the `max_instances=1` + `coalesce` behavior so a wedged job is detectable/recoverable without a container restart. |
| **Fix implemented (this session — NOT committed)** | **A1 — aggregate per-call timeout:** `AnthropicClient.generate_with_usage` is now wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for` over the WHOLE call (the unbounded `rate_limiter.acquire` gate + the full 429/5xx retry loop), distinct from the per-HTTP-attempt httpx `timeout`. On elapse it raises `LLMCallTimeoutError` (new, subclasses `TimeoutError`) which propagates as a per-doc failure (no swallow). Budget = `settings.anthropic_call_timeout_s` (new, default **300s**; env `ANTHROPIC_CALL_TIMEOUT_S`), wired via `factory.create_llm_client`. 300s comfortably fits the heaviest single doc (a couple of 120s attempts + a 60s 429 retry-after) while bounding the multi-retry worst case. **A2 — per-source watchdog:** in `scheduler_service._process_source` the `run_full_pipeline` call is wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for(timeout=settings.scheduler_source_timeout_s)` (new, default **1800s**/30 min; env `SCHEDULER_SOURCE_TIMEOUT_S`). On timeout the in-flight coroutine is cancelled, the semaphore slot released, and the tick recorded as a `pipeline_timeout` FAILURE — so a stuck source no longer wedges the scheduler and self-recovers well within the 1h interval. **A3 — concurrency:** `scheduler_max_concurrent_sources` default **1→2** (intra-tick: one slow source can't starve the others; kept at 2 because the Anthropic rate-limiter is shared per API key, so higher gives no real throughput and risks more 429s) and APScheduler `job_defaults.max_instances` default **1→2** (new `settings.scheduler_max_instances`; recovery headroom behind the watchdog so a single long tick no longer skips every subsequent tick). **Tests:** `tests/test_llm_clients.py::test_anthropic_call_timeout_fires_on_hung_rate_limiter` (A1 fires on a hung rate-limiter, fast), `tests/test_scheduler_service.py::test_a2_source_watchdog_times_out_releases_slot_and_records_failure` (A2 cancels + records `pipeline_timeout`). |
| **Review-round-2 hardening (this session — NOT committed)** | **Fix 1 (HIGH):** `LLMCallTimeoutError` (A1) is now special-cased in the `_process_batch_parallel` worker (`llm_only`) and fails the doc in ONE attempt — previously it subclassed `TimeoutError` and fell through the generic retry path, so a single hung doc could burn `max_attempts × anthropic_call_timeout_s` (e.g. 3×300s). Recorded as a `timeout`-category failure (default short cooldown next tick). Test `tests/test_processing_pipeline.py::test_fix1_call_timeout_not_retried_in_worker`. **Fix 4 (MEDIUM):** A3 raised `scheduler_max_instances` 1→2 with no cross-tick per-source guard, so an overlapping/coalesced second tick could run `run_full_pipeline` for the SAME channel and both pass `exists()` for the same new docs → duplicate Telegram/LLM work. Added `_source_processing_lock(source_id)` — a Postgres SESSION-scoped `pg_try_advisory_lock(ns, hashtext(source_id))` on a DEDICATED connection held for the whole tick (mirrors the F5-C resummarize lock but session-scoped, since a tick spans many transactions; the dedicated connection avoids the pool-leak footgun). A second concurrent tick is skipped (`source_already_in_flight_skipped`, counted in `sources_skipped`), not double-processed; degrades to "acquired" if the DB engine is unavailable. Tests `tests/test_scheduler_service.py::test_fix4_second_concurrent_run_for_same_source_is_skipped`, `::test_fix4_source_lock_degrades_to_acquired_when_no_engine`. |
| **Workaround** | Restart the `tg_parser` container to clear the stuck tick (the scheduler cannot self-recover). |
| **Artifacts** | Prod evidence (2026-06-25): the 20:08:23Z `incremental_pipeline` tick reached `murashko_med`, started its processing batch (`processing_batch_start total_messages=33113`) and stalled — last pipeline activity 20:25:13Z, then no `Source murashko_med completed` / no `Incremental pipeline completed`. At 21:08:23Z: `Execution of job "incremental_pipeline ..." skipped: maximum number of running instances reached (1)`. APScheduler daemon stayed alive (health_check every 5 min, `incremental_embedding` ran at 21:08) but the pipeline job was stuck >1h; no source processed after ~20:14; manual restart required. Code refs verified against HEAD `695b5ee`. |
| **Linked** | BUG-067 (billing swallow → billing-failed docs never persisted as processed, so `murashko_med` re-attempts its entire ~21.7k unprocessed backlog every tick, maximizing time in the vulnerable processing loop and amplifying exposure to this hang); BUG-065, BUG-066 (same 2026-06-25 dogfooding watch). |
